title: First and last Azio purchase
text:
[[VIDEOID:77406e2632ec10a2d41e11662cfee6cd]] Edit: Reduced to 1 star from 2 stars. After contacting Azio support I was told they only deal with customers in North America, so I have to ship the item back to Amazon from Australia which would likely cost the same as the keyboard itself, so for people living outside North America I would steer clear.

I really wanted to like this keyboard. It looks pretty good, and the price is very competitive but I don't think the Kaihl switches come close to Cherry MX switches. The keys with stabilizers i.e. shift, return, backspace etc. all feel sticky and/or they feel loose. This might be down to the implementation of the key mounting mechanism, but it doesn't feel good. The only way I can describe is clunky (see video). The other thing that bothered me is the backlighting which in my opinion is not bright enough in comparison to the Logitech G710+ (see photo).

Positives:
Price ($60)
Media
Controls (volume wheel)
Backlighting
Aluminium finish

Negatives:
Some keys feel sticky
Backlighting not bright enough
Very loud
No warranty options outside North America
license: Apache-2.0 (dataset repository); underlying Amazon/McAuley source terms require separate review

**Update 4/17/17** After a painful call to customer service and a one week wait, an engineer came on site. The engineer was obviously passionate about what he does and was a nice guy. He replaced the board sent to him by Sony but no luck. Apparently this is a common fault for this high-end model. Not happening. Their best offer a supposedly new unit and an extra 90 days on the pitiful 1 year warranty that comes as standard. Wow Sony, you have really gone downhill. I have purchased 6 high-end TVS and projectors from you over the past 12 years, this will be the last. We'll see how the replacement goes. Update to follow...

text:

I tested the camera and monitor using a 12v plug with bare wires since I heard some of this manufacturer's items come DOA.

I still have the camera powered from the 12v plug at present.

-Better grip and buttons

-Amazing video upgrade over LX3, audio too

-I finally just had to buy the RX100 and compare. WOW! night and day difference, in just about any mode, shooting indoors, low light. RX100 blows the LX7 out of the water and I cringe even writing that. I am not a pro-sony guy at all.

I am left frustrated, and let down with the LX7...Come on LX9! Until then, I am keeping the Rx100 and learning Sony. I am very very impressed after 400+ indoor low light shots with the Rx100.

title: Fantasic TV at a Great Price!
text:
I began shopping for a 42" LED TV about two weeks ago. I am limited to a 42" only, as that is the largest size TV my entertainment center will allow. I don't need anything larger than that anyway, so I am happy with that configuration. I did research on all of the brands that I had seen in the stores, and found that LG seemed to make one of the best rated TV's in that size. I then went to LG's website to narrow down the model that I wanted. Then I ran into a problem, there are ZERO retail stores near me that sell any 42" LG TV's, let alone the 42LV5400, the model that I really wanted. WalMart.com stocks an older model LG 42", but it did not have the same new features as the 42LV5400.

I was delighted to find that Amazon not only sells this model, but does so for less than the older model offered by WalMart.com. I was even more delighted during the checkout process...I also ordered the optional Magic Motion remote control. There was a hidden promo during checkout that gave me a full credit for the remote, so I got it for free! Throw in the free shipping and zero sales tax, and I was happier than you know what!

Now, my review of the actual TV. When I first turned it on, I liked the picture, but I was slightly disappointed in the quality. It wasn't as true to life as some of the other 120hz LED's that I had seen in stores. After I enabled the wi-fi, the on-screen menu told me that I needed to update the TV's software, which I did. After the TV re-booted, I was amazed at how much the picture quality had improved. It is now better than I had hoped for. Needless to say, I am happy about my purchase from Amazon and thrilled with my new LG TV.

5 stars!

title: Not Properly Designed / Does Not Fit WD My Passport Ultra 2TB Properly
text:
Buyer Beware: Not all Hard EVA Shockproof Carrying Cases are made the same. (OK, maybe that is obvious.) I purchased a "KhanKa Black EVA Shockproof Carrying Case" last year, and was looking for a different color this year for a second drive I have; I wanted to be able to quickly tell the two drives apart. I came across this case, the one from Lacdo, and thought I would give it a try. I am glad I did not order the red one as well, as neither would have been acceptable for my use.

I have attached several pictures, showing the differences between the new Lacdo case on left and the older KhanKa on the right.

The first thing I noticed, and is visible in the pictures I have attached, is how the protective divider is attached. Instead of fully separating the contents of the netted pouch as seen in the first picture, the divider on the Lacdo is sewn into the half of the case which would hold the drive. Thus, the divider has to fold OVER the drive, as shown in the second picture (notice how the KhanKa is designed so that the divider sits neatly over the netted pouch, fully protecting the drive from whatever is in the pouch). The next thing I noticed was that the width of the elastic bands that hold the drive in place are much thinner in the Lacdo than the KhanKa (third picture); to me, the thinner bands will equate to lower quality and life of the bands -- only time will tell. As can be seen in the forth and fifth pictures, the Lacdo case really cannot handle the thickness of the My Passport Ultra 2TB drive, and it really has to be forced closed if the USB cable is placed inside the pouch (as shown). The KhanKa did not feel too tight to close with the cable also in it (also as shown).

The only upside I found with the Lacdo case was that it was better formed in the width and length dimensions for this drive, but not in the depth. The KhanKa was a little too long for the drive, but it does not seem to be a real problem.

Overall, I was not impressed with the Lacdo case, and would not recommend it for any drive as thick as the WD My Passport Ultra 2TB. It may be good for ultra-thin external drives; however, buyer beware.

NOTE: I paid full price for both of these cases, and have no allegiance to either company. I did NOT receive either case in this review for free or reduced cost as others have. I have given my unbiased opinions and have backed them with the pictures attached. I hope this review is helpful for others.

title: Excellent for the home or small office, just be sure to follow the directions for wireless setup.
text:
I'm pretty tech savvy, but have avoided getting a wireless printer until now because of all the nightmare stories I've heard about setting them up, keeping them connected to the network, and getting all the functions to work over the wireless connection. I'm glad I waited for this printer, because it is everything I'd wanted in a wireless all-in-one.

Setup: This goes easily, but not quickly. If you have Windows 7 and can use the wireless setup functions, it makes this setup go a lot faster and easier, but you will still spend a half hour or so getting the software installed. If you don't have Windows 7, expect to spend about an hour on setup, but thankfully the instruction manual is very detailed on this, so as long as you follow the steps, you can't go wrong.

Functionality: Standard all-in-one functions: print, copy, scan, fax. None of these seem any more or less than you'd find in any other similar printer.

Print quality: Very good quality on documents and pictures. The documents are almost (but not quite, of course) on par with my laser printer (Konica Minolta 1650EN) but the picture/photo output is much better.

Wireless: I don't see any issues with the wireless. I tried a few places around the house and anywhere a laptop could find enough of a signal to connect to the router, the printer was able to connect and function. Basically, if the blue light on the front is on, you'll be able to access all the functionality of the printer through the wireless connection.

Size and Weight: The printer is a bit larger than other all-in-ones because it has the paper feed in the back. I don't think this is an issue since you can set the printer anywhere you'd like because of the wireless connection. The weight is fine for any shelf you'd trust a couple books on, so again, not an issue.

Time to print: From standby mode, it takes 15 seconds from the time you hit the "Print" button in Word until the first page of the document is out of the printer. There is nothing here to complain about; that's an excellent time and is much faster than a lot of other printers in the same price range.

Scanning/OCR: I did a screenshot of the scanned page and OCR output of a double-column page from a tool safety manual. Granted it isn't perfect, sometimes it sees an I as a T, sometimes it misses spaces...but recognizing column breaks as something other than just plain whitespace is pretty good, in my opinion. Look at the image at the top of the page and decide for yourself if this is good enough for your home or office.

WOW factor: Since a printer is a printer is a printer...I look for a "that's cool" thing or a "you're kidding me" thing to separate one from the other. One thing I noticed about this printer that convinced me that they'd really put some thought into it is that if you don't open the outfeed door before you start printing...it opens automatically! Okay, that's a great little, "why didn't everyone else think of that" feature that makes me feel very confident that they've put at least as much thought into all the other aspects of the printer.

Summary: I'm very happy with the printer. It seems to be very well made, the print is clear, the time to first page out isn't any longer than other inkjets and shorter than most. Perhaps the biggest thing that impressed me was the detail of the installation manual; it doesn't sound like it was translated from Russian or some other language and it has step-by-step, detailed instructions that will get the printer set up and running with a minimum of frustration.

Of course, I'll update as needed, but I feel this is a good printer that you should strongly consider for the home or even small office.

If you want a fun LED keyboard with mechanical switches for a reasonable price this is the one for you.

title: nice idea, but not there yet
text: I tried the IO2 for three weeks at my work, using it in different note taking situations: internal meetings, client meetings, taking notes on articles, "thinking out loud" on new product designs on my own, and my other day-to-day activities. I still like the idea of the IO2 but the pen didn't work for me in these real-world situations. The pen is a bit fat for everyday writing, uncomfortable in your hand and therefore tiring. The handwriting recognition isn't good enough, even after training, for the variation in my writing in different situations (hurried at times and not at others, sequential at times and jumping around the page at others...). It struggles if you have any note-taking habits such as using graphics such as arrows to set off your notes, or shorthand such as initials for people's names or abbreviations for words. The pen doesn't allow you to go back on a page and cross out a word or clarify a letter or insert a word -- the text will show up on the digital page but it seems to confuse the heck out of the handwriting recognition. The software also doesn't seem to keep learning with you -- you train it and that is all it ever knows. Another small but irritating problem was that you can't use one page of paper for more than one digital "page" -- that is, if you write two sentences on a page and then want to use the rest of the page for another topic or meeting, you can't tell the pen to treat these as separate pages on the computer. All in all, a good idea, with great promise for the eventual IO4 or IO5, but not ready for real-world use if the handwriting recognition is critical to you.

title: Best value for under $50 (when it's on sale)
text:
Title says all.

The other reviews will tell you most of what you really need to know, so I'll just add a few caveats, things the manual does not state:

(1) Advertised battery life is 15 hours, as long as you don't use lights or extra bass. In my practical day to day experience, in the way I use it, for occasions when I really want some volume, (meaning it's not my normal day to day BT speaker), I get 10 hours.

(2) Speaking of the extra bass, they really shouldn't have called it "extra" bass, and merely called it "bass." It's because, even if you set your source material's EQ curve or present to be bassy, there won't really be any out of this speaker with the "extra" bass button off. You'll need to have it on in order to have any bass.

(3) The sounds that sound like telephone busy signals, two each spaced out from time to time, are the low battery indicator, and in my estimation, they seem to start when battery life is at 1%. That is one of my pet peeves about many BT speakers, that they start whatever their battery life is low warning is, way too soon, circa 15% battery life left. And sometimes, said warning is intrusive, and interferes with whatever you're listening to. This device starts the warning at the correct interval, IMHO, at 1% left, and does not much interfere with what you're listening to.

(4) It's pretty big, with decent materials, especially along the right and left facing sides. It is actually heavier than it looks.

(5) I generally find the lighting schemes to be cheesy, but every once in awhile, with the right song, they can be entertaining.

(6) Overall sound quality is not the best, even among BT speakers I own, and I don't own any expensive ones. But that's to be expected for the price point. It does get plenty loud.

title: Wirh correct accesories, perfect for video!
text:
Update Jan. 2018:
I took off one star because:
I guess I was so happy to finally have a perfectly good tripod that fit my criteria (which is in the initial review below) that I overlooked the fact that the tripod kept on sliding on flat surfaces when panning during video. Looking at my cheap Neewer tripods, which work very well, I realized that their feet are much better designed and that's why it never slipped. I ordered the "Leophoto sc-50" feet that is sold here on Amazon and now this tripod doesn't slide.

Update:
I also ordered the Manfrotto 128RC tripod head which pans and glides beautifully and now it doesn't tip. When I used a tripod head that was more stiff, the tripod tipped over when panning because of its lightweight. With the Manfrotto tripod head and Leophoto feet, it's absolutely fantastic for shooting video.

Initial review
Finally!!! I tried 4 different tripods and the Benro TAD27A is the one! I have a cheap Neewer tripod with a fluid head that is pretty nice. The head pans and tilts smoothly, the legs are stable and open and close quickly. The problem was that I bought a slider and the Neewer tripod's head could not be detached and the slider didn't work well on the fluid head. And so I ordered and tried 4 different tripods until I hit the jackpot with this one.

Before I ordered I knew I don't want a twist lock as it's very frustrating to open and close, it takes three times as long as a clip lock. I wanted a three section leg, not four section. And it had to be sturdy, of course.

Every tripod I ordered, besides for this one, had something wrong with it. One tripod tipped easily, one was sturdy but very stiff, I had to fight to open and close locks and push hard to to get legs into an open and closed position. And on one tripod the center pole wasn't centered, when I tightend it it leaned a few mm to one side.

So I ordered this one hoping very much it will be the right one. And it is exactly what I'm looking for. Not too heavy, but still nice and sturdy, clips and legs open and close easily, and a big bonus is the center pole can be moved quickly and smoothly with one turn of the knob.

I feel that's it's well made and think (and hope!) it will last a long time.

It's great for video. I've used it many times and it works very well provided the feet are replaced so it doesn't slip and a very smooth fluid head is used so it doesnt tip when panning. As mentioned above, The combination of the feet, lightweight and smooth tripod head, together with this Benro tripod, creates an excellent, lightweight tripod.

title: 1st monitor lasted 20 min but the replacement is fantastic.
text: I was excited to get this monitor and had very high expectations.  I set it up and it looked great as I started playing a game.  It lasted 20 minutes until there was a bright flash of light that appeared toward the middle of the screen and it wouldn't go away no matter what I tried.  I researched the issue and turns out it is a common QC problem with Samsung panels and requires a panel replacement in most cases.  I decided not to test my luck again so I packed it up and shipped it back for a refund. I was not going to try for a replacement but decided to give it one more chance since it was $800 during the week of Black Friday.  My 2nd monitor arrived flawless.  It took some getting used to the curve but I don't even notice it during gaming.  It is very noticeable though when browsing the web or doing anything other than gaming or watching movies.  Isn't too bad though.  The image quality with the bright HDR, deep blacks and stunning colors is where this monitor really shines.  A little bit of blooming is visible at times but it doesn't bother me.  I have had OLED TVs since 2018 and am very happy with the HDR and the black levels on this monitor.  I have it paired with an i9-13900k and RTX 4090 FE PC and they're a gaming match made in heaven.  It doesn't have official G-Sync support but you won't even know.  PC games run buttery smooth with zero screen tearing.  Even the PS5 looks exceptional on it and I'm replaying games I haven't touched in a while.  I am glad I decided to try this monitor again because it is fantastic. I use it mainly for playing AAA titles.  I personally wouldn't use it for competitive fps games as the curve may be a hinderance for those.  For competitive games I use a 1080p Acer Nitro XV252Q 390 Hz monitor.  Neo G7 checks off all of the boxes for anyone not wanting to go the OLED route and risking a burn in. The image quality of this display is so close to OLED that I don't feel like I compromised on anything and the colors look better than on my LG C1 OLED.  139 ppi make everything, inluding the text nice and crisp.  If you can live with the curve and the hefty price tag I highly recommend that you give the Neo G7 a try for PC or next gen console gaming.  I see myself enjoying this monitor for a long time without buyer's remorse no matter what new screens come out next year.

At beginning I thought it was the problem with my SD card. And I bought a new one and replaced it. Then, it happened again. I insert the SD card to my PC. Windows was able to recognize the disk, but wasn't able to format it either. It seems that the camera's format option can easily mess up the disk format.

Update on 09/26/2019. Reached to the seller. The seller only offered me a replacement. The shipment was fast. However, the new camera comes with a different problem -- it often reboots several times after power on. More specifically, I noticed the following sequence:
1. Turn on the power
2. The emergency button starts blinking, indicating the camera is recording. But the LED remains dark (the LED auto turn off is 3min. So it should turn on)
3. After about 10 seconds, the emergency button stops blinking. The whole camera is stopped
4. After a few seconds, the camera restarts again, and we can see the emergency button starts blinking again. But the LED still remains dark.
5. After another 10 seconds, the camera stops again.
6. Then the camera restarts, the LED is turned on this time. Everything seems to be working this time.
I also confirmed that two small recording files were generated during the reboot. Each is about 10 seconds, which is aligned with what I saw.

I also recorded a video about the reboot problem. Will follow up with the seller and see what they are going to do about it.

title: Does not fit Ford 2019 F series without major modifications
text:

In order to use, I had to grind out the INSIDE of these adapters in order to get the speakers to fit INSIDE the adapters. Additionally since I was fitting the speakers on the inside of the adapter one of the pre drilled screw holes did not want to align up with the speaker holes, I had to drill a new hole beside the original in the adapter. I also had to grind down some of the inside of the door trim plastic around the speaker grille and even then it is a tight fit.

Screw holes on the door side also did not line up as this adapter only has two holes on one side and a couple of plastic pins on the other side which does not align with anything. So I had to cut the pins off and drill new holes in the proper spots in the adapters..

You will also need to buy bolts (with nuts), most speaker manufacturers no longer supply screws or bolts and this adapter does not supply any either. 4-40 machine screw at least 3/4" long should work.

If someone from Metra is reading, they need to take note of this depth issue and create a new adapter with reduced depth and proper door mount screw holes.

title: WARNING: It's NOT 'UL Listed'! Use may void your insurance.
text:
I'll start out with what I liked: The whole thing feels "solid". The 4 USB chargers are fast. The plastic is especially hard, and the mounting tabs look like they could survive a moderate drop onto concrete. There are no exterior signs of quality being compromised, but I did not open it up.

I have to give this two stars because it has NOT been UL/ETL tested. I would argue (and so would your insurance company) that if there is any fire, it's YOUR fault... insurance won't cover damages from using non-UL devices.

I feel a bit deceived here. Brick-and-mortar stores will not TOUCH non-UL equipment because of liability, so why shouldn't Amazon be the same way? (If you're listening, Amazon, at least put a warning - a graphical one so we don't have to read all the "fine print"). I just assumed Amazon was the same. You'll see this is a "Amazon Verified Purchase", $26... I paid to return it.

The manufacturer notes in response UL-concerned reviews that they have a "quality" product. This is response is deceptive or evasive, as it's meant to be word salad without actually conceding to the UL concerns.

Let's be clear: UL-listed does not "necessarily" indicate quality. UL-does not mean it will "never" break, or that you can't be shipped non-working part. What UL-Listed DOES mean is IF the device fails, it will not risk your property, your life (or the lives of others, such as Fire and Police). UL also means it has been tested to confirm how it behaves if something you plug into it, has failed. You can expect a UL-listed device to fail gracefully without short circuiting and without rapidly combusting. With untested, you do not know what it will do when it fails.

If you bought one and don't want to return it, I suggest using it only for temporary installations, such as a portable/rolling cart - used in a way that you can supervise.

title: SO much better than other camera straps....
text:
I was using the Peak Design Slide Lite Camera Strap. It's a great strap but there's SO much strap on each end it gets in the way when I use my camera and I'm just waiting for the connector to give out since they do wear out. I don't want to take a chance that my camera and lens will hit the ground when I least expect it.

I have been passing over using the Black Rapid straps for so long and when the bulk of the Peak Design strap got to be too much I finally bought one. I didn't want the strap with the under arm strap because I don't like to feel confined and I can't see how this would work with bulky clothes on so I bought the "original" RS-4. It's also a VERY minimalistic strap.

I've been told by many photographers that the tether included with the strap is pretty much useless. I ordered this "Foto&Tech Safety Camera Strap Tether Leash Fits Any Sling Up to 1.5 Inch Wide with Durable Stainless Steel Carabiner and High Strength Cord " and I'm very happy with it.

The strap itself is very very light. It almost feels like it's too light to hold any weight. No so...The strap is wide enough that it will fit on any shoulder. Without the under arm strap though it does shift around a bit. My solution: I put several lines of a hot glue gun. (see picture) Problem Solved! Now it doesn't move around.

You do need to pay attention to the instructions when installing the strap. When you screw on the connector you screw it on hand tight and when you add the locking carabiner you hold onto it and make another small twist which helps the rubber washer expand and stay tight.

The strap has a very convenient zippered pouch on it so you can store a lens cloth or sd cards. It also fit either a LEFT or RIGHT shoulder. A few of the black rapid are left or right specific.

The strap has spring loaded bumpers that you can put on each end of the carabiner so the camera doesn't move around when you walk. It's totally adjustable so you can wear it above your hip or at your hip. Depends what is the most comfortable for you.

It's probably one of the most comfortable straps you can buy in my opinion. The only negative I can find with the strap is the carabiner knocks into the camera when you're handling it and some people have had the coating on the camera come off where it touches the camera. I just make sure when I store it to put something under the carabiner so it doesn't knock around.

Adding the additional tether I feel this strap is very secure and very comfortable. Do Not buy the knock off brand unless you're 100% sure it's safe. There are many mixed reviews on the knock off on Amazon. I'm looking forward to many many photo shoots with it.

title: Problematic, but a few tips
text:
Just like any dog, you have to understand it's quirks. If using for functions other than the barking, you might appreciate it more. As others have described, the 3rd level of 'frenzy' barking is not at all realistic, and it is very difficult/impossible to keep the unit functioning at the one or two-bark level before it jets off into uncontrollable noise. Actually, the barking mode does not appear to be intended for detection of an object that continues to stand in the same place. It is intended for a person passing by. If you pass by it, it can bark once; if you delay, then it will get more agitated with multiple barks, and if you stay very long, it *will* make an incessant annoying noise that does not sound like a dog. If you want to use this like a dog, you have to put it somewhere that people will pass by on their way to your door. And then you will not have the effect of a dog barking at an intruder at your door; but at least there will be a bark along the way. The unit says there will be different sensitivity in different weather, perhaps rain, etc. I think I have experienced that quirk also. If you want it to work right under different conditions, then the battle for adjusting sensitivity begins anew. Sorry about that.

The unit does not see through walls either. I had to find a window with no screen to put it behind.

And the only way that I could actually set it up was to buy a remote on/off switch, and power the unit off while I was adjusting it. Setup is tricky because it will bark 5 seconds after you turn it on, and you think you have just triggered it with your presence. You have to ignore that bark. And while you are near it making adjustments, it goes into frenzy mode because you have been detected for too long. Turn it off to adjust it, then walk past it after it has been powered on for more than at least 5 seconds. If you stand within it's range past the two-bark stage, it will sound like hell. With an on/off remote switch you can at least shut it up.

---

I found an alternative that so far is meeting my needs. It is the [[ASIN:B001JT13NE Scytek MP Siren True Sound MP3 Player Siren]]. I now notice also a [[ASIN:B001CCZP7I Galaxy SRMP3 True Sound MP3 Player Siren]]. The fake roar of the [[ASIN:B0006FV0E4 Electronic Secure Dog Barking Dog Alarm]] is just a nuisance. I suggest you see my review on the Scytek unit; it is difficult to set up. Basically, in that setup I am using an IR Motion Controller to send signals to an X10 transceiver which sends signals to an appliance module connected to any electrical outlet in the house. It's complicated. So now I have a Scytke Siren that barks like a dog from a custom MP3 file, and that is happening in one part of the house, and I have a doorbell chime activated by the same signal in another part of the house. I plan on putting in additional Motion Control sensors around the house. And with multiple alarms, I could have different dog sounds barking all around the house. In case you're wondering, I'm also the guy that put an electric fence shocker on my windows. Now that's awesome! I also have floodlights, sirens, and a camera if someone actually enters. How cool is that?

title: Edited review of new security driveway alert purchased to replace my original.
text:
Purchased the same item several years ago and was very happy with it. Bought a new one a couple months ago and it worked for one month and then quit. This is an updated review of the new purchase. Needless to say, I am NOT HAPPY with the new driveway alert system from Bunker Hill.

Below a review of product purchased in 2014.
Very pleased with the product. My receiver is placed on a window sill and the loud alarm can be heard both by myself inside, and by anyone outside entering the property. Hopefully hearing the alarm will discourage intruders. My units are protected from rain, Maybe that will help them operate for a longer time.

Edit: July 2015 and the product still works perfectly. I brought the outside unit inside in December when the temperature dropped below zero. I replaced the battery and put the unit back outside in March.

Edit: Product purchased summer 2014. May 2017 and the product is still working. Left the unit in the unheated garage with the batteries in during the 2016-2017 midwest winter and it never quit even on subzero nites (which may be a tribute to the batteries as much as the unit). Am purchasing another of these units. I'm really satisfied with placing the receiver in my window (between screen and glass) where it can be heard outside as well as inside. That just may be enough to alert a prowler to an alarm system and help him decide to prowl elsewhere.

Edit: Sept. 2018 after four years system seems to be failing. Certainly got my money's worth from this unit. Will purchase another to replace.

title: Good hardware paired with sloppy software
text:
This product has two parts, the actual device and the software for your phone. The problem is while the device itself is solid, the app does not perform well.

The actual iHere device is well made, feels pleasant to use and has a reasonably loud speaker in it so finding it in most circumstances is quite easy. It does not use a standard micro usb charging cable which is a ding against it, and the shape and thickness do make it rather bulky on any keychain and definitely won't fit in a mans wallet well.

The battery life has been quite good, on the first charge it has gone over a week and still at 95% battery. I suspect after a few charge cycles this will decrease but initially it's quite impressive.

The range is acceptable and usually ends up going out of range around 30-50 ft away from your phone.

The device itself gets 5 stars.

The problem is the app - without which the device is useless.

Nonda seems pretty light on testing their updates, at least for older phones (4S) and so several times now I have had an update render my app useless. Their support is quick to answer requests and usually the response is in very clear English. A few times I have gotten a response from someone with poor English but the response is still understandable.

Usually they fix the issue with their app within a week or two, which is a reasonable turnaround time but due to the number of issues I have spent more time with it not working than it has been working. This is a big ding for a device that you rely on for when you need it.

When it is working some of the app functions are very reliable - ringing the iHere works well, the car park feature seems pretty accurate and the camera shutter works but you cannot use it with the iphone camera app, but rather the picture mode build into their iHere app. The voice recorder works similarly.

Less reliable is the function to call the phone from the iHere which only works sometimes. I think this is largely due to the phone closing the app in the background which means it's not looking for or listening for the iHere signal.

Completely unreliable is the "Last known location" of the iHere as it seems to mark the last location that you had the app open and connected to the iHere. This obviously isn't very useful and possibly also due to memory management on the phone.

The software lacks a safe zone for the anti lost feature which is kind of annoying as just walking around your house with the keys in another room can trigger the alarm, sometimes just random connectivity issues trigger the alarm also. This can happen in the middle of the night while sleeping so safe zones would really be a good feature as it's annoying to turn the feature on and off regularly.

The app looks good and runs smoothly for the most part and is fairly intuitive to use.

Overall this is a 5 star device hampered by some lacking software. I don't know if other keyfinder devices have similar issues, so can't compare, but if you get it working, then set your app not to auto update and keep it charged I think it will at least reliably serve it's base function of finding your keys.

Consider the other functions bonuses that work sometimes or most times but are not always reliable.

title: STOP HESITATING AND DO IT
text:
If you are going between this attic mount antenna and one of the "table top" type antennas- GET THIS ONE. You will be happier in the long run, despite the inconvenience of the attic installation.

We dropped cable over a year ago, and went with a 50 mile range table top style antenna with an amplifier. It worked ok- but not nearly as well as I hoped given that all the station antenna's are within a 30 mile or so radius to us. We put up with spotty stations that at any given time would decide not to receive a signal due to weather, tree foliage or lack of, PMS, minor positional changes of the dog, neighbors in their yards, etc.

So back to the drawing board I went, and decided to get this one. The husband installed it (it took him basically a full day, but he's got ADD, so everything takes him 3 times as long as the person sans ADD) and I was AMAZED that we had ALL THE CHANNELS. We basically watch PBS and occasionally a Boston news channel, but now we had 3 PBS stations to pick from and all the Boston channels and then some.

All of the channels we picked up that first day still come in despite weather, foliage, dog positions, neighbors mowing their lawn, etc. And the bonus is that the antenna is no where in sight as it's neatly tucked away in the attic as opposed to draped across my living room in hopes of a signal.

title: Great daylight images...HORRIBLE night images
text:
I received this Hikvision DS-2CD2142FWD-I 2.8mm network camera very quickly, and I was eager to install it to replace an old wireless IP camera that had degraded night vision.

I have 3 other Hikvision camera, so this was a breeze to install and setup. The hardest part of the problem was running the Cat5e cable to the corner soffit that didn't have an existing cable run.

I finished the install well before dark and was very pleased with the daylight video it provided. My joy turned to sorrow, however, once darkness settled in.

This camera suffers from HORRIBLE IR bleeding, creating an extremely washed out/foggy image. A quick search resulted in a technical bulletin from Hikvision explaining the problem. Once I went through the checklist it became obvious that the rubber gasket that surrounds the lens, and shields the lens from IR light reflecting off the inside of the glass dome, is NOT pressing against the glass, as the bulletin states it should.

I'm really disappointed in this model and am returning it. Of my other three Hikvision cameras, two are bullet cams, and one is a dome camera. I've included photos of that camera, nestled on my porch at night, along with this new DS-2CD2142FWD taken with the dome on, and another with the dome off. The resulting effect is crystal clear, even if the night time video is not!

I'm returning this ASAP and will rethink a replacement model.

title: UPDATED These are AMAZING with one detrimental issue..white noise
text:
What follows is my original 3star review from Nov 2022. Update will be indicated toward the end.

Pros:
-extremely comfortable
-stays in small ears
-very good sound quality
-controls are easy and useful
-very pleasant design, attractive, great materials
-no app necessary
-stays on ears very well
-great mic quality

cons:
-constant low white noise
-volume doesn't go low enough
-not comfortable with glasses
-case doesn't have battery, but you can buy one that does separately

I have teeny tiny ear holes that have never once been able to support earbuds. They just fall out.
I've been enjoying Samsung Live Buds since they came out because their stemless design actually stayed in both of my ears and only hurt on one side. When they died, I decided to try a few new options that might not hurt either ear.

I love these headphones. I can hear what's going on around me but the sound quality is as good as earbuds. They're so comfortable that I forget they're on..this coming from someone who finds ALL headphones and buds painful.

They're almost perfect. Except:

Constant white noise. CONSTANT. I've messaged the seller and got a copy-paste response that didn't seem to have the issue addressed in it. The white noise is completely lost if the volume is above a 2 or a 3 but that leads into my next issue.. the lowest volume setting on these is about 1/3 louder than I like to listen in a quiet room. If i'm listening on the lowest volume, which is what I choose to listen at, there's always white noise. If nothing is playing, it'll just hear white noise. I tend to leave my headphones on all day for calls and this is a problem
=( For me, they're just too loud at times.

I wondered if the issues with the volume and the white noise were because my unit was faulty so I exchanged for a new pair and the issue is present in the replacement unit.

There's a possibility that it's a software issue with my phone or something, so I'm not going to pretend to know if this is entirely the fault of the headphones. If I figure out how to fix this issue I'll update this review with any info that can help.

Update January 2023:

Further pros:
-The batteries of these really do go FOREVER. I'm very pleased with the battery life. I don't know what the actual playime is but I've had them in my ears playing off-and-on for 12hrs+ and didn't run out of battery.
-They still look quite new after a couple of month of daily use

Further cons:
-I don't know how I missed this before, but they fall off completely when I tip my head all the way back. Just plop right off. Not good for yoga or painting the ceiling. This issue could be because of my personal ear anatomy, but it's worth mentioning.

Further exeriences: (neither pro nor con)
-They don't give detailed battery info. They only display battery life in 10% increments. I don't care about this but I've given so much detail in this review I might as well include it.

After my initial review, Oladance messaged me using the Amazon messaging system. They noticed that I'd mentioned getting a copy-paste response in original review and they wanted to improve my experience with their company. I thought that was quite friendly.

In the new response, they addressed my initial question about the white noise. They said that they're aware of the white noise and it's not a software issue on my end. They explained that during their product testing phase the white noise was all but unnoticed by their testers and to remove it completely would compromise the quailty. I believe this explaination because this is a unique product.

Personally, I don't think I have superb hearing that would pick up the white noise better than anyone else but I do find myself hypersensitive to sensory stimulation in some scenarios. They also confimed my suspicion that the white noise probably isn't bothersome for almost everyone.

They also address a few other things in my "cons" list from my original review. They were attentive and let me know that they're releasing something new this year and to stay tuned. Cool!

Here's why I dropped the star:
They offered me a refund.
That was very nice, right? I didn't think for a second that I was entitled to a refund, I didn't ask for a refund or elude to wanting one. But you're darn tootin I was happy to accept a refund so I could put that money to purchasing their new 2023 lauch. As you can tell by the rest of my review, I'm actually a huge fan of these headphones. I used the word "love" in my original review and I was geniunely excited by how great they really are.

There were a few pleasant back-and-forths with customer service and I repeatedly mentioned the refund they were extending to me and they repeatedly ignored me. When I asked directly about what they offered me, they told me that they couldn't for *reasons* beyond their control.

Just felt icky..why would they extend a generosity then ignore it and eventually withdrawl it? Made me feel like they were dangling a carrot but for what, I don't know.

TL:DR

Never had headphones that sounded so good and worked so well for me.

minus 1star for unrelenting white noise
minus 1star for being too loud
minus 1 more star for icky customer service experience

And they all lived happily ever after.

title: Perfect in every way
text:
I've had an Amazon Origami case for my Voyage ever since I first got this device, and I've hated it from Day One for the way the cover flops around, its design that for me serves no purpose, and for its fold-down-from-the-top style. I got my Voyage from Best Buy on the day of its introduction, though, and it was the only case available.

My Paperwhite, OTOH, has worn *its* leather Amazon case from the start as well, and I *love* that case. It operates as a case should, with the fold on the left and, after 3 years it still feels and looks good. None of the "almost" leather, it is *real* leather and it just makes me feel good whenever I pick it up. The Voyage case, though? Not so much. In fact, it pisses me off. Every single time.

Not too long ago, I finally got fed up enough to go shopping to replace that floppy, ersatz case that pisses me off every time I see it and this is the case I found and I am so glad that I did. For half the price I paid for either of the Amazon cases, this brown leather case is almost *identical* to my Paperwhite's brown leather case.

So, thanks to this case, I no longer feel pissed off at the morons at Amazon who created that first case, and I feel good whenever I see it or pick it up. Function-wise, it fits the Voyage like a glove; there was no prying or pushing required when I put it in. In fact, it fits better than the Amazon cases. It is light in weight, thin in profile, accommodates the power button on the back, and is generally perfect in every way.

If YOU want a case that won't piss you off and is generally perfect in every way, THIS is the one to get. Do note, however, that there are 2 styles of cases grouped together on the sales page -- leather and fake leather -- so make sure you're getting what you think you're getting. The fake leather cases have a metal bar on the front (like the *real* leather Paperwhite Amazon cases have) and the title, as you mouse over the item, identifies its color and type.

title: One-Of-A-Kind, But Beware Of Differences
text:
Here's what's rotten--there are about a zillion different "y510p" models of the IdeaPad. So comparison shopping is extraordinarily difficult. This is compounded by the fact that, despite what some commenters are saying, this exact model number is *not* available on the Lenovo site. Even more hilarious is that contacting Lenovo support to ask details on the differences is a moot point--they'll tell you that, despite it being their product, if it's not listed on their website, they can't tell you about it.

So for more details on this exact model number (59406648), check out the listing on Tiger Direct. As I said, there are many, many different IdeaPad models, but that Tiger Direct listing has some more specifics (for example, on the processor).

Another thing to be wary of is all of the confusing information that exists about the Ultrabay. In terms of the Ultrabay, this exact model from Amazon comes with the second graphics card. So yes, it's a dual-graphics card setup straight out of the box--you do not need to upgrade this. I have to add that this might still be confusing when you first fire up this machine, because they give you all of the DVD software, including the burning suites.

But again--this does NOT come with a DVD or BluRay drive. You do get tons of bloatware though! A quick internet search will help you delete the garbage you don't need.

Performance-wise, this is amazing. It runs a little hot, but modern games on high settings play well, and don't seem to chug. The speakers (the JBL ones everyone's so hyped about) are nice and loud, but they tend to favor the mid-range.

That's the bulk of it. Everything else is pretty clear-cut, but I wanted to help anyone else who was a little confused about the lack of and/or conflicting information out there. Especially when it comes to other models--you *cannot* get this model many places, including Lenovo's own site, and it really is remarkable for the money! Thanks!

title: Bad quality, technical support, overall experience
text:
Problem after problem after problem. If I could go back in time, I would never have purchased this system. I got the 8 bullet version and installed all around the exterior of my house through my attic. The setup and running of wires is a difficult and pricey process if you have someone do it for you so even if you are unhappy with the system, you will not likely be returning it. Quality for 720p left something to be desired. Viewing angle for cameras is small. Wall/side mounted cameras do not flip so your view is sideways. Technical support that has no idea what they are doing and put you on hold while they consult a booklet and read you verbatim and have no real idea whats going on (usually read you something unrelated).

Problem #1 - Bad receiver out of the gate. Kept overheating or something and rebooted. Tried to deal with it for a week but was rebooting too often. They diagnosed as HDD error and had me send it back. You are forced to send your unit back before they send a replacement UPS ground so that was about 2 weeks.

Problem #2 - I received a unit back with a HDD error. I e-mailed support again and after about week was told I should have removed my HDD before sending it back to them. I told them the replacement was due to HDD and they offered to reimburse me a HDD through Amazon. I installed it myself because I know how to do that but they offered no support.

Problem #3 - After about a week of consistent monitoring, one of my cameras went on the fritz and eventually the picture went black. Two days later it came back on for no reason.

I have reservations about the quality / longevity of this system, to say the least... After about a month I was able to use this system to do what it was supposed to do from day 1. If running the cords (I had custom electric put in as well) did not cost me almost the price of the system I would have returned for sure. If you have a problem with your system, I would go through AMAZON to do the replacement and you'll get a new system. I would not repurchase Amcrest or advise anyone to buy this system.

Fast Forward to April 2020. I upgraded my wifi router which meant that I had to reconnect all my devices. All my echo devices handled the router change like champs. . . That is except this one. I may not be an expert, but I am no technical slouch. So, I contact Amazon technical support and spent two hours on a chat with them going through all the steps to reconnect it. First they said there was an issue with my Alexa app. So, uninstalled and reinstalled it. No dice. They had me do, I don't know how many resets of the glow which did nothing. We removed it from my devices. . . At one point, it was constantly blinking green and blue, but the tech had no idea what that meant.

After about two hours of going through all this, it was finally determined that there is a problem with the device. Fine. . . send me a replacement. NO CAN DO. The warranty already expired. SERIOUSLY? Yep. . .While all other Echo devices have a one year warranty, for some reason this only has a 90 day warranty. It's almost as if they knew that it was a piece of junk. I even pulled the, "I've been loyal to Amazon since 1998 and have been loyal to Amazon devices" card. Yeah, I know, not the classiest move. But, apparently there is nothing that they can do. Honestly, it is truly disappointing. Not so much because I'm out the money, but because Amazon won't stand behind their product. . . Oh well. Live and learn. But I would definitely not recommend this product.

title: I expected more from K40
text:
For a company widely known in the CB antenna market, with a proclaimed product made in the U.S.A., I expected higher quality. This antenna so far has been a let down, and I haven't even completed installing it. What should have taken ten minutes at most, took over 30 minutes before I had to quit because I had to get back to my day job duties.

First issue, the whip antenna was hidden in the seam of the plastic container. I was about to stop there and call them but I happen to pick up the container and the whip fell out. It should have been taped in plain sight or had a flag of some kind attached to it in order to draw attention to it.

Next, the set screw had been placed in the mount backwards. This means that the hex side of the screw was on the interior and the hex key could not be used to back it out. Careful work and a lot of tapping on the base was needed to get it to back out far enough that I could unscrew it by hand and turn it around.

Once the set screw issue was resolved, it was time to insert the whip into the base. However, as there is no tip on the whip, I did not know which end to insert. I read the directions, but there was no mention of which end should be inserted and which end was the "Radius 180 Tip". I found a scribe mark on the antenna and I have assumed that to be the top of the whip. I sure hope so, since the other end of the whip has been trimmed for tuning.

Speaking of tuning, the final issue before I had to stop was the tuning of the antenna itself. The VSWR was lowest below CB channel #1. All legal CB radios cannot transmit there. This is fine, it allows the antenna to be finely adjusted by shortening the whip. However, I have no idea what the whip is made of, by my cutter, which has been used to cut whips before, could not cut through this material. Nearly broke my cutter. A hacksaw was needed to cut the whip. I will probably have to replace the blade after I get it tuned correctly.

I won't speak to performance as performance is relative to the installation and the radio. But I am not impressed with K40 at this point. Probably won't buy another one.

title: This laptop sounds too good to be true, but it truly isn't.. (edit 1/26/2017)
text:
Post-Purchase Impressions:

I bought this laptop about half a year ago now, and for the most part, I'm happy to report that the "new," impression I got over this laptop did not falter much over time. It still runs impressively fast, and I have not had many issues with it. However, I'd like to add a few shortcomings I've noticed as time went on.

- The "bleeding" effect of the backlight mentioned in some reviews has become more apparent to me, especially in dimly lit settings. While I dont find this particularly perturbing, I felt it was worth mentioning for those who would be bothered by it.
- The laptop, while easy to disassemble, and add additional hardware to the interior, has become a bit.. easy to come apart. On the left side of the case of the laptop, near the folding latch that connects to the screen, the plastic interlocking pieces has seem to come apart in a non repairable manner. This is particularly a problem if you accidentally spill something nearby or face humid conditions in your workspace. Needless to say, the quality of the plastic encasement itself isn't built to last. Or perhaps, it was a special case for me, but I digress; this is something you should consider before buying this laptop.
- The charger cord becomes easily frayed near the connection to the charging port on the laptop. It hasn't ceased functioning, but it has brought about concerns that it may need to be replaced by a sturdier charging cable in the future.
- The backlit keyboard is a godsend, and the chiclet-style keys feel very nice on your fingers, even during long gaming sessions. However, I've come to notice that the spacebar easily wears out, as mentioned in other reviews, which often leaves me going back to add a space into what I type. Pressing the space bar in the middle seems to circumvent this issue, but it is a minor annoyance all the same, yet again, referring to the cheaper build quality.

I also should add, that I am very aware and careful of caring for my technology, and do everything in my power to ensure its longevity. That being said, I noticed these issues popping up in the first few months, regardless of the careful measures I've taken. For a (at the time) 650 dollar laptop, it is still definitely worth the price at even 750, in my opinion, but I want to spread this information to help those on the fence and seeking feedback on this product. I still highly recommend it for its hardware specs and its overall performance, design, and appearance. The only lacking factor appears to be the material quality/durability.

title: You could have been the chosen one...
text:
Project S - Midi (mid size)

This case does what you ask - the size of a receiver and fits right into your tv stand as you'd want. It fits comfortably and does what it needs to, but with major problems from my experience with it.

Pros:
1. Excellent HTPC box for gaming rigs
2. Fantastic design ideas, and looks
3. Enjoyable building as you can remove the entire rig from the case and build it out simply and comfortably.

Cons:
1.Thin walls on the inner chassis
2.While it supports a 240mm AIO, the Kraken X52 COMPLETELY blocks the hole to run the CPU EPS connector. With some custom sleeved soft cables, perhaps you could squish it through, but I was forced to run my cables across the motherboard like a peasant.
3. Alignment of the screw holes for the PSU did NOT line up - only 3 screws fit
4. HDMI cable is blocked by a random L shaped area on the back, resulting in me having to squeeze it in before securing the inner chassis to the external. Makes no sense
5. PSU is completely exposed and offers no option for cable management except a tiny cutout that cannot accept thicker sleeve cables.
6. Designed for numerous drives...without options. Instead of allowing you to mount a 240mm radiator in the front instead of drives like most cases with removable drive cages, it just becomes wasted space you end up just filling with excess cabling
7. PSU is not pushed up against the bottom of the case, resulting in no gap between the PSU and motherboard, which prevents front panel/USB connectors from being easily routed to their desired location through extra holes like most quality cases
8. No dust filter on front intake for some reason, but there are filters on every other side, even the left which has no fan options, but can support a 3.5in drive only (again, for no reason should this not be interchangeable)
9. Due to all of the above issues, thermal capabilities are limited. Simply removing the top glass reduces thermals by 10c. An option with a vented top and/or fan mounts in the front would significantly improve the case. There's a reason smaller cases have dedicated ventilation for GPUs.

I'm sure I have a couple more gripes, but that's a LONG list of cons, but I don't hate this case. It's going without a top panel in my entertainment center, and should be adequate. Disappointed that I can't run it with the glass with a high end build, but it is what it is.

title: Clear instructions and independently programmable outlets
text:
My feelings about this product are mixed. The first one I purchased died--completely died--in less than 30 days. So, clearly, that's bad. However, I was pleased enough by the operation and simplicity of this product to buy another one right away. If this one, too, dies shortly, then I'll look for a different brand of contraption. If it does not die or malfunction, though, I'll be perfectly happy with it.

BTW, contrary to what is said in several other reviews, this timer is simple to program, the four green outlets can, in fact, be programmed independently, and if you plug in devices during the period in which they are programmed to be "on," yes, they will function. Now, you *do* have to read the directions because the programming process is not very intuitive. But the steps are few and easy. The printed directions that came with each timer I purchased are identical and clear. Here are the first three steps:

"1. Press the PROG button once. [example of what the screen will say if already programmed, and of what it will say if not programmed]
2. Press the DAY button repeatedly. The display shows the day on which you want the timer to turn ON. [example of days of the week]
3. Press the HR (HOUR) and MN (MINUTE) buttons to select the time of day when you want the timer to turn ON."

And so forth. It's not hard. EDIT: I've had this device for over a year now. I've had to replace the battery once, which was surprisingly difficult. Otherwise, no trouble at all. Constant, reliable functionality and (when I had to reprogram it, after changing the battery) easy operation--as long as one reads the instructions.

title: Syncing time zone erases footage
text:
If you are out of town and change time zones, the next time you log in, the app asks if you want to sync your time stamp. I thought this was cool, so I did it.
But if your time zone is Eastern and your camera has recorded from noon to 1pm, then you log in from Central time zone and it just turned noon there, when you sync, it just backs up the time and starts recording with a time stamp of noon again, overwriting anything else that was previously labeled as 12-1. So your camera will skip an hour. From an Eastern time zone point of view, you will have footage from 11:59:59 and then footage from 1:00:00, with everything else deleted.

Rather than just change the time stamps on the previous footage, the system just backs up and erases an hour of footage. This is nonsensical. If that's how they want to do it, though, fine, but provide a warning that syncing time will result in a loss of footage.

title: Nice big and simple dual alarm clock
text:
Why is it so hard to find a large, sleek looking, inexpensive alarm clock these days that doesn't do stupid stuff like play soothing sounds of the ocean or have a plug for an ipod?

I was happy to finally find this one that is similar to my old Sony that started to crap out. I should say though, that the first one I received was defective. Some of the buttons didn't work, and I couldn't turn on the radio or set the clock. I returned it easily enough and received a 2nd one quickly that worked fine.

I am happy with it overall. I really like that the alarm time is displayed on the front, so no more double checking is necessary. The radio tuning is better than the manual tuning of most radios, but a little weird. When you are turning the dial, the frequency is displayed where the time is usually displayed. This is cool, but I would rather have up and down buttons than a dial that turns. It is a little sensitive and not much easier to pinpoint the exact station number than the old school sliding bar analog dial. It's not like I ever change the station though. Once I set it I will have no reason to change it, unless the local npr station goes under. Also, the audio of the radio is pretty weeny sounding, but then anything is better than BEEP BEEP BEEP BEEP BEEP!!!

That being said, I am very happy with it.

**UPDATE**
Downgraded from 4 stars to 3. The other day, after owning the clock for 7 months, one of the buttons no longer works. Now when setting the alarm time, I cannot advance forward, only backward.

title: ERGONOMICS are AWFUL.
text:
First off, let me say, I love Bushnell Binoculars. I've owned a set of 7 x 35 Bushnell Porro's for 25 years and the optics are fine and I really liked them, but they were beat up and I just wanted to upgrade to a brighter pair (42mm lens) and Roof Prism's. I chose Roof Prism Binoculars as they are more compact than the Porro Binoculars which make them easier to tote and travel with.

1. The optics, the focusing knob, and the eye relief in these Bushnell's were just fine.

HOWEVER!

2. The ERGONOMICS and FEEL of the binoculars is AWFUL.

a. RUBBER COATING. The rubber coating on the outside looks great and feels strong, but the ridges incorporated into the rubber skin
got very uncomfortable after just a few seconds of holding.

b. STRAP MOUNTS. The strap mounts on the barrels are placed in too low. These Roof Prism Binoculars aren't very long
barreled (5" vs most Roofs which are at 6") and the strap holders hit the joints of my pointer fingers every time I held them. AND
since the barrels are short, it is hard to reposition your hands to overcome the bulging neck strap mounts. Now I'm 5'5" with small
hands so having large hands wasn't the issue, in fact, if you have BIGGER HANDS than mine the "strap mount issue" would be EVEN
WORSE!

c. Weight. These Bushnell 8 x 42 H2O Waterproof Roofs weigh in at 25 oz. I thought that when I got them that the weight wouldn't be
an issue. I was wrong. These suckers are HEAVY which led to ARM FATIGUE in a hurry. I compared the H2O's with a pair of 8 x
42 's Vortex Crossfire Roofs I bought at Dick's Sporting Goods. The Vortex weighed in at 21.5 oz and, although 3.5 oz seems like a
small weight difference, it made a huge difference in arm fatigue.
BOTTOM LINE - Buy a lighter pair of binoculars or with better weight distribution, ie. longer barrels.

I felt bad returning these Bushnell's, I really did, because the optics of the Bushnell's were fine, but the ergonomics were just too uncomfortable to overcome.

UPDATE: I bought a pair of the 8 x 25 Bushnell H2O's Compact Binoculars (the mini-me's of these) and I LOVE them (see my review). They are light, comfortable to hold, have two hinges for compact carrying, have really nice optics and look great. For the 8 x 42's I wound up with the Vortex Crossfire II Roofs (see my review) from Dick's Sporting Goods which were a bit more pricy than 8 x 42 Bushnell H2O's ($75 vs $120) but the optics and especially the ergonomics were so much better.

title: Very noisy and annoying, even at idle.  Beware in any environment except loud ones.
text:
I'm a huge fan of the Intel NUC line since the first generation. This particular one (7I7BNH) is a real disappointment, though. It has a blower or fan that is intolerably loud. Even at idle (0-1% CPU utilization) in Windows 10, it's screaming along at nearly 4000 RPM and sounds like a small hair dryer. I updated to the latest BIOS (46) and tried changing the cooling settings to Quiet, performance from Max to balanced, and to customized and it still runs like this. The only way to get it to a normal level of quiet is to set the cooling option to fixed speed / 30-32% cycle and then it runs too hot (60C+) with any normal office type use. Going up to 35% is still noticeably loud/annoying and still too hot.

Further UPDATE: I also just bought an older (6th vs. 7th) gen i7 NUC -- the 6i7KYK -- which has a much faster i7 processor than this 7i7BNH in it and the 6i7KYK is MUCH BETTER with the fan noise. During heavier use, it does spin up, but under normal load it's audible but not annoying. Even under higher load, it's more tolerable than the 7i7BNH is at idle. I suspect there is either something wrong with my brand-new 7i7BNH or there's a firmware fan bug still present.

I realize how tolerable noise is depends on both the user and the environment. For reference, we have 3-4 older-gen i5 NUCs which are virtually undetectable under normal office type loads in a home office and on high sustained CPU are probably about the same dB level as this 7i7 at idle but at a tone/pitch that is more tolerable. I also use as primary machine a significantly faster i7 high-wattage HP desktop that is slightly louder than the other NUCs at idle and significantly quieter under heavy CPU loads than the other NUCs. It is also a more tolerable lower pitch noise due, I presume, to the larger size fans it can use.

I thought I might be able to shuffle this out to lab server use, but alas, driver availability/hackability is very limited. So this 7i7bnh has to go back.

title: Maybe The Best USB Light I've Ever Used - Or NOT !!
text:
I've bought half dozen different USB LED lights and have been disappointed with most of 'em. THIS model is excellent. I've bought a few and reordered from Amazon a couple more batches. The bendy part is very smooth so some people may have problems gripping it to adjust the angle; I thought the bend action was great, as it's easy to bend into all sorts of nifty positions. I even use a couple as handy hallway and bathroom night lights because they draw such an infinitesimal amount of power, yet they are bright as blazes and do not (so far) seem to degrade in output over time. Best NOT to grab the head to do adjustment, as the head can be forced to spin on its mount. That's not good, depending on the stress level of the wires inside the tubing, so don't do it. When plugged in, it does not light up until you press the contact button on top of the lamp head. It starts up full bright (2 LEDs) and if you press the button down again, then only the farthest up LED stays on. The PRECISION LENS aims the two LEDs so perfectly, you cannot tell that there are two distinct LED's underneath. All you see is very bright or bright. One down-aspect of this design is that the light continues to stay OFF when power is withdrawn and re-applied. So if you use it on your laptop/desktop computer, and you need to reboot the computer, the light will shut off on restart, and then stay OFF. Fortunately the ON button is easy to tap on to re-ignite the LEDs, then YET another tap is needed to go down to "bright" output level, since "very bright" may be just too bright, if other people are sitting around you. Lamp head measures 2" x 0.75" at widest point. It's 0.50" thick but the lenses and rubber switch cover bulge out about 1/32" above and below. The bendy tube is about 10" by itself. The USB plug body is 1.5" long, not including the male portion of the USB connector.

Update, September 18, 2014 -- I have several of these lights running several hours a day. Out of 4 units, one has begun to fail electronically. Both LEDs have lost about 50% of their output. Since the failure is on each LED equally, I assume it's the electrical circuitry that powers the lamps. This speaks to a possible selection of low quality components within the lamp. I'll keep a close eye on the other units in the array, and we'll see if more lights fail. For an item of this relatively low cost, the maker is likely aware that few people will spend $11 in shipping to collect on the one-year warranty of their $10 product. I've had to reduce the product rating to 3 stars from five.

For the difference in price, you may want to get the oem battery. This one fits the GIGARANGE series of phones. Here's what I've found- shelf life is about 3 yrs. OEM BAT seem to last longer between charges. Here's one weird thing: when using factory nimh bat. you get a warning beep tone in your ear before phone shuts off. When the oem batteries are new, you get maybe a 3 min. warning. With old stock oem or with the aftermarket batteries, you usually get no warning. The aftermarket bat. can be quite irritating when they die suddenly and you drop a call in progress.I have also run into state oem bat. If you get one, buy from Amazon direct, not a marketplace vendor. Amazon will do the right thing and exchange a poor battery. When you get battery, charge it immediately for 24 hrs. BEFORE USING.
Then use the phone heavily and run the battery down all the way before recharge. Factory batteries are nimh, not nicads, and they should not develop a memory effect problem.

title: A bit pricey but nice
text:
When I bought this I did not realize that this Kindle does not have audio capability. My old Kindle does and I love it for audio books. My old Kindle does not have a screen light however, and this Paperwhite does. Now if I could get a device with both it would get 5 stars. Audio aside I am quite happy with the illuminated screen, the font choices, and the the device's light weight. It has been a joy to use while riding the bike at the gym.

The only real con here is the price (Amazon has all but eliminated the competition as far as dedicated e-readers are concerned so they can charge more for them than the Fires where the competition for customers is fierce). The Paperwhite has only 4 GB of memory and that is not expandable unlike the less expensive Kindle Fires. The Fires are heavier to hold and the screens are "glarier" than the Paperwhites. But in their favor the Fires are less expensive, have expandable memories, and can be used for everything from movie watching to reading books to checking email, etc. Screen glare can be mitigated by using an anti-glare screen protector. So why would anyone choose a Paperwhite over a Fire? For just reading the Paperwhite is the clear winner because of it's weight, anti-glare screen and the battery life which is much longer than the Fires.

All in all I am happy with the Paperwhite. It is a nice addition to my "collection" of e-readers and tablets. However if I had to choose and keep just one device it would be my 8 inch Kindle Fire as it is a great tablet and a very nice e-reader in one device.

One last comment here. Do not be afraid to purchase a certified refurbished Kindle of any kind. This is my third refurbished purchase and they have all been great.

title: Works well, a headache with Frontier
text: A DSL modem-router with good reviews was hard to find at a good price.  This is that.  The setup was challenging with Frontier.  The setup wizard did not work.  I had to call Frontier several times to get the information I needed.  Either the dsl tech wasn't interested in helping me set up a device they did not sell me or they gave me incorrect information.  Finally after many phone calls and waiting forever on phone trees (got disconnected once after a 20 min wait) I got the info I needed.  If you have Frontier as your internet carrier, you must: 1- get your DSL username and password (you don't know it) 2-find out whether your dsl mode is VDSL or ADSL and then get the 2 codes related to each of those modes before this will work.  Then you must call Motorola to get a link sent to you so that you can upload additional software into the modem to accept the username that Frontier uses (if you just use The Wizard it doesn't accept all the digits). Motorola knows of this problem with Frontier and are helpful, but its not an easy set up.  Frontier is the big problem.  Don't call Frontier after normal business hours or you tend to get people that aren't as knowledgeable.  Don't let Frontier off the hook on this one.  If you get a good rep (and I finally did) they have access to all of this information.

title: Missing Wire for Pin 19 to Steering Wheel (-)
text:
I bought this adapter to go with my Ford Focus and the Pioneer AVH-P2400BT. I also purchased the Metra Axxess ASWC Steering Wheel Control Interface. The Metra wiring harness was very easy to coordinate with the aftermarket radio harness, and instllation was a sinch. My main gripe with this harness is that it was missing the wire going to pin 19. The steering wheel controls on the Ford Focus use pin 18 (SWC +) and pin 19 (SWC -). Pin 19 needs to be grounded (i.e. connected to the negative terminal of the battery). This would have been simple, had the wire been provided. But since the wire wasn't provided to pin 19, I had to cut the OEM harness to ground the wire at Pin 19, ultimately defeating the purpose of the Metra Harness.

Overall this product fits is purpose, but if you are looking to keep your steering wheel controls functional go with the Scosche instead.

title: If short isn't a problem (or if it's a plus...) this is an excellent solid tripod.
text:
This (AM-223) is a very short tripod, not a full sized tripod, not something you will use to take family pictures, not something you will use to sit on the ground and take pictures of fireworks, or pics of the sunset. Well ... unless you want to bend over a lot.

However, I'm SOOOOOO glad someone finally made a ROCK SOLID small tripod!!! I like to hike, backpack, and shoot nature - flowers, animals, waterfalls, etc.. My full sized tripods (Benro, Manfrotto, etc) have great stability ... total pain to heft those guys some of the places I go. So I don't. I've got a several Al and carbon travel tripods from similar level manufacturers. They are good, but still a bit bulky/long and really, I never extend the legs beyond maybe one segment as extending more they cross that line of adequate stability IMHO. And I have to rework them and/or remove the center column so they can go low. Then there are those table-top versions that are compact and light but are flimsy even from decent brands. And the heads on those ... can we even call those "heads"...?? Makes me want to cry. That's where this guy comes in. Even though it's far more compact than my travel tripods, it's more stable d/t larger leg diameter and overall beefier construction. Finally, a short/small/compact tripod that is rock solid.

It holds a FF DSLR (ie Nikon D750) with a decent sized lens (ie 70-200F2.8 using the collar mount of course, 105F2.8 micro, even my 135mmF2DF... etc.) without any problem. For mirrorless, I shoot SONY and use MFT when I'm going light; for those it's more than solid, no problem with anything I've got for those including fast telephotos.

Works with my dozens of different brands (some cheap-o no-names) Arca plates - locks them all down tight. Ball head is solid and smooth (not RRS or Kirk, or such, but on par with similar brands/price). No creep, even with heavier setup and in vertical. Legs flatten out so goes as low as any other tripod I have, and is very stable with legs 'flat.'

I've used it for 4-5 months (I typically wait to write reviews until I've really put an item through it's paces...) and it's holding up and functioning great. No concerns about quality, durability, or function.

Fantastic compact tripod. If you need elevation to sitting/standing position, then go with the typical carbon or Al travel tripod - there are lots of those, including larger models in this line. If you don't need much elevation AND you want compact BUY THIS ONE! I've been looking for/ waiting for this guy for 30 years!!

title: Don’t waste your money
text:
Second time reviewing this product (first time Amazon removed it because my colorful language offended them), but it’s still just as garbage as it was the first time I tried to review. Realizing that it’s Mid-March of 2019, this piece of crap has now been installed in my car for a whole year!!! Which really says something about my patience, because the screen hasn’t worked in about 10 months!!!

The design is crap to begin with, no matter how I installed it in my car, there was 0 chance it was going far enough into the dash to not be sticking out nearly an inch from the dash, and I don’t mean the faceplate. I mean the legit metal bracket that the radio sits in is sticking that far out. The screen died quick but I was able to find a way to make it work on a case by case basis....until the motor burned out and it doesn’t even open anymore. Lucky for me, I reset the Bluetooth connect code to one I can remember before the screen died or I would have never been able to reconnect my phone when I got a new one.

Speaking of Bluetooth, today started the very annoying issue of disconnecting my phone randomly while I’m driving with my music playing. Not exactly what you want to deal with when driving on the highway in the rain. It disconnected and reconnected itself 3 times in a 30 minute drive which is what reminded me to review this turd.

In short, don’t waste your money. I spent $80 on a Sony radio without a screen to put in my truck 6 years ago and that radio has still not had a single problem. This one has been nothing but a problem
