title: Don’t Bother - Misleading Description and Photos
text:
I did a lot of research before buying this bag from Amazon. I give it a one-star rating because the photos and description are misleading. First, the laptop compartment does not fit my 17” laptop: when I took it out of the laptop “sleeve” in the compartment, I even had to squeeze the corners inside the zipper. My laptop is 16.5 inches long. I thought about just putting the laptop in its sleeve and then putting that in the slightly larger main compartment. Even that was a poor fit, and I was concerned about the laptop sliding around in that big compartment, with no good protection except its sleeve. The second thing that really bothered me is the fact that the side straps do not unfasten. This makes it very awkward, cumbersome, and frustrating to put things inside the main compartment without constantly having to move my hands over and under the straps. Every other piece of luggage like this that I’ve researched (and I’ve researched at least 15 different brands) has side straps that unfasten/unbuckle. Also, that main compartment’s zipper does not allow one to open the compartment all the way, contrary to all other similar bags I researched: even if the straps did unbuckle, that compartment could not open all the way (to a 90 degree angle) because the zipper won’t allow it. Finally, the description of the height of this bag, wheels included, was incorrectly stated in the several descriptions I read before deciding to buy: the height is reputedly 21.5 inches, according to said descriptions. That is incorrect: the height is 20.5 inches. Yes, I know that the current description states that the height is 20.5”; that was not present when I was researching this item over the last 2-3 weeks. I could have worked around the side straps problem, but I literally cannot work around the fact that High Sierra’s description of the height misled me.
In all fairness, I cannot speak on the durability and sturdiness of the case because I haven’t used it - and won’t, based on my abovementioned experience. As to the travel worthiness and appropriateness of the case, and based on the trouble I had trying to securely and effectively place even only one article in it, I stand by my rating of one star. One should not have this much trouble in packing and using a rolling laptop backpack, a case that comes from such a (supposedly) reputable company as High Sierra (HS). I am disappointed in HS for the abovementioned reasons and - in a way - in particular, for the poor design of side straps that do not unfasten. I will be returning this item and will buy a more appropriate - and truly described - item from a High Sierra and Amazon competitor. Had I known the case would be like this, I would not have bought it. I do not recommend this product.

title: Sheds carbon fibers!
text:
This thing sheds carbon fibers when use. And carbon fibers conduct electricity. If any of these fibers find their way into electronics, it could be a major problem. And they could also cause problems in other moving parts.

The fibers are about 1/2" long, and are very fine. You don't see them unless the lighting is just right. And then you can see them on the surface of the vinyl, or the platter mat (if it's something like a rubber mat).

I'm not sure if this is a problem that is typical of these carbon fiber brushes. It may well be. Carbon fibers are stiff, and I suspect these fine fibers will break off as they get repeatedly flexed.

It's bad enough getting lint and dust on your vinyl, which needs to be removed. But the tool you are using should not leave anything that is worse (tiny electrically conductive fibers)!

title: Buyer beware
text:
Apparently there are two version of this drive floating around:
One mounts as a fixed drive (for windows 8 compliance)
Other one mounts as a regular USB drive

Sandisk originally had them mount as USB, then switched to fixed, then switched to USB again.
The problem with this is twofold:
Windows 8 users have to have the fixed disk version in order for the drive to be W8 compliant
Non windows 8 users have to have the USB version in order to be able to create a bootable drive (windows install disc, Unbuntu, OPenelec etc)

there is no way to tell what you are getting, the item numbers are exactly the same - total crapshoot, if you get the wrong version you are SOL as Sandisk will not exchange/RMA the item for you since it's not technically broken. Buyer beware

title: Updated to 4 stars! Read updated comment. Working again!
text:
First off I baby my iPhone 6s Plus. I take very excellent care of it and was very disappointed in this case. Yet still it is a very nice case for these reasons. No.

I don't have good experience with aftermarket batteries - quality varies considerably, even among samples from the same manufacturer. It appears that Amazon's quality control on batteries for these devices let at least one bad one through.

title: Have you tried turning it off and on again
text: I had high hopes when I bought this router to upgrade from my ISPs provided WiFi. I looked around and read all of the reviews and decided the TP-Link Archer C7 was the one. I chose it because it was dual band supporting both 2.4 Ghz and 5GHz, seemed to have good reviews, and a reasonable price. I was excited when I took it out of the package because it just looks more substantial than the junk my ISP supplies. I set it up adding it to my network and disabled the WiFi on my ISPs equipment. I connected all the various devices in my house to the 5GHz network. A lot of my devices are newer and already supported 5Ghz. I had a few devices still on 2.4 Ghz and I connected them the the 2.4 Ghz network. Everything seemed to be good for a few days. Then the lost connectivity started happening on various devices. Sometimes devices would work fine, then start to lose connectivity. The entire 5Ghz network would seem to drop out of existence and no device could see it. At other times the 2.4 Ghz network would drop out and could not be seen. Each time the only cure was a reboot of the TP-Link to restore connectivity. I am an IT guy with 20 years experience in the business. I am the guy everyone calls to troubleshoot and fix their tech. I have done everything short of sending the device back for a refund to try and make this router more stable. When it works, it is super fast and life is good. Then seemingly at random, things go south and a reboot is the only cure. I know that this is a piece of consumer grade equipment and I shouldn't expect it to perform like a business grade piece of equipment that costs 20x more money. However this thing frustrates the crap out of me anyway. I am very close to writing a script to reboot the router nightly when no one uses it. It's crazy sad when the guy who says "Have you tried turning it off and on again" is forced to turn it off and on again.....

title: Buyer Beware!
text:
I bought this laptop on Prime Day because it was small and thin (good for travel and being mobile) and was a Windows OS. I am the owner of a Lenovo (IBM) Thinkpad that is about 6 years old, running Windows 7 and I LOVE IT! Given my enthusiasm for my ThinkPad, I thought giving this a try was worth it. Upon receipt the Free Windows 10 upgrade was just around the corner so I really didn't do much with this device other than begin to browse some and try to learn Windows 8.1. Can safely say I am not a fan of Windows 8 so was really happy when I finally got my alert to download Windows 10 .. but that's when the trouble started. This device has a 32GB hard drive. 22GB is partitioned to normal use, 6GB is supposed to be a recovery partition and the other 2GB not real sure. Well of the 22GB for operational use roughly 12GB is used by the baseline image on the device. So, when the WIN10 upgrade was available I was unable to download as there wasn't enough space (Note: could download but not enough space to install). While I hadn't really added much I tried to purge anything unnecessary to recover space. The best I could get to was 14GB but WIN10 needs 16GB. Next I tried to use an external hard-drive to complete the install but it kept stalling and couldn't sense the external drive on the multiple re-starts needed as part of the WIN10 install process.

Frustrated with the whole thing and only being about 15 days past receipt, I thought .. well maybe if I do a factory reset this will give me the space I need. Oh no .. although Windows 8 has a very user friendly "Recovery" menu it couldn't sense the recovery partition. I called Lenovo for help and they had me search for the "one button recovery pin hole" - but it doesn't exist on this device (should note the Lenovo agent hung up on me as she couldn't really help me .. or maybe it was the end of her shift). The "push-button recovery" procedure in the user manual didn't work and the restart and press F2, F8 or F11 didn't work either. After getting hung up on I thought "forget it, I'll just return it" so I called Lenovo back and requested media to restore the OS because the is NO MEDIA INCLUDED WITH THE DEVICE and low and behold they wanted $69 bucks for it, no way!

I have spent HOURS trying to recover, download new media and install it or try again to install WIN 10 - no luck. In the course of all this I also learned that the OS on this is "special" it is Windows 8.1 with Bing .. a special version the Microsoft made available to manufacturers for free. While I get it helped with the low price not having media or a product key is crap!

So .. here I sit trying one last time to install WIN10 - not because I want it but rather it is my last hope to wipe the device before I return it. By now new versions are likely shipping with WIN10 so maybe most of my points are moot - but be warned! I may have caused some of my issues as a result of my purge but when its said and done this device is not a good value, even when taking into account you get what you pay for.

title: I bought the camera to make sure that had amazing photos from a trip that had special meaning for ...
text:
I've just returned from my Christmas vacation where I used my new NX1 for 3 solid weeks. 1400 photos and a number of 4K videos later, I wanted to share my experience. I bought the camera to make sure that had amazing photos from a trip that had special meaning for me and I wanted to ensure I had a tool to capture the moments. My photos do not disappoint. My videos are amazing. So while here are a few things that push my review down from what I want to give (5 of 5) to where it really should be (3 of 5), there’s a whole lot to love about this camera and the ‘S’ lens 16-50mm OIS F2.0-F2.8. First the build quality is amazing. The body feels solid and the lens (I have the 16-50mm S lens) are just amazing. The machine feels precise. The ergonomics work great for me. I have average size hands and they never felt tired or awkward in any way. It was a real pleasure to hold the camera. I've previously used a Nikon SLR camera extensively and so I can say that comparatively this one really felt right. The photos I've taken are amazingly good when using the RAWs. It's a really treat to be sitting in front of my 4K display and seeing that level of sharpness and clarity. If you sense there's a gotcha, I'll get to this in a minute below. I figured out the manual settings quickly and had no problems figuring out the menu system - it's quite easy for the stuff that matters. Just have to remember that when you're in manual mode, the camera remembers the settings across frames so if you put the camera down you need to double check - that's why you're in manual (usually) since you want the control. Overall I have some really great shot in various lighting conditions, including great shots in terrible indoor lighting. The included Adobe Lightroom let me use the RAWs to produce really good to amazing photos. The ‘S’ lens is fast across its full zoom range – so f2.0 to f2.8. This made no-flash indoor photos possible and the combination worked extremely well. So much so that most of my photos indoors had no flash. Only time I used a flash was when there was really strong backlight (windows) or for some group shots with inconsistent lighting. Otherwise I shot without flash, without tripod, indoors, outdoors, from moving trains, etc. and got really great photos.
So why not give this thing a 5 of 5 review? Here's what you need to know: The “AUTO” mode is useless for two reasons that combine together to make for a terrible outcome. AUTO only shoots in JPEGs – there’s no option that I’ve found to enable it to capture JPEG + RAW. So if you’re like me and want to ensure you’re getting amazing photos, then you have to go to one of the manual settings. So that’s already a problem but one that I figured out quickly and actually I don’t mind setting the manual setting – I usually shoot aperture priority anyways so it’s not a stretch for me. Where it’s less desirable, it’s harder to give the camera to a novice and have them produce anything worth not deleting. But on top of that, JPEGs coming out of the Samsung NX1 suck. If you're used to the image quality of a Canon JPEG, this camera will disappoint you. You'll need to go to Lightroom and export the image from RAW and then you'll get an amazing JPEG, but the ones the camera produces are terrible, disappointing, and a waste. When smartphones can create amazing JPEGs these days one would think Samsung of all companies would have that code nailed. I bought the camera to get amazing RAWs so I'm not terribly upset by the JPEG issue. But the JPEG issue + the AUTO issue, take a -1 star hit for this camera since it’s harder to use for the novice and more time consuming for the pro. Wonder if we'll see another firmware update to fix this (one can only hope; please read this Samsung!).
Auto focus is fast but really questionable/unreliable. When you press to autofocus, except in rare occasions the focus goes quickly to something usable. But it’s not amazing. Too often, it doesn’t pick the most interesting feature in the center of the frame. It has no face detection! (if it is there, please tell me because I tried to find it and failed) If you press to autofocus repeatedly on the same composition, you’ll infuriatingly see the focus change to other features but there’s no rhyme or reason to it. For a $1K camera body I have to say its -1 star for that! Having used many cell phone cameras that have great face detection, the auto focus here is lacking. It’s really surprising that Samsung seemingly didn’t take learnings from its smart phones and feed them into this feature. Too often, I had to resort to manual focus to get the right focus for portraits and group shots. It doesn’t help that the 16mm lens actually works against you for some of these shots! At 16mm the area that’s in focus is extremely tight (depth of field) so you have to be very careful as to what you’re focusing on. In my indoor group shots that were taken in small rooms it’s noticeable that some faces are clearly in focus and others are slightly blurry. This I’m thinking is due to how precise the focus and the sensor are so I’m not faulting the camera (it’s mostly a photographer skill issue). But that aside, the autofocus should really be able to help me get better focus in these situations so I don’t have to do it all manually. For example, it could offer the option so scroll through different focus features and offer face detection. The manual focus works well. I was a little concerned at first by the amplification during manual focus since it doesn’t let you pan around in the zoomed mode (that’s a gripe more than anything). Once if figured it out it wasn’t a problem.
Reviewers previously noted that this camera uses the newer H.265 4K video codec instead of the more commonly used H.264. The benefit is smaller files (a good thing long term) at the cost of default compatibility (a bad thing short term). I’m not seeing it as too much of a problem yet myself. More of an issue is that my computer at home seems to have difficulty playing the 4K videos – not sure if it’s a codec issue or just that my hardware is older (Intel Core i5 2500K + AMD 6770 graphics card + new 4K monitor) and now I’m pushing it beyond where it’s comfortable. But knowing that I can capture the video at those rates is really compelling as a ‘future proofing’ for this camera purchase. Software to view the videos was easy to find - I just downloaded the latest DIVX media player and I’m off to the races. Still need to find a good encoder to re-encode my videos to a more usable codec or resolution.
One more thing – the built-in flash is useless when using the 16mm-50mm ‘S’ lens. The problem is that the ‘S’ lens is so big it shades the flash in photos. You’ll see a pronounced dark oval centered at the bottom of shots. Here’s the good news: you don’t need a flash for the vast majority of shots with the ‘S’ lens. It’s amazing what fast glass does for you and how jarringly harsh light from a flash is once you have fast glass. I did use a flash for some of my photos, but that was a Nikon SPEEDLIGHT SB-600 flash inherited from my earlier Nikon days and just keeps working – here’s the thing – I used it on maybe 20 out of the 1400 photos I shot on my trip. Most of those were figuring out how much light to add to a specific scene and mostly after playing with it for a bit, I figured out that I can set the flash to its minimum output. The lens and camera are just that good.
Overall I’m really happy with the purchase. While I’m giving a 3 of 5 star review, I’ll also say that when I was doing my research (November 2015) this was the best camera by far for the price. It had the biggest and highest resolution sensor (28MP), with fantastic RAWs, the best overall lens combo (in my opinion) with the ‘S’ lens 16mm-50mm f2.0 – f2.8 with OIS, and was the only sub $3,000 camera to shoot true 4K video (I paid just over $2,000USD for the combination). Other cameras were selling for less if you got the kit lens that typically was f3.5-f5.6 or similar. But when I started to look for faster glass I found two things – it was hard to match the versatility of the 16mm-50mm ‘S’ lens in any other single lens or two lens system in the same price range. The fast shooting rate of the camera is amazing if you can keep your subject in focus (or just as a party trick since it its sounds just amazing!). All the controls on the body are built solid and feel like they’ll last for a decade. The OLED screen is really awesome. There’s even a selfie mode built in that will beep when you’re in focus! There’s a ton of software trickery features built-in like wifi and emailing photos from the camera, or using your android phone to remote trigger the shutter that I’ve not fully played with. It would say that some things like detecting/connecting to my network are slower than I’d hoped for, but then I wasn’t buying the camera because of those features. They stay out of the way until you want to use them, which is high praise. You get a ton of stuff in the box – an extra battery, an external charger (this is priceless!), a portrait grip that can contain the second battery, and Adobe Lightroom. It’s really one hell of a package compared to what you get with other cameras in this class. While the initial idea of spending $2K on a camera was a lot to ask for, the photos I got have made it worth it. Most importantly I feel I bought a tool that I can use to make amazing photos, one that will not show its technology limits for years, and one that will keep me engaged for many years to come.

title: Great Mouse, EXCEPT for one button...
text:
Ordered this mouse a while ago and it worked great for a couple months until it started failing on me. More on that below. First let's look at the pros and cons of this mouse.

PROS:
- Good design: Looks great on the desk and it is very comfortable.
- Plenty of buttons and features.
- App for Windows and Mac to tweak all the settings.
- Bluetooth AND USB receiver option.
- Battery life is great lasting for months a time with just one charge.
- The infinite scroll wheel feature and the thumb/horizontal scroll wheel are fantastic features to have in a mouse. Many uses like video editing (timeline horizontal scrolling), long and wide spreadsheets, brush size adjusments, zoom; etc. become a breeze to navigate.
- The expression button under the thumb brings a whole new layer of functionality (until it breaks).

CONS:
- Pricey, but might be worth it depending on your needs.
- The back and forward buttons are crammed on top of the other and way into the back of the thumb side of the mouse, difficult to access and tell apart from each other just by feel.
- Connectivity issues, especially on Bluetooth, not so much with the included USB receiver. They have improved over time with software updates, but still present from time to time.

AND NOW FOR THE BIGGEST DOWNSIDE OF THIS MOUSE: THE EXPRESSION BUTTON BREAKS.
I know this is not an isolated issue with my unit only as I went online to search for a fix and a lot of people were having the same problem. There are even YouTube video tutorials on how to fix that button.

At first the button was great, adding a ton of functionality. Basically you hold down on it with your thumb and the cursor is disabled so you can do "gestures" or mouse movements that will control functions like volume, change songs, or whatever you configure in the app.

I had it set so that I while pressing the gesture button and moving the mouse up or down will change the volume. Sideways would skip music tracks. That was a great feature to have and it saved me a lot of time.

The button started being very clicky and responsive, then after a while it started to become mushy, but it still worked ok. Some time later, it was so sensitive that normal resting of the thumb on it would activate it, triggering the gestures at unwanted times.

Finally it became stuck, rendering the mouse unusable. In gesture mode, you cannot move the cursor. In my case, trying to do so would only change the volume and music tracks. I had to move the mouse around, place it upside down and bang it slightly with my hand to TRY to free it again. It was a pain and it seldom worked.

Finally, I gave up and had to disable the gestures altogether from the app.

I was so used to that feature that I became frustrated for not having it after a while. So I followed the tutorials posted by others having the same problem and opened the mouse to adjust some screws that hold the button mechanism in place. This is not very easy, because you have to remove the sliding pad under the mouse to access the screws that hold the case together. This piece is GLUED to the mouse, so you have to be careful not to break it while pulling it off and, when you're done, you need to glue it back again.

This worked for a little while and then it became stuck again. I did it again but it failed AGAIN within a couple weeks.

Ultimately I gave up, because it was just not worth it to do that painful repair every couple weeks to keep that button working.

CONCLUSION:
I keep using the mouse as of today because, other than the gesture button breaking, it is comfortable and works well on the other aspects. But still I feel let down by Logitech after spending $100 on a mouse with an issue like this.

I bought this 5 channel amp to power all but the front L/R in my 7.1 system (which use a cambridge 840w amp). I previously bought a xpa-2 for my mulit-room built in system. I was delighted with the xpa-2: tremendous sound quality, most noticeable in the bass when compared with the NAD it replaced.

This noise is modest (sort of the same volume as a whisper) and does not at all interfere with watching a movie. The manual clearly states a slight buzz may come from sensitive speakers, which I have.

So, practically the amp s great- I really enjoy it. But I have owned three other power amps, and the buzz from this is far worse.

Thus, a fine surround amp, but clearly not audiophile grade.

I also spend multiple nights per year out in the backcountry on backpacking trips. I had it set so that the only notifications that I got were texts and SnapChats. I set the workout to Hike and began the weekend’s adventure. Unfortunately, the watch died even before we stopped for the night, approximately 7 miles in. I was extremely disappointed that it didn’t even last the full day. I always charge my Fossil every night and it always lasts a full day. Based on my experience with the Fossil watch on the backpacking trip, I won’t be purchasing another Fossil watch to wear on backpacking trips nor will I get another one when my current watch needs replacing. I need a watch that will last at least 12 hours when much of it is in hiking mode. If Fossil would significantly improve the battery life, I would definitely get another one. It’s great watch.

title: Great form but lacks sufficient power to serve power-hungry devices
text:
After reading all the reviews before purchasing this hub, concerned mostly with the reliability, I went ahead and bought it because it seemed be a stylish yet functional hub that was also weighted enough to keep from twisting and rocking off its base when its ports were all loaded.

As far as the form, it is perfect design and handles all stiff cabling connected to it without lifting off the table or being pulled to a particular side.

The USB cables stay tight in the ports. The power plug, however, tends to be a little loose and can accidently be pulled out when handling the hub.

The major drawback, however, is its poor power serving abilities. Hard drives, iPhone (3G) and iPod all seem to malfunction in weird ways when used with the hub. When transferring large data to hard drives, my USB speakers (Harmon Kardon) and other sometimes other ports disconnect and are no longer recognized, sometimes necessitating a reboot.

If syncing large data such as music, photos and/or videos to my iPhone 3G, iTunes will ALWAYS disconnect the iPhone 3G during the Sync.

Basically, this hub is only useful for low-to-no power consuming USB devices, such as flashdrives and printers.

To summarize, as just a "plain" hub, this works as expected. And its aesthetic design is beyond reproach, with its callout feature being a weighted base. But being sold as a POWERED hub, it fails miserably. And thus, even though this hub has more than enough ports to handle my current platoon of USB devices, for my power hungry USB devices, my search continues as I will be forced to have TWO USB hubs on my desk.

title: They had a good run, but it's over now
text:
I've had various iterations of Arlo at my home since their first release of cameras. I went from the original wire-free to Q-series and now some Ultra 4ks.

I've been absolutely tired of replacing batteries on the older Arlo's, so I was glad to switch to the Ultra design that allowed me to run an external power adapter to it. I also decided I really wanted the full 24/7 recording. This is because these cameras (including the ultra), routinely MISS triggering motion, especially if the object moving is not within 10 ft of the sensor. This causes a lot of missed/truncated clips. That's why I thought 24/7 (CVR) would be the ticket here. I decided to opt for the Continuous recording for my 3x Ultra's and 1xQ-series. Cost $365/year subscription.

I've had these units for the past 6 months recording 24/7. The Arlo app itself is not super responsive with these cameras and very often the time-scrubber doesn't work at all when using 24/7 recording. The regular "clip" based recordings usually work if the camera actually trips the motion sensor. Most of the time, you are just lucky if you can scroll to the area of the video you want to watch. The majority of the time, you are greeted with failures to connect to cameras in addition to unresponsive timeline loading.

This past new year, I noticed all 3 of my Ultra's were not recording 24/7. Tech support asked me to disable my CVR plan and resubscribe. This led to me needing a new updated subscription which was recently rolled out. My bill went up to $515, over $150 more than before per year. This didn't fix my Ultra issues, so I started to look elsewhere.

That's when I found Nest. I currently have 3 of their cameras with two more on the way. Instead of jacking up the prices like Arlo did, Google is REDUCING theirs. The New Nest Aware Plus subscription coming out will have a flat rate of $120/year for unlimited 24/7 (10-day 24/7, 60-day event history) regardless of how many cameras you have. Their cameras respond INSTANTLY vs Arlo. The timeline scrubber is real-time. It's insane the speed difference. The video quality is much better in addition and notifications are instant too.

Arlo had a good run, but code quality and lack of a reasonable subscription plan has priced them out of contention.

Edit: 6/2020. Absolutely love the nest cameras. Can’t believe I stuck with Arlo for as long as I did. I have 5 nest cameras. They have worked perfectly!

title: Inconsistent device
text:
Initially i was suuuuper excited to have a tiny, sleek-looking device that would integrate with other fitness apps (like MyFitnessPal) and allow me to compete with my friends on daily exercise tasks. However. The software for this device seems to be half-baked (and I'm a software tester with 8+ years experience, so i feel confident saying these things). I'm running into several different kinds of software bugs that are negatively influencing my opinion of this device.

The problems I've encountered include (but are not limited to):
-- some days this device just decides to stop counting my steps the right way and reports 1 step for about every 10 i take
-- some days this device decides to count steps but NOT REMEMBER them, reverting to some "remembered" step count, for example, even after a 2 mile walk telling me I'd only walked 253 steps
-- resetting the device only sometimes works to fix the above issues (usually I'm resetting 5 or more times to get it to work)
-- the bluetooth syncing speed is inconsistent even when I"m at home on my own wireless network. some days it takes 20 seconds to sync, other days it takes 5+ minutes
-- the app challenges get reset and/or not counted if my phone turns off while I'm doing them and in fact I've yet to record a successful challenge on the app yet!
-- after the most recent upgrade, the app keeps messaging me about losing connection with the device
-- the striiv website is hard to navigate, has poor trouble-shooting and FAQ info, and so far i've been unable to link my device to my web account at all
-- customer service *claims* 1-day turnaround for questions/concerns submitted to them but I've been waiting nearly 2 weeks now with no reply (much less answers) about the above concerns

If i were to do this again, I'd probably buy a FitBit instead, even though they're more expensive.

I sometimes shoot while wearing a vest with molle attachment points and this fits perfectly on the loops. No more sticking the flash in a cargo pocket on my pants or shorts ( had a flash unit destroyed this way while shooting a wedding. ) I have not played with the off camera triggering options yet but hope to soon. Unlike my previous auto zoom flash, this unit will auto zoom and ttl meter at different angles. The xit flash will automatically enter a sleep mode if not used for a few seconds but it is easily awakened with a half press of the shutter release. The value and quality to cost ratio here makes this an easy decision on whether to purchase one or not. I use mine on a nikon d90 and d80 body and it works flawlessly on both. In general:

The remote is quite limited, and as your trying to think of what you are wanting to make happen next, the box will follow along. In other words, you can't surf for something while watching a program or listen to a music source. That was a little lame to me.
As a music player: It does OK. I use Pandora a lot. So I can go to my subscription, free of charge (other than choosing to pay Pandora for commercial free music). The navigation on the Pandora screen allows me to thumbs up or down a track, skip, book mark and so on. So it's not bad for that use, which is the primary use.

Free, for a limited time, then you get subscribe or buy shows or what have you. I was really bummed that you can't watch Hulu for free. What's even more ridiculous is that even if you do pay for Hulu "Plus" so you can watch it on your player, you're still gonna get hit with "limited commercial interruptions". LAME.
Oh ya, one more little thing. When you're setting things up, get ready to bring out those 1990's navigational skills, because you'll need them, again and again. It doesn't auto fill your e-mail or anything when you're signing up for channels. So you get to hunt and click your way through the alphabet one character at a time. That's really fun... especially if you have a long e-mail address.
In the end, would I buy it again? No, I don't think so. Do I hate it enough to return it. No, it's playing my music right now, and that's all a really wanted.

title: Does not work with the iGo splitter!
text:
We always use the iGo splitter to charge either a GPS and a phone or two phones at the same time. Never had a problem with Blackberries and Treos. If the iGo splitter is connected to the iGo charger, even if I am trying to charge only the iPhone 3Gs and nothing is plugged in to the other end of the splitter, the phone does not recognize that it's plugged into anything and does not charge. If I remove the splitter and plug this tip directly into the iGo charger cable then it charges the phone. That's ridiculous and unacceptable. I'm blaming iGo for that, not the phone, because clearly the splitter just being inline changes something as the phone only plugs into the tip.

title: Loud popping noise between tracks and with use of buttons, it drove me to return the device.
text:
I'll say the good things first because honestly I wanted to keep this device because after looking at a LOT of different players this one NAILED the looks, price, size and all the main things I wanted. But the main issues drove me to return it the very next day.

The overall build of the device is pretty solid, the phone jack feels secure, the case has a nice solid feel to it, it wasn't too light (cheap feeling) and it wasn't too heavy. The overall design of the button layout and case shape looks great, it's reminiscent of the 2000's era of Zunes, Irivers, Ipods and the Nomad. And it looks as advertised, smooth and solid. The buttons were satisfying to push and responsive but I was on the fence about the scroll wheel, it didn't move too smoothly but the response to the actual movement was accurate enough to satisfy me. The slight dislike I had was that there wasn't an on/off lockout option. Once the screen is off the buttons don't respond to any touch. That's good for accidentally leaning against it and having your music blast into your ears but bad for really quick music selection and volume control. Luckily this isn't a touch screen based model, so you can simply tap the on/off button quickly, so it is more of a nit pick for me.

I definitely enjoy the simple interface/installation it has, you simply slide in folders and you're good to go. It has none of that proprietary program junk I had to deal with for itunes or other devices I used in the past. It was so easy I took the Micro SD card from my old MP3 player, popped it in and didn't have to do any adjustments. Navigating was easy too, you can look at artists/playlist/genre's/etc but also take a simple route and look into a folder directory, that's something missing on other devices I've had in the past.

The sound on this thing is fantastic! It pushes quite a lot of power and the range of sound it has is very desirable. I don't own a lot of flac files but this is definitely pushing me to seek out higher quality sound files. AND I was actually excited to use my studio headphones again, I was using midrange earbuds because my past device didn't output nearly as well!

Battery was great, it lasted all day at work and I didn't even have it 100% charged yet.

I would have kept this device, especially at the price but the 2 main issues made me change my mind fast. I had it suddenly not recognize a file I had JUST played earlier and it suddenly shut down. When it restarted it refused to play a single file at all. It wouldn't respond to any menu buttons and it endlessly cycled through each one stating "Play Failed Unsupported File!" Once I rebooted it a second time I was able to listen to music but there was another issue that put the nail in the coffin for it. At the start/end of ANY file type a very audible pop or static noise was heard, this also happened when the play/pause button was pressed and some menu navigation buttons. I tried really hard to ignore it but it was 90% of the time and very apparent. I ran every kind of test to get it to stop, I tried reloading files, I used multiple SD cards brands, I loaded every file type I could think of, I listened to the same track on a different device, I tried letting the audio tracks auto skip because I thought maybe the buttons interfered, I tried it with the screen off, I tried it with the screen on, I used three different headphones with quality ranging from $30-$180, used it with my 7.1 sound system, I even removed album art thinking a rare possibility of loading the image interfered. It all had the same result.

I still gave it a high review because if I had a working one I'd be totally happy but I was afraid of doing the endless loop of bad luck devices and ending up with a defective one anyway.

title: Beware of Netgear - Won't be Purchasing from them again.
text:
My experience with this "Top of the line" router has been sketchy at best. Thankfully the wonderful Gods at Amazon were able to compensate for Netgear's JOKE for customer service.
We bought this December 31 2014. "1 year Warranty" it claims. It worked pretty well for that year, but honestly not perfect, and definitely not worth the extra $100/$150 on other good models. It still lost connectivity infrequently, more and more so as the year passed on. Finally, just after year exactly, only 1 or 2 weeks, the thing DIES. Orange light DEAD. So now we're on our 9 year old router (which still works just fine, take a hint Netgear) trying to get customer support. This part killed me how prudish and difficult they make it to get online assistance. First, they really want to make sure you're not wasting any of their time by requiring proof you've even purchased a device by making you enter in a serial number and purchase date of your device. After I finally got all that, they notify you that assistance with your device is only free the first three months after your purchase! The year warranty was misleading. So you will be charged for trying to talk to them if your device is older than three months! Who do you think you are!? APPLE??? If it sounds like a personal vendetta, it is. This is a Giant peeve of mine that ANY company has this policy. Denying your customers (especially ones that have spent money on your top of the line devices) the right to free customer service is beyond outrageous to me, and for this reason alone, Netgear, we will never be purchasing from your company again.
Livid at the injustice of not even being able to somehow contact Netgear for free assistance, I reached out to Amazon, who promptly responded and offered me a replacement! (THATS customer service Netgear!) I asked Amazon if the router dying was a consistent problem because obviously I didn't want to go through this again and he said not particularly, this is a "top of the line product" and I must have just got a lemon.
SO I have another nighthawk on the way, my only hope is that it lasts longer than a year. Much longer.
Overall review of the unit: Works well. Worth $300? Nah. Forget Netgear though. Go with a service you can actually talk to if you need to.

Thank you Amazon for making up for Netgear's failures.

title: USB port randomly shut down!
text:
As my review title might tell you, I'm not (EDIT: WAS not) super happy with the reliability of this receiver. Originally I thought the USB port just completely failed (circuit burned out, whatever. It totally quit!) Instead, here's how easy, yet stupid, it was to fix; I unplugged the receiver and then plugged it back in and the USB port went back to working. (After over a month of ownership, the USB port shutdown hasn't occurred again since the 1st time.) So glad I thought to try that before shipping it back! (The "Raytheon reset", as they say (or used to say) in the Navy.)

If you're honest with yourself, you will probably not go wrong in the sound quality department with any receiver you buy above a few hundred bucks assuming your audio/video sources, speakers, and video monitor are up to snuff as well. The Sony STR-DN1050 does not have any fundamental issues in the sound department according to my listening nor research. You can find many reviews that say this unit sounds great. Above great, even. Plenty of other folks will tell you that ANY Sony receiver is crap (whether or not they have actually listened to one, or this one in particular). If you are in the latter group then you are only here to troll, and you should just go back to listening to your vinyl records on a $5000, 50watt/channel, stereo tube amp through $1000 dollar cables to $5000 speakers and leave the rest of us alone.

I replaced a ten year old, $1000 level Yamaha with this Sony, and that Yamaha was itself the replacement for another $1000 level Yamaha that I also had for about 10 years. Neither of those Yamahas had any significant failures and still sounded as good as the day I got them. They had just fallen behind in the receiver features race. My initial evaluation is that the Sony is not as high quality in basic amplifier details as those Yamahas (no surprise at nearly half the price), but I can't tell the difference by the sound and as long as the 1050 also lasts 10 years I will have no complaints about the trade off. With HDMI 2.0, wifi, bluetooth, etc., the 1050 seems as future proof as receivers ever get.

Hopefully, if you're here looking at these reviews, you've already done your research and know what this receiver can (or should) be able to do, so I won't re-hash those details.
This receiver can (or should) be able to do A LOT, and so I'll say up front that most everything I'm about to tell you may have a fix, or some sort of rhyme or reason I just haven't figured out yet. However, I'm a reasonably smart guy with a reasonably high level of aptitude in home theater and I haven't been able to figure them out so I'll just go ahead and tell you about them.

So on to my experiences and gripes:

1. As mentioned, on day 2 of ownership the USB port went dead (NOTE: again, it's working now). It worked fine out of the box. Then on the 2nd day I was using it to listen to an iPod and then came back a few hours later and nothing plugged into the USB port would work. I tried different cables, devices, thumb drives, you name it.
The loss is tragic, because the fact that this receiver plays music from (while charging them!) all of my family's Apple products is pretty awesome. Also, in my short time while the USB port was working, I really liked that I could plug a USB thumb drive in and play music straight off it. And not just mp3 or wma, but also AAC (and a bunch of others I didn't try)! I can't think of an electronic product (that was not a PC based computer program/app) that I got that didn't come from Apple that would play AAC, and subsequently a large portion of my music collection is AAC so that is a great feature in my book. Come to think of it, I have had one other component that played AAC as well: My PS3. Well done, Sony!

2. As you've probably seen, this receiver does not have unlimited inputs. Probably more than enough for any normal person, but it is what it is and you have to decide if you can live with what it has. (For HDMI, that number is 5 rear panel HDMI and 1 front panel HDMI. Add in 2 HD capable component inputs and you get a total of 8 HD inputs. Why does the Sony site and the Amazon page for the 1050 say 8 HDMI inputs and 10 total HD inputs? I can't begin to guess, and it really irks me in principle, but if you've done your research then you know what it really has.)
My critical needs were 4 hdmi inputs, and I was really hoping that the fact this was a Sony product would mean that I'd finally have real interoperability between my Sony XBR6 TV, Sony BR player, and my receiver.
Regarding inputs, of the limited inputs the 1050 has it repeats them across several formats of input (e.g. there is a "SA-CD/CD" input in HDMI, Optical, and Analog RCA). It's a little confusing, and I'm still playing with it, but one of the ways that they've gotten around conflicts is to have separate "watch" and "listen" groups. In my case I have an external HD Radio receiver, Sony no less, (what is it with NO ONE having HD Radio in their receivers still after all the years it's been out?) plugged into the SA-CD/CD analog input, and my HTPC hooked into the SA-CD/CD HDMI input. I've been able to rename each input to what I actually have in it, and since the HTPC is in the "watch" group and the HD Radio in the "listen" group, the receiver is able to use both of the inputs even though they are labeled the same even though there is a limited number of buttons on the remote. Basically you push the "listen" button on the remote a number of times until you get to the source you want to listen to on an OSD, and similarly with "watch".
While this works pretty well if: 1. You've got the receiver hooked up to an external display, and, 2. You've got that display turned on, there are limitations. Considering that the receiver only has a single line front panel display, if I want to just listen to my HD Radio and have no reason to turn on my display to do so then I have to blindly punch the "listen" button on the remote until I get to the right input. (The front panel display does not tell you what input you're up to until you stop punching the "listen" button, so it can be hit or miss. It is very intuitive if you've got a display hooked up, and on, but still...)

3. EDITED (see updated part at end): Interoperability between home theater components: There is a link going on between my Sony TV and this receiver, but it's not perfect. Case in point; when I turn the receiver on to watch a video source, it does not turn on the TV. (My 7 year old Sony BR player DOES turn on the 7 year old Sony TV through the HDMI link when I hit "play". Go figure.) But, if I've got the TV and receiver both on and turn off the TV, it will turn off the receiver (or turn it on if they were off) automatically even if I was, say, listening to music from my HTPC and just didn't need the TV on but still wanted the receiver to stay running. (Conversely, I had to hunt down and turn off the "auto off" function of the receiver because, even though I was actively viewing/listening to my HTPC output it apparently didn't register with the receiver and the 1050 would shut off a few minutes after my last input from the receiver remote.)
If the TV and receiver are both on and the receiver is turned off first it doesn't turn off the TV, it actually keeps the HDMI input last selected on the receiver running into the TV, and switches the TV speakers on. Because of this "feature", at one point I spent a while watching a movie on my HTPC through the TV speakers after the 1050 had done the auto-off thing I just described, thinking "geeze, the receiver sounds as crappy as the TV speakers!".
EDIT on interoperability: Well, all the stuff I said previously was technically true, but... it seems on further evaluation that the link is actually working pretty well. Here's what I was missing: The 1050 assumes that if you turn it off FROM the receiver then you either weren't using the TV or didn't want to effect the TV, and so leaves the TV on (or off, as the case may be). If you turn the TV on or off FROM the TV, the receiver will turn on (or off) as well via link. Here's the really cool part: When watching a video source through the TV, any volume input that would tend to change the TV volume actually changes the 1050's volume via the link. I really like this since we tend to keep the component section of our home theater blocked off with a rolling toy chest (darn toddlers!), and in the past I had to roll it out of the way every time we wanted to watch something that required line of sight to the receiver in order to control volume via the remote. Now we can leave the toy chest where it is: The cable TV remote, which we previously set to control the TV volume (but never did use, because with the old receiver there was no link with the TV), now controls the 1050's volume through the TV. Seems small, but pretty sweet in practice!

4. Input switching speed: This would be a real deal breaker for me, and I'm glad to report that, once up and running, the switch time between inputs is very reasonable. My big gripe is this: If I start up the 1050 to listen to a "listen" only source (e.g. the USB input) I get sound pretty quickly, but the TV spends several minutes reporting that there is no compatible (visual) input signal instead of showing the receiver's GUI. The "workaround" I've found is that I can briefly switch to a "watch" source and the TV will immediately recognize the input, then I go back to the "listen" only source and I can then see the OSD of the receiver.

5. Software update: WiFi is there, obviously, and it works, but it isn't a great priority for me (so far, since I already had an HTPC in my system that does far more than the Sony can). The one quirk I saw that I wanted to share was the update process: The 1050 almost immediately reports upon WiFi connection that there is an update available, but doesn't force you to start it. My advice is do it right away! I spent an hour or two messing around in the menus and setting up my system before I started the update. When it finishes (which takes a while), the 1050 resets to defaults and you have to start all over! Aggravating.

Going on a couple of months I'm pretty happy with the 1050 (aside from the USB thing). Hopefully they will come up with a firmware update to fix the "video source not supported" issue.

title: very disappointed
text:
I'm very disappointed with this product. It has a lot of complex logic including relays to turn audio and video on and off for various reasons. If I fast forward the DVR (cable box), the audio switches off. I can hear the relay click. The audio switches off automatically if no activity. Sometimes when I resume playing the DVR the audio doesn't come back on. The fact there should be audio is not sensed! I have to turn the Onkyo TX-SR608 off and back on before I can hear audio again.

Sometimes there's a lag before audio starts and I miss a few words of speech.

If I connect a PC via HDMI, the relay clicks on and off all the time. On with each Windows sound then off again. And I only hear part of each sound because of the sense delay. I bought a HDMI video card for the PC so I could pipe 5.1 sound from the PC through the Onkyo TX-SR608, but the relay problem was so bad I had to go back to VGA and normal sound output.

The remote controls several devices and it recognizes my DVR by default. Goody! But it also controls the DVR by default, too, and not the Onkyo TX-SR608. So if I have cable selected I must continually press the receiver button on the remote before the remote will send commands to the Onkyo TX-SR608.

I wish I hadn't bought this product. I'll go ahead and use it because I paid a lot and can tolerate the issues.

They could have done a better job with the equalizer such as given a graphical representation. It's very hard to keep jumping around on their cludgy menus trying to adjust things.

This is my second Onkyo TX-SR608. The first died. The second has the same audio problems as the first.

title: Has the potential to be great, but needs major redesign.....
text:
This radio/mp3 player has a lot of good things about it, but the bad things far outweigh the good.

I'll start with the good:

The speaker sound is great for a unit this small. FM reception is fantastic. The ability to play am/fm/sw/mp3 is great, as is the ability to record. The fact that it can take a memory card is what sets it apart from other units. The integration of the card port was the major selling point for me (32GB max).

Now the bad:

The charging/data cable connection is loose and unstable on the radio. AM reception is mediocre. The battery only lasts about 12 hours at moderate speaker volumes (longer if you use headphones, or low speaker volumes). There is no wall charger, rechargeable battery charges only through USB ports. You can't use the radio while it is charging, as the manual claims that doing so can damage your computer's USB ports. There is no practical way to fast forward or rewind mp3's. The touch sensors are not backlit, so adjusting the radio in dim light is impossible. The unit feels very light, plastic-y, and cheap. But, by far the worst thing is the touch sensor controls. The sensors are terrible. It often takes me 30 seconds to do a simple volume adjustment. You can hit a sensor 5 times and it might only register one touch (if you are lucky). Sometimes I will tap away at the "volume up" button and when I can finally get the touch sensors to respond the volume will actually turn down a notch. Or I'll hit "volume down" and when it finally responds the volume might actually increase a notch. Other times it might not respond at all. Often times it is so slow to respond that it will automatically flip itself out of volume adjustment mode while I am still trying to make volume adjustments. By the time it finally responds to my repeated taps it will often have returned to radio mode, which results in it unintentionally changing my radio station. You get the same inaccuracies and poor touch responses when you change radio stations, navigate mp3's, shuffle through the menu, etc.. The touch sensors are just an inaccurate, unresponsive mess that make this radio a total pain to operate. Sadly, it was completely unnecessary to design this unit with touch sensors. Had Degen simply kept all of the functions the same, but used regular old buttons instead of touch sensors, this radio would be lightyears better. These horrible touch sensors were not perfected at the time of manufacture, and they essentially ruin the radio if you want to make quick adjustments.

title: Design Idea is Great!!!  Quality control isn't reliable - save your money
text:
This is an ingenious little devise. It is the second one I have purchased. I WAS TOTALLY, deliriously, fiendishly HAPPY with the first one - a slightly shorter legged version - the MP3-D01. THAT ONE has TIGHT SPRINGS and THE LEGS STAY IN >any< POSITION I PUT THEM IN.

THE LEGS on this MP3-BK only stand VERTICALLY. If I position them at different angles the way I could with the MP3-D01 - they SPLAY OUT AND THE CAMERA LANDS FLAT on the base. Have tried and tried to make this one work. Alas. QUALITY CONTROL ISSUE. Not a concept or design issue nor too heavy a camera. I use a Nikon D5300 and that is NOT a heavy camera.

If I was so happy with the first one - WHY DID I BUY A SECOND ONE? Well... here's the reason - and the reason why this review is only 1 star instead of 5

The FIRST and ONLY time I took my first 'pocket tri' - the MP3-D01 off my camera (needed to switch out pocket for tall Tri) I reached up to place the 'pocket tri' on the dashboard of my truck AND the SCREW THAT HOLDS it TO my camera FELL OUT of the base AND ROLLED DOWN INSIDE MY Dashboard via a heating vent.

Hmmmmm. Garage Est Cost to find the screw? $275+ So -

When I got home I looked around for any kind of replacement screw that might work. Nada. So I looked online. A replacement screw costs over $6.00 plus shipping !!!!! !!!! !!! So I contacted Manfrotto. E-mail reply was fast but unfortunately there would be a 3-4 WEEK wait because they were out of replacement screws, and to call to place my order if I wanted one. When I called and explained what had happened, the customer support person was very kind and understanding and said (among other things) that THE SCREW ON THE MP3-D01 SHOULD NOT HAVE COME OFF.

Well, DUH!

So - I ordered TWO screws and then ordered this larger Pocket Tripod - the MP3-BK because I needed something right away. (the second screw was a 'just in case' spare)

And GUESS WHAT? The screw that holds the new MP-BK to my camera? IT FALLS OFF JUST LIKE THE FIRST ONE DID! It too has no retaining washer or gizmo or ANY MEANS OF HOLDING IT IN PLACE.

So - even tho this is a perfect - PERFECT CONCEPT... the manufacturing or the Qual Control - is a bust. There should be a split ring washer (OR WHATEVER) to keep the screw in place AND the springs on the legs SHOULD BE TIGHT enough to KEEP A CAMERA IN POSITION.

That's why I recommend you DO NOT BUY - UNTIL - Manfrotto has it's manufacturer fix these failures OR.... the next dashboard with a screw loose could be yours.

title: WARNING: faulty wiring!
text:
I spent 2 months trying to figure this thing out, using notations on the board itself and extrapolating from the 3-motor version. I even went so far as to document my findings. However, when put into practice, the wiring information didn't match the actual board wiring.

The biggest problem was that the manufacturers used a PC-style parallel port--in a non-standard way. The way they set it up, the data lines would control each of the motors, and the "enable motors" pin (#1) had was flipped opposite from the printer "/strobe." This meant bit-banging. Most computers today don't have a native parallel port, and USB parallel ports don't allow bit banging, at least the way needed for this board. (One really annoying thing about the USB parallel ports is that they put posts on the D-25 connector. The posts are supposed to be on the male connector. The female end is supposed to have screws. I had to tear apart the connector just to plug it in, only to discover that USB parallel doesn't allow bit-banging.)

To get around the nonstandard port definition, I bought an Atmel microcontroller board to wire the port by hand. It didn't work, and I know that I was programming the pins correctly, because I tested them.

I begin testing other pins and found that the manufacturer had reversed the counting order of D-25 from top 1-13/14-25 to bottom. So pin #1 was supposed to enable all motors, but it became #25. Pins #2 & 3 would control the first motor, this board responded to pins #24 and #23. Soon after discovering this flaw, I *literally* burned up the board. At this moment we're trying to air the house out.

The board is useless. I can't even work with the other motors without causing the servo controller to smoke.

Another possibility is that the port is wired correctly with the wrong interpretation of pin polarity. Pin #24 is the ground to pins #2 & 3. By pulling #24 high with +5V, the floating #2 & 3 could invert to ground. But since I got motor A to move, that would mean that pins #2 & 3 be enabled low not high, as the 3-motor documentation indicated.

All in all, the lack of external documentation and definitions and antiquated parallel port usage caused this entire project to fail. The manufacturers should have used a USB serial connection with a very modest command language. It's simple and straightforward. I know it sounds like a sob story, but I was building a system so that my son could construct a robotic arm. We're very disappointed and uncertain what to do now with 4 servo stepper motors and an Atmel microcontroller (along with all the hardware!).

title: Definitely the best bang for the buck vest, just be prepared to tweak it.
text:
[[VIDEOID:b139207062450071e5ba8613a443f50e]] Big complaint. The yellow springs (the lightest) were machined incorrectly. When I installed them the first spring went in fine. The 2nd spring when I was installing the barrel spacer that goes into the spring can use a little tap to remove and install, well.. the hole on the 2nd spring had a taper in it that wasn't noticed until I tapped the sleeve in and it was stuck. I had to cut the sleeve to get it out and put it back together with bits and pieces I had around the house. I didn't need the yellow springs so I threw them away, no big loss, but I had to order the correct pieces so I can put it back together. That out of the way. I recommend checking every screw and adding blue or red locktite where you can.

Once I got past the problems I got my Ronin M flying on a Flycam5000 with some added weight on the sled. The red springs are maxed out with my setup: Ronin M, Canon 5D MK IV, 10-20mm, Neucleus M motor 7" monitor on the sled and a some added weights from a cheap glidecam. It is insanely smoother than just the Ronin alone. I tried mounting the Ronin directly without the sled and it is doable but the spring was so stiff every shot required two passes of warp stabilizing so on the sled it lives!

Test video was shot at 60mm and no warp stabilization. I never shoot that tight on this rig, but I wanted to test the worst case. PS it won't be in focus all the time because I left it on manual since normally my focus motor but didn't have it hooked up.

title: Easy to install for someone who doesn't know how

I was going to wait until my tech savvy friend was available to help me install the cards but I was so delirious about having such a slow computer that I took it upon myself to do it. I had her on the phone. It made me feel better. It was moral support. And yes, she laughed as I worked and cheered and yayed myself on.

Three little screws on the bottom on the computer were easily removed but the cover was removed tenderly as I felt if I used my full force it would snap into a million pieces. It didn't. There are a couple of clips in the plastic that had to be maneuvered. Then there are metal clips on each side of the cards. I tried pushing on the cards to make them come up. Didn't work. I tried wiggling the cards. Didn't work. I then remembered the review I read when I bought the laptop. The metal clips pop out on either side. Viola! It worked. Old cards were removed and the new ones were placed into position. There is a little notch in the cards that will show you which way the cards need to be placed. Then metal clips were put back into position and cover was popped back on. I turned the lap top on and it was a smidge faster. As I used it, I noticed it getting faster and faster. I got happier and happier. As the final step, the screws for the cover were placed back in. It was a success. The computer in maxed out on memory something or other.

So to someone that knows enough about computers to know it's running way too slow but not enough to feel comfortable changing parts, this part is easy enough for you. Even if your friend is on the phone for moral support, you can do this. You can change this. I have faith in you. If I can do it, you can do it. And feel free to call for moral support.

title: Defective Product + Poor Customer Service
text:
The X-Grip has two knobs on it: a short screw knob on the upper arm to tighten the upper shoe, and a long screw knob underneath the base to secure the camera. The one on the base is supposed to have been drilled with a 1/4" hole in order for you to mount the X-Grip on a tripod.

However, their factory drilled the 1/4" tripod hole in the wrong knob: the shoe tightener. Since the screws are of different lengths, they're not interchangeable.

It makes the unit far less flexible. Picture this: I'm out in the field, shooting with the X-Grip, with my video monitor, XLR adapter box, and camera mounted to it. I take my freeform action shots. Now I want to change to a tripod shot. If the hole was drilled properly, I could just attach the X-Grip directly to the tripod. Without that 1/4" hole, now I have to detach everything from the X-grip and remount it on the tripod.

This is apparently an ongoing issue with this product, as more than one reviewer has mentioned it as far back as September. I hoped they would have fixed their stock. Obviously, it still has not been corrected.

Yes, I can return it. But if I replace it with another one, how do I know if THAT one won't have the same issue? All I want is that one part, properly manufactured.

I emailed Opteka several times in November, asking if they could just send me that single knob. I think it's ridiculous to have to spend all this money and effort on postage, packaging, and handling to exchange the unit, when all they would need to do is mail a $1 part with $1 of postage.

I received no response. I finally posted it on their Facebook page. I received a response from an M. Coleman. I emailed him that day, on Nov. 25, 2011. It's now mid-December, and I have received neither a part nor a reply.

So - that's two stars off for a defective product. Minus another two starts for horrible customer service. And I'm just going to return the unit and get my money back. Thanks for nothing, Opteka.

title: Good radio, but BEWARE! Dynamo eventually stops working!!!
text:
If you bought this radio because it has a dynamo that you can use in emergencies, you should be aware that, without periodic cranking, the internal rechargeable battery eventually goes completely dead. I checked my radio recently and found that all other options (A/C, replaceable batteries) are working fine, but no amount of cranking will charge the built-in battery.

I think this is true of rechargeable batteries in general - if you let them discharge too much eventually they can't be recharged, so I suppose that's what’s happening here.

I suppose that means that you might be able to keep the built-in battery alive by cranking it every month or so. But if you forget, eventually the internal rechargeable battery will go completely dead. I bought one of these for my girlfriend, and hers has gone dead too, so that's how I know it's not just I have a defective radio - I believe they all will eventually do that.

Otherwise it’s a great radio, I’ve had it playing in my kitchen using an AC adapter for years.

Magazine viewing - It's a joke; magazines do not fit on the screen and are not easily viewed.

Loading content on the CLOUD - If you a thinking you can load some of you videos onto the cloud and watch through the fire you are WRONG, only items purchased through amazon can be viewed through the cloud.

Disappointing Purchase - The Kindle Fire is pretty much just a front to purchase AMAZON Content on a rushed product that doesn't meet the hype. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND TO BUY

title: Buyer Beware!
text:
I purchased two of these Lenovo Yoga 720 Laptops; as joint anniversary gifts for my husband and I. They are very nice...light weight, and have many great features. However, one of the two has problems with the hinge; it frequently causes the screen to glitch and get streaks on it. Since I consider this to be a defective product, I decided to return it and get another one. When I went to the 'Return Policy' section, I discovered that the seller of this item has a very extensive and costly Return Policy... EVEN for defective items!!! Not only do they charge Return Shipping Fees, but a 15-50% Restocking Fee! The company also states that THEY decide whether the item is truly defective! This would mean I would loose HALF the original cost of the laptop!!! This is highly unacceptable and a very 'draconian' Return Policy!!!
While the Lenovo product itself is a very well made product, all items are susceptible to having defects. These defects are not the fault of the buyer; therefore, the buyer should NOT have to forfeit so much of the original cost! Because of this excessive and harsh Return Policy, I would not purchase any further items from this seller in the future. I will also do a much deeper research (beyond just researching the product specs and the customer reviews); my 'research' will also include taking a close look at the individual Seller!
We chose to keep the defective laptop and hope that we can get better help from Lenovo directly.

title: There are much better options in this price range.
text:
This thing cost $350 for 32GB storage, 4GB RAM and a low-end Celeron processor. It should have been closer to $100.

It's nice that it's a 2-in-1 (touch screens are always convenient), and it transitions well between the two modes, but that doesn't make up for the bad stuff.

32GB of storage just isn't enough for Windows 10. Looking at the storage analyzer, Windows reports that it's using 16.8GB of the available 28GB of storage. That leaves about 10GB for the user, which is ridiculous. It also means it's not possible to update Windows without a 16GB+ USB drive handy.

4GB of RAM is also not enough for Windows 10, even if you don't use Chrome. It's immediately used up by whatever you have open. It certainly doesn't help that Norton Antivirus comes preinstalled, which uses about 1.5GB of RAM continuously.

For such a low-powered machine, you'd think the battery life would at least be amazing, but it doesn't seem great. And the power plug is so loose, touching it makes it fall out, which makes charging it pretty difficult.

The design itself is all very weak plastic, which isn't good for the use-case of constantly folding the screen around. The laptop creaks every time you change the screen's angle, and the casing has already cracked in multiple places. Screws are also now falling out and the keyboard has started to fail.

The Asus Q405UA is about $400-$450, and it comes with an i5-8250U, 8GB RAM and 1TB HDD storage. The built-in hard drive is slow, but it can be replaced, or a SATA m.2 SSD can be added alongside it. It's also a 2-in-1, with a much better construction that doesn't creak or break.

title: The display is good, the stand is horrible, mine won't wake from sleep mode
text:
The picture was nice to me but I have not used/had any other 4K monitors to compare it to. Be aware that things will be tiny on a screen of this size at 4K but the clarity is extremely good as well. Viewing angle is pretty limited on this monitor. I do experience flickering and artifacts playing 1080p videos full screen (at full UHD resolution). I had the problem many have complained about with the monitor not waking from sleep. I tried two other cables, including the specific Accell model many have recommended. It did not help my problem. I contacted Samsung support and they weren't really helpful at all. They want me to pay to ship them their defective device and have no monitor for over a week so they can do whatever. I have had some very bad experiences in recent years with Samsung televisions and kitchen appliances. Their phones are the only thing I've had good luck with. I'd say this experience has just about completely turned me off to anything other than their phones. Obviously I could just not let it sleep but that's an unacceptable solution IMO. I'm returning this to Amazon and have already ordered an Asus 27" 1080p monitor. I will wait for UHD technology to mature and come down in price.

UPDATE: The picture quality of the non-4K ASUS monitor (VS278Q-P) that I ordered was so bad I decided to return it instead of this monitor. Despite Samsung's lacking customer service, poor design and/or quality control in that this monitor won't wake from DPMS sleep, and that the stand is completely non-adjustable and very flimsy, I am going to keep the monitor simply because the picture quality is very good. Hopefully either Samsung will right the wrong of their defective design some time soon or some other company will come out with a high-quality 4K display at a reasonable price soon. I will live with this one for now despite its shortcomings. If Samsung decides to fix the issue in a reasonable way (which could include cross-shipping with a hold on my card) I'll update the review appropriately. I do have to wonder how long the display will hold up since it never goes to sleep and I leave my computer on 24x7.

UPDATE 2:
I broke down and sent the unit to Samsung for service. They were kind enough to prepay UPS shipping. The return only cost me packaging by UPS. Samsung insisted I NOT ship it back in the original package. They returned it five days later, stating they replaced the main board. It has the exact same behavior as before. It goes to sleep and will not wake. Other monitors do not do this on this same machine (which runs Linux and is driving the display over DisplayPort) and the same monitor has the same behavior attached to my laptop running Windows 7. I guess I will just live with the power management disabled. I'm very disappointed in that.

Oh, and I eliminated the artifacts I was having by switching to compiz as my window manager (Linux-specific). I won't go into the details here since it was the video card and not the monitor, but be aware the monitor has no issue with artifacts.

So I will summarize once more. The display is very good IMO, but I have no other 4k experience to compare it to. The monitor case itself is made fine but the stand is horrible and flimsy and completely non-adjustable. The lack of VESA mount compatibility is disappointing. It will not wake when put to sleep (power management, AKA DPMS) and Samsung will not even acknowledge the problem despite all the similar feedback here on Amazon. Despite all its shortcomings I will keep it for now since I know of no other 4K monitor in the price range that's any better.

title: You need to know, it’s not as great as it seems on paper.
text:
I wanted to love the Authentrend ATKey.Card, and I was extremely excited when I found it and was reading about what it is supposed to do.

The problem is, it’s doesn’t really do it quickly or reliably. In fact, the thing was so frustrating to try to use, I had to send it back before I gave in to my urge to snap it in half and set it on fire.

If you buy this device, be prepared to play with it and try to figure out how it works through trial and error, because instructions are not easy to understand, and it just does not explain everything about the card.

I have a college degree in computers and security, so I did eventually figure out exactly how everything works, but I know that just means a lot of people never will.

So after a lot of fiddling and feeling my way around the thing, I came to the conclusion that it’s a great idea, it’s just very poorly executed.

First of all, I was very disappointed to find out that it will not work with windows hello without downloading and installing a software that runs as a service, taking up system resources. If you can live with that, you’re still not going to like how slow it is to use to log into windows. I’ll tell you how the process goes.

You have to turn the card on! That’s right, you have to push the power button because it shuts off automatically after 1 minute, even if it’s plugged into a USB power source. It will stay on if it’s plugged into a computer USB, but it’s not sleek at all, and the USB connector is one of those super space saving half sized plugs that are super flimsy. Besides, if you’re going to use USB you can buy fingerprint readers for $23 on here that work much faster, and are always on, and don’t require any software.

For me, Bluetooth was ALL of the appeal. I loved the idea of logging into windows with just my fingerprint via Bluetooth, because that would allow me to have it where I sit instead of on the computer, without running a wire. It’s really too bad it takes so long, a USB fingerprint reader for $25 is ready before windows finishes loading the sign in screen and logs you in the moment your fingertip hits the sensor (unless it’s dirty or something lol)

It almost seems like this card was meant primarily for people who go through NFC doors a lot, because it certainly seems the Bluetooth takes a backseat to the cards attempts to use NFC first, no matter what. I don’t know how many times I turned the card on and Bluetooth wouldn’t connect until it had gone through the process of searching for NFC devices first. It could be a problem with the software you have to install, or it might be a problem with windows. Then again it could be a design flaw, or who knows, maybe even designed that way intentionally.

So, if all does well, you can log into windows using hello fingerprint in maybe 1 minute after you turn the card on. You better hope it doesn’t fail though, 2 failed fingerprint readings and the thing has to reconnect to Bluetooth, and it might fail doing that and then you’ll have to press and hold the power button to force it to shut off.. so yea, far too often you end up taking longer to sign in than if you’d just typed your password or PIN. Not cool.

The NFC works fast, once you turn the card on, you can immediately touch with your fingerprint to enable the door key mode. I didn’t have a door to test it on, so I can’t speak to that, but it should work pretty quick.

So unless you have an over abundance of both patience and laziness, don’t buy it. Or if you use a lot of NFC doors and stuff, maybe get it, but I can’t imagine a better solution doesn’t exist.

For windows logins just get a cheap USB fingerprint reader. Have a separate security key for online accounts, and a nfc card for doors. Trying to combine them all looks great on paper, but I haven’t found a company that actually has done it right yet.

title: Very nice and inexpensive wireless video connection!
text:
I used this inexpensive item to wirelessly connect my Esky one-button camera to my Esky 4.3 inch foldable TFT LCD monitor. I installed the camera on the lower edge of the front bumper of my new Tesla model S and pointed the camera downward to enable it to view the concrete barrier that separates nose-to-nose parking slots in many shopping mall parking lots. These low-height concrete barriers are not detectable by the factory installed front sensors in the Tesla. I got tired having my wife get out of our car to indicate how close I was to the barrier while parking. Corvette and other sports car owners probably have the same problem of their low-bottom car potentially striking one of these barriers during nose-in parking.

I did not want to hard-wire my front bumper mounted camera to the 4.3-inch LCD monitor I have positioned just below the 17-inch LCD screen in my Tesla. The wiring route would be tedious for me and I didn't want to possibly interfere with the side air bag mounted in the A pillar. So, before I permanently installed this wireless connection I bench tested it. I compared the image displayed on the monitor when I connected the camera to the monitor with the 18-ft video cable that came with the monitor, with the image displayed when I replaced the video cable with the wireless transmitter-receiver. Both images were excellent for my needs; I was unable to see any difference, hard-wired vs. wireless.

The entire system cost me much less than $100 and the overall image performance of my concrete barrier-detecting camera is outstanding.

title: Great picture with no problems.
