title: Small design flaws make this case less than ideal
text:
I bought this case along with another gray kwmobile case for my Kobo Libra h2o. There weren't really any reviews on either case, so it was hard to decide which one was the best choice, so I just got both to compare. Ultimately, this case has quite a few design flaws that make it less than stellar, and I am going to be returning it.

Pros:

- This case is a really nice color, and that alone is what sold me on it in the first place. So kudos for a lovely color!

- The case does magnetize nicely over the cover of the e-reader and it does put the Kobo to sleep.

- There is a single hand strap that you can use to help carry your Kobo more securely

- The Kobo secures into the case by snapping into a black, plastic case that is embedded within the fabric cover. I did appreciate this design aspect, especially the fact that it allowed the white border of the Kobo to still be visible. The gray case I purchased surrounds the Kobo with a gray frame, so that was a bit of a downside, but this case lets you still see the color of your Kobo so if that is important to you this could be a good case for you.

- This case does let you fold it around to act as a stand for your Kobo. It took looking at the pictures online to figure out how to do it properly, but it did work!

Cons:

- The flap of this case flips up along the top of the Kobo rather than along the side. I personally prefer to have a case that flips open like a book, rather than flipping up and around.

- While this case does magnetize and close over the front of the Kobo, the flap does not magnetize to stay open. This was a huge downside to me. As I carried the Kobo in this case, the flap was constantly moving around, and yes there is a hand strap to help secure the case in your hand, but I really would have preferred to have the case magnetize both open and shut. Before receiving the gray case that I ended up keeping, I spent time thinking about how I would alter this case with magnets or other elastic so that the flap would stay open and secured. So if that's something you are wanting, this is not the case for you.

- Although the description of the item states that there are 2 elastic straps, one for your hand and one to keep the case securely closed, there is only the hand strap. No strap to keep the case closed over your Kobo. The case does magnetize closed, but it bothered me that it advertised 2 straps, but in reality there were not. This was something that had sold me on the case initially, so the fact it was falsely advertised was a huge downside.

While this case does have it's pros, the cons definitely overrode them for me so I am returning it. For the same price, you can get the gray kwmobile Kobo Libra h2o case, and it's design is FAR superior to this one. I suggest going with that case instead!

title: An exercise in frusteration
text:
I bought two of the DataComm Electronics 45-0051-WH to use in my remodeled bedroom. Hiding the wires and adding an outlet behind the wall mounted tv was just as important as having the options to run data and video cables from below to behind said tv.
Reading the description and studying the photos supplied I pulled the trigger and spend close to $60 bucks on two of them. One below and one above.
They arrived in good order, packaged well and made of a sturdy plastic that felt good in the hand. The old work clips on the back for securing the box are fairly long and metal, nice touch since I am going through lath and plaster as well as a 3/8 inch wainscot.
It came supplied with an outlet suitable for a 15 amp circuit only. The outlet did not have screw terminals but had push in type terminals sized for 14 gauge wire only.

For the above I give the box 4 stars. I subtracted one for the quality of the outlet. Push in terminals are horrible for positive and stout electrical connections.

Now the profound frustration starts when I start the installation.
I intended to add speaker terminal to this box. This is when I discovered everything that has to do with this box is proprietary.
What does this mean?
well, nothing off the shelf will fit the cut outs in this box. The areas for cables, whether they be speaker wires, HDMI cables or optical cables all have to use the supplied cover. Nothing else will fit. So trying to use an off the shelf HDMI panel or speaker terminals (like I show in the photo) will only frustrate you when you try to place your connectors within the areas intended.
The holes for mounting the plates are not the industry standard for anything made for standard boxes (low voltage boxes or outlet boxes)
I cut out the back with an oscillating tool and mounted mine there.
Next frustration is the supplied outlet and box.
wow, what a cluster $%^&.
The supplied box is mounted to the media box from the rear!
First you run your electric wire through the back of the box, which by the way is a simple hole once you punch out the tab. No provision for a tension tab or clamp to hold the wire from falling back through and loosing it in the wall.
Code says boxes like this are ok however the wire needs to be secured within 12 inches of the box or the box must have a means of holding the wire.
Since this is an old work box, meaning a box intended to be used in a wall that already finished there should be provisions for securing the electrical wire.
Now, once you run the wire through the box and wire your receptacle you then mount the receptacle to the box. Then screw the box to the media box from the rear with the supplied 4 screws.
If at any time you want to access this receptacle in the future you have to remove the entire media box.
Again, a proprietary system, no other way of doing it. Something happens there is no off the shelf solution.
FYI: I did not use the supplied electrical outlet. I used a surge protected outlet. Luckily it was square so it fit - bonus.

Next frustration.
You have to use the supplied cable and keystone covers. Again, they are a propriety design.
I intended on adding my speaker block in one of the openings but the industry standard block I had will not fit the openings.

Another frustration
the outlet will only mount on the left as shown in the pics. It's at a slight angle.
The distance between the molded in trim and the outlet box is only about 1/2 to 5/8 inch.
As I mentioned earlier I am going though lath and plaster as well as 3/8 inch wainscot. no way was this going to fit using the supplied template. My wall was simply to thick to fit between the face of the media box and the outlet box.
I had to use my handy dandy oscillating tool to to carve out an extreme bevel inside my wall leaving only my wainscot as a mounting surface.

The photo's in the description of this media panel show an HDMI cable attached to "something" on the right side. I included this photo in my review.
I assumed... I know, I know...
I assumed this "accessory" area could be used as a mounting point for a media panel for this such as HDMI, Optical connection, etc. After all, the photo shows "something" there. Misleading if you ask me.
Nope. It's simply a large box. Much larger than the other openings so no dice.

Frustration point.
The supplied keystove cover, not only is it proprietary (no off the shelf keystone cover will fit) but it has six spaces for keystones. Great!
What's frustrating is there is no supplied blank inserts in case you don't fill all six.
ok, this is a small annoyance but it does compound the annoyed feeling I have already.

Hints:
Pay very close attention to the size of the completed box. You may not have enough room to install the large "accessory" box if your not careful.
I recommend finding your studs and cutting an outlet size hole in the middle of the area where you intend on installing this. the measure to each stud and allow for enough room on either side for the protrusions.
ie: the outlet box on the left and the "accessory" box on the right.

Loose 2 stars for annoying and frustrating me.
I despise propriety things.

title: Cloud interface is terrible, unable to adjust view, no search.
text:
It was easy to setup and share across all my devices. However, I really hate the interface. It's horrible. It doesn't act like a traditional file folder, like a plugged-in harddrive or Dropbox does. I also had trouble trying to get iTunes to use this for the file source.
In the end, I can only really use this as a backup system, which is a bit disappointing considering I would have been better off forgoing the cloud option and going for a plugged in external HD or a paid subscription to Dropbox in order to navigate more easily.

---------------------------
Update: I am downgrading this rating to 1-star. I do NOT recommend buying this if you ever plan to use this for, even as a backup.

Now I have to parse through all the files and figure out how to get them over individually. title: Awesome for geocaching!!!
text:
After switching from the eTrex Venture HC to a paperless Delorme, I wasn't real satisfied. The Delorme was easy to use, but freezes up constantly. So, when I heard that Garmin was redoing the eTrex line, I got excited and kept watching for the official release.

I've been using the new eTrex 30 for about a month for geocaching. I love that it feels just like my old one. The interface is very similar making using this unit straight out of the box a dream come true! I love how the new units have room for a micro SD card so you can expand the memory. Being able to do a pocket query instead of having to load all of your caches one by one is a sweet improvement as well. The addition of being able to read the cache description, hints, and the last several logs. The number seems to be adjusted by length of log entries so it varies on how many logs you get--minimum so far is 5.

The unit feels solid. Garmin fixed the "rubber ring" issue of the old eTrex units and made the outside casing of plastic. They did give it the classic look though by modeling the plastic to look like the old rubber rings. Nice!

The real compass is a sweet upgrade. Unlike many hand-held GPS units, the compass would stop moving when you did. The new eTrex line has a true compass that points the direction you need to go--even if you stop moving.

The only downside to this machine I have seen so far in my caching excursions is that the compass will freeze when the batteries get low. The battery indicator isn't really great. The unit will let you know when your batteries are low by the freezing of your compass. I had that happen yesterday and popped in a fresh set of rechargeables. That fixed it, and I proceeded to find a few more caches before heading home.

Overall, I am pleased to be using an eTrex again. See you on the caching trail!

title: Serious case of buyer's remorse
text: I was initially happy with this purchase, which replaced a VSX-1021. I recently upgraded to a 4K OLED set and needed something to handle the HDMI 2.0/HDCP 2.2 requirements. I also have an Epson 5020UB projector which is not terribly ancient (5 years old), and expected to be able to use it with this receiver as well. However, thus far, in every configuration I've tried, I've had zero luck getting the receiver to connect to the projector via HDMI. I have tried connecting it on both MAIN and SUB HDMI ports, and switched the TV and Projector cables between MAIN and SUB. I also connected the projector only to MAIN and completely disconnected the TV. The input device I am testing against is a gen 1 Xbox One which is coming in on a non-HDCP 2.2 port (HDMI 5) and the Xbox output is set to 1080p with standard 24 bit color space. The receiver is set for no upscaling of 1080p to 4K and CEC and ARC are both disabled. And yet, nothing. Just a "No signal" message on the projector. But the projector works with the same cable (a costly Monoprice active one) directly connected to the Xbox One as well as an Apple TV that I tested it with, so it's not having issues with other 1080p HDMI sources. Pioneer tech support thus far has been useless. Unfortunately, I received this item shortly before going on vacation and my return window closed before I discovered this, because otherwise it would be going back in the box. I am hoping either Pioneer or Epson tech support can resolve this but I don't have a good feeling about it based on my experience to date.

title: 2008 toyota tundra double cab
text:
Installed on 2008 toyota tundra.
These trucks are pre wired.
There is a white plug on the left when u drop the overhead console. The plug has 4 wires u need to splice into: green, red, white, black/white striped. Plug wires: Green is 12volts when truck is in reverse, black/white striped wire is ground, red brings power to plug in rear of truck, black is negative video, white is positive video.

Splice the positive red wire from the mirror display into the green and red wires on the plug.

Splice negative black wire from mirror display to black/white striped wire on plug.

Strip back the yellow rca plug and connect the yellow wire to the white wire on the plug.

In the rear of the truck (under tail gate behind bumper towards passenger side) there is another plug. There is a red, black, another black and white (these 2 are right next to each other).
Red is bringing power from the front as per earlier. So, red is spliced to camera positive wire.
The white and black paired adjacent to each other are positive and negative video. So, strip back the yellow rca and splice the yellow wire to the white wire. Then, attach the black negative wire from the camera to the black negative video. Finally, the negative camera wire and negative video wire must be grounded to the frame of the truck (**important**).

Hope this helps.

title: Longer than expected
text:
Overall I'm happy with this purchase. Be warned though, this is made to be mounted on a high ceiling. I wanted to mount this in my basement gym and be able to rotate it for when I'm doing laundry, etc. However, my basement ceiling is a low 7-8'. This mount has a ~4ft tube with another ~3ft telescoping shaft on the inside. The bracket that mounts to the TV only mounts to the smaller inside tube so the highest you can mount the center line of the TV is a good 4-5ft from the ceiling. I ended up tossing out the inside tube and modifying the bracket to fit on the larger tube which also required drilling new holes on the larger tube and cutting off the a few inches of excess tubing.

Also, the top mount is a hole with a plastic bushing. The large tube has a flange that sits in the hole which is what allows it to pivot 360 degrees. With this design however, the tube will never sit vertical, the weight of the TV tilts the tube giving a ~15deg angle at the minimum, which makes the variable tilt start at that angle and go further - don't expect a completely vertical viewing angle.

Again, I don't have any regrets as this is the only mount I found with a full 360 degree rotation and the cost was very reasonable.

P.S. I mounted this with a 40" TV.

title: Product Description Not Accurate - Short Cable Length Required
text: Most of you should have no challenge with this DMI splitter, however some of you will experience challenges with it and here is a short list of the challenges that affected us. Product description states up to 1440p which is not accurate resolutions above 1080p cause device to fail, and lights to either blink or go off. Device maximum resolution is 1920x1080 according to manual, and 1900x1200 according to box, so there is a lot of confusion around this products capabilities.  Also, the power adapters at 9.5v not 5v so if you plan to use 5v distributors this won't work.  Finally, and most importantly, this splitter is limited to output cable lengths of 10 meters, which is very short. Most 8 port distribution environments will have cables beyond that length, and this is the ONLY splitter we have ever bought that has had this limitation and more importantly, actually failed to work on cables over 50 ft. Once any single cable which exceeds that length, whether it is directional, bi-directional or has a built in repeater, this device fails on all outputs, and the lights blink erratically until the long cable is unplugged.  We gave it a lower rating simply because a cable length restriction is critical in most 1x8 environments and a) the manufacturer failed to place this limitation in their description, and b) every other splitter we have used has had no cable length restrictions.

title: GREAT! Super easy setup for Windows 7 Home Premium 64 bit.
text:
Great product! Would definitely recommend and purchase again!

I chose this product to convert and save my old VHS movies because it works on Windows 7 Home Premium 64 bit. Not all of them do. Many of the lower priced conversion products do not.

Setup was a breeze for this non-techie. NOTE: Make sure your connections are where they should be. I had so many color coded outlets on my VCR I initially plugged them into the wrong place and got a NO SIGNAL message. So I tried again - you'll know you've got it right when you hear the feedback and see the picture appear on the screen.

Just plug in the red, yellow and white connectors to your VCR and plug the other end to your USB port.
(I also ran a coaxial cable to plug my old Samsung VCR player into my old Toshiba TV).
Then insert the CD to install the drivers, unplug the device, and then install the software.
Screen pops up to name my movie and we're off!

I have a dozen or so VHS tapes and will update with the quality of the finished product.

Update: Love it! I have now completed converting 7 tapes and couldn't be more pleased. It prompts you to edit if you want - I use Windows Movie Maker - and from there I am able to easily split the sections on the some greater than 2 hour tapes. I find the quality of the finished product far above my expectations - even the stills I have captured and kept as photos are great considering they are more that 20 years old.

Important Update after a week: It has been problematic . . . I was forced to go to the Elgato site and update my drivers after making the first half dozen conversions??? Then it refused to pick up the first few minutes of my video, but after fooling around for a while I got that to work too. So its not perfect - and could be extremely frustrating for a tech novice.

There are all sorts of issues with this thing. The laser mouse has trouble tracking on most surfaces. The scroll wheel doesn't scroll, but it does work as a button. If you press the mute button on the keyboard, it will become stuck down. It did this right out of the box. The keyboard will occasionally refuse to let you capitalize letters - When you depress the shift key, certain letters will not work. They'll work just fine as soon as shift is released. Other letters will work just fine. Which letters become nonfunctional seems to change with every shift.

I thought it might be a missing driver, but no. There's no software for this marvel, just a program that tells you to turn your keyboard off and on again. (?!)

The items feel incredibly light and cheaply made. They are all plastic, and there are places where you can see light through the keyboard. The battery door on the mouse is difficult to get off.

It's bizarre. It's baffling. It's totally unacceptable, and it's a pollution to Logitech's brand.

Let me be clear here: DO. NOT. BUY.

title: DO NOT BELIEVE CLAIMED "INSURANCE"!!
text:
Tripp-llte prominently features "$50,000 Ultimate Lifetime Insurance - covers connected equipment against direct surge damage, including lightning!" with this item.

I had a lightning event involving both telephone and power line surges, with significant damage to pieces equipment connected ONLY to these ISOTEL protectors. I also had other damaged equipment on isotel protectors but also connected to ethernet, etc.

To claim the "insurance" I was asked to return the units, with diagrams of all connected equipment.

Tripplite DENIED all claims, SOLELY on the basis that they said they found no evidence of a surge INSIDE the protectors. Tripplite's representative also claimed there are "other pathways" and "ground strikes" which cause damage which is not covered.

BUT the terms of the "insurance" are online at:

[...]

and they state that equipment properly connected to the isolator IS covered, say nothing about requiring internal evidence of isolator damage, and do not assert pseudoscienctific exemptions to coverage.

1) I clearly did have significant damage to pieces equipment connected ONLY to these ISOTEL protectors.
2) Assertions of "other pathways" and "ground strikes" which cause damage which is not covered are pseudoscience when there are no other connections, and are contrary to the published terms.
3) No examination of a lightning protector can prove that no surge has passed through it; peaks and damage do not necessarily occur at the protector; this requirement is ALSO contrary to the published terms.

No protector can prevent all damage - that's the reason for the insurance, and the reason it is advertised -- but you do have to have some trust in the insurer.

My experience with Tripplite was extraordinarily distasteful. I will no longer trust, purchase or recommend their products.

title: DO NOT PURCHASE THIS PROJECTOR - FIND AND ALTERNATIVE - UNLESS YOU HAVE MONEY TO BURN!
text:
DO NOT PURCHASE THIS PROJECTOR ( Panasonic PTAE8000U 1080p Full HD Projector) - for long term use. The specific issue is with the main board (the one with the CPU). The main board appears to be a weakness with moderate use over a period of time and when it fails - PANASONIC DOES NOT OFFER A REPLACEMENT BOARD. Yep, you heard right. They expect for you to come out of pocket to purchase or a $3000.00 projector that the manufacturer does not service !! I know, right ?! Check on Ebay and you will find tons of these Panasonic PTAE8000U units for sale for "parts only" for pennies on the dollar . The common denominator seems to be (you guessed it) - they all have a bad main circuit board).

I purchased the projector from Amazon in December of 2013 for home theater use the unit had less than 3700 total hours on
the projector with approximately 3400 hours on first bulb and 300 hours on the second (replacement bulb. So, moderate use - mostly home theater stuff with the occasional gaming session mixed in. Other than the recommended filter cleans (it has like 4 filters ) and the expected replacement of the original bulb - no issues. Until a couple of weeks ago - when while watching a movie then projector cut off and went into "Safe Mode". I had a Projector come out and ultimately take it with him for further diagnostic. I got a call last week that the main board was fried. After more than a week of looking the tech calls me back and confirms that the replacement board is not available though the manufacturer, refurbished, aftermarket - nowhere and nothing! I did some checking myself (trust , but verify - for this kind of money - am I right? and confirmed that no reputable (or non reputable for that matter) source supplies a replacement main board. I now have a $ 3K projector (with an almost new $300.00 replacement bulb in it) that is worthless as anything other than a boat anchor. So , to summarize - unless you have money to burn, Find an alternative brand at this price point, with these features - DO NOT purchase this projector.

title: Died after 13 months
text:
There were certain features I really liked about this watch when I first started using it. It did a pretty good job of tracking swim laps for me. The touch screen was never very responsive. I felt like I had to push hard and hold for a bit many times to get the touch screen action to work.
My wife bought this for me for Christmas 2016. As of January 2018 (only ~13+ months later), the watch is COMPLETELY dead. It started with a couple of the firmware updates. The screen displayed a bunch of data like core operating voltage, watch temperature, etc. I.e. a list of a bunch of firmware data -- not the normal interface. Then, I had a couple times (for 24+ hours each time) where the watch would not respond to ANY touch screen inputs at all. Only the two side buttons. Then charged it for several hours, then it would come back. Then more buggy things started happening, like saving a bike ride put the watch into a loop of "saving this event" on the screen that could not be stopped / interrupted. Finally the battery died and after charging it, it came back.

Then about 3 weeks ago, I was swimming with it, the battery was fully charged the night before the swim. About 10 minutes into my swim, the face went completely black. It has not come back since then.

Putting it on the charger, once in a while, I can get the "Garmin" logo to show up in the middle of the screen, followed by a charging status saying the battery is at "0%". I would leave it on the charger for multiple hours, then take it off, and the screen would go completely black again. Tried to reset it with holding the power button for 15+ seconds multiple times.

Called Garmin support. After the rep tried everything, my options were to a) send it in for repair for $99 -- a NEW one on Amazon is $107 right now -- or b) send it in for 20% off Garmin MSRP price for a new Garmin device. Ugh. Really! I only get 13 months for this expensive Garmin watch!?!? Very disappointed. I have owned 8 Garmin devices over the past ~12 years. This was the worst device of any. Hope this helps you decide.

I'm attaching a picture that shows the most amount of life I'm able to get out of it now while it's attached to the Garmin cradle that came with it, attached to my Mac's USB port. :(

The positives are the tablets seem to be fairly durable with the foam padding and the battery life is good. Aside from the complaints above, there are a ton of apps to choose from. I added 32 gig SD cards to both of our tablets and loaded them with games. Once the games start, they are fairly easy for the kids to understand (mine are two and five).

From what I found out by comparing kid tablets, I still think theses offer more bang for the buck, because as my kids grow, we can alter these tablets to grow with them.

title: Expectations too high?
text:
I am a casual photographer, who for the past several years has shot with a Nikon D300 that I purchased primarily for underwater photography. However, my Nikon gets a lot more use above-water now that diving has taken a back seat to raising our son. :)

Obviously, you can't compare the two cameras. Nevertheless, I can't HELP but do so...
1) I found it annoying to look through a viewfinder only to see a "miniature" LCD rendition. "EVF" or "Electronic Viewfinder" may be handy to see how settings will impact the picture (I assume it did this but can't recall now), but I found it more of a step down from the D-SLR viewfinder. I think I don't like having the light from the EFV shining in my eye, plus it feels like I am watching t.v. when I am taking a picture.

2) I did not find the focus to be that great, indoors. I do a lot of picture taking indoors and I had hoped that the low light abilities of this camera/lens would not disappoint. But, it disappointed me. I found that putting it in Auto or Ai mode didn't really let me take decent pictures in ordinary room lighting. Perhaps if I upped the ISO manually it would have been fine, but I bought the camera primarily for my wife, and I was hoping for a point and shoot experience with a terrific zoom lens that would let her take shots that werent blurry when she was in the house, without having to use the flash.

3) I probably expected way too much -- and with the pop-up flash, I didn't have any complaints with the photo quality. I just hate to shoot with a flash because I don't like people shooting flashes at me.

4) I hated the fact that when you are "in between" shots, and just holding the camera, you risk having your fingers pinched quite badly when the camera goes to sleep and the lens retracts. You really do have to be careful not to have the barrel of the lens in contact with your skin at all times, even when you aren't manipulating the lens yourself.

5) I found that I missed not having a zoom ring.

So, basically, I gave the camera very little chance. It did not impress me "out of the box" and it may be unfair to give the camera only 3 stars. However, I thought it should be able to take more reliable indoor pictures without a flash and, generally speaking, I did not feel like I was getting sharp pictures, and I decided to try the Canon Ti4 instead. I know it won't shoot like my Nikon, but the camera is for my wife, and I have a feeling that she will get much better pictures out of the DLSR then she could get out of the Lumix.

Having given the camera very little chance, I can't really answer many questions about it. I did not try the software that came with it, I did not shoot any video with it. I did very little flash photography with it, though perhaps most of my pictures ought to have used a flash. I found it very difficult to acquire fast focus in low light and got lots of blurry pictures or missed picture taking opportunities, something that I just didn't expect and something I can't really tolerate after shooting with a different class of camera.

title: Disapointing... terrible battery life.
text:
Wanted to love these and had big hopes for them. The initial perception of headphone system was wonderful at first but within a week of use the inherent flaws began to emerge. The functionality would have been perfect for my aging parents with onset hearing issues but soon the shortcomings of the product outweighed their usefulness.

Please read on.

The good:
• Super easy hook up. Two plugs into your TV and you're off an running. Couldn't ask for a simpler installation.
• They connect automatically within seconds of turning on the headphones. Most of the time I'll say... 2-3 issues first month which I haven't really identified the root cause of. Unplugging the transmitter (pwr) and plugging back in resolved the issue.
• My father wanted the full headphone version and he finds this comfortable. We'll see how that is come summertime (I'm thinking hot/sweaty). Mother opted for the in-ear design (see other review).
• Aesthetically pleasing design. They look nice.
• Sound quality is decent, not studio quality but good for their intended use, i.e. TV or computer. I have found no audible latency in the TV setup. Please, read on...

Negatives:
• While a nice design the materials are not made for long term durability. Definitely manufactured for cost not quality. I've already noted, within a few weeks of use, material separation at the ear cups.
• The BATTERY LIFE IS TERRIBLE. 40 hrs is a complete fabrication under normal use. At a full charge, within 3-4 hrs of use (50-60% volume) you will begin to have one of the ear pieces (speaker) die out rapidly and lose volume leaving only audible sound to one ear piece. The other ear piece soon follows suit dying out shortly thereafter. Manufacture claims the use of lithium ion batteries however, this electronic characteristic is NOT indicative of Li-Ion battery use. Hmm...
• Controls are odd and cumbersome. Better tactile feel is needed on the buttons. Hard for my parents, and myself, to find and use controls by touch alone. Also, the volume up/down require multiple presses to adjust, unlike any typical volume control found on 99.9% of all AV equipment/remotes. Granted this product's control function is a learned behavior, it could have been easily averted in design.
• No USB power supply provided?!? You'll literally need two separate USB power ports, one at the TV/Computer (transmitter) and another located where you'll charge the headphones. If you don't have a USB port on your TV and another at your charging location, headphones, you're put in an awkward situation of having to buy this additional equipment and at least one USB cord. At the time of this review, this requirement is NOT stated anywhere.

Bottom Line:
Personally I like to have/use a product for a few weeks before reviewing and I should have returned the headphone system but missed the return window. While a great idea, and potentially great functionally, just poor execution. Likely driven by sourcing through the cheapest overseas vendor and materials available.

For the interim, this headphone will provide my parents some relief and comfort until a better quality product can be found. And so, we'll continue to look for a better quality product.

Unfortunately, in the current state of functionally and performance I cannot recommend this product.

title: Not amazing, but decent
text:
After nearly a month of delays, I finally got the Lighted Kindle Cover. I was so happy with the new Kindle design and was hoping the Kindle cover would be just as big of a step forward.

First thoughts:

- Cheap materials. Apple has probably spoiled me, but the cover is made with a low-quality, flimsy leather material with a soft, felt-like inside. The part holding the Kindle is a sturdy, yet rubbery plastic that simply feels cheap.

- Better design. Amazon has definitely improved the design, both in terms of anchoring the device and the plastic arm providing light. It is sturdy and moves easily, unlike the flimsy arm of the previous generation.

- But still not 100%. For $60, I expect a high-quality product that does not detract from the device itself. The case more than doubles the thickness of the Kindle. The leather on the back of the cover is totally unnecessary and probably a waste of space. The lack of a strap to hold the cover--open or closed--is concerning. Because of excess front cover material that wraps from the back of the device to the front, the front cover is able to wiggle and twist on top of the device when closed. That would not be a problem if there were a strap to hold the cover closed, but I worry about putting this into a large space in a backpack.

All in all, I think this is the best cover for Kindles yet, but I think having more third party manufacturers would be good for increasing the quality of accessories through increased competition.

You don't want to take a whole entire minute to screw the camera on, take a photo, then take another AGONIZING minute to unscrew the camera from the tripod and get on your way. What's the point of having a mobile tripod if you can't take photos 'on the go'?! If you take into account how long it takes to set up the tripod, you would be losing at least 2-3min every time you want to take a photo. Then another 2-3 to put it away. How are you suppose to take any candid shots? Let alone have people wait to pose for a picture.

This camera is not meant to be an 'on-the-go' tripod. I was looking for something like my last one that took 20secs or less to set up. I hate to stop other people to take my photos for me. Their hands shake, and they don't know anything about angles, cropping, or framing. Especially when your photos are taken during low-light situations or golden hour, you want absolute certainty that your photo will come out clear. There's really nothing that can match the quality of the pen, pressure sensitivity, etc. of a Wacom, so anyone doing professional image manipulation or digital illustration really has little choice but to get a Wacom. That said, the firmware is a mess. Settings don't stay set when you switch between different monitor settings and sometimes after the tablet has been sleeping, so I'm constantly re-entering settings over and over again. A huge annoyance and hit to productivity. You also have to open an entirely different piece of software just to monitor your battery levels, because the battery monitor on the firmware doesn't work, and the settings don't contain any information about battery level, either. On top of all of that, their technical assistance reps are awful. Like other reviewers, I've also noticed that the mini USB port is shoddy and could pose a potential problem later with functioning of the unit. It's a shame; I used to use a Wacom in the early 00s regularly, and back then, Wacom was known for the best quality. Sad to see the brand's reputation degrading because of easily fixable issues and bad customer service.

So if you really don't need the high-end functions of the Wacom such as the extra pressure sensitivity, tilt, and ability to customize the interface controls, definitely go with a cheaper competitor.

title: Too early to buy 1440p 240hz? Maybe
text:
I'm a competitive Overwatch player who plays on the Varsity Team for my university as well as a photographer/ videographer for Monster Energy. I have a powerful desktop computer for editing 4K video: i7-8700K, 2080Ti FTW3, and 64GB Ram @3200mhz, so I did not want to settle for 1080p resolution for gaming. While 144hz is fine, its not optimal for serious competitive Overwatch. I was happy to see there are 1440p 240hz monitors available but ONLY two choices. I really don't understand why most companies are focusing on 4K 144hz right now but I bought one of those also just to see if its worth it since I could do video editing and casual gaming on it if need be (its still being shipped to me so no review on the difference).

I have never had any Omen products but the alternative was Lenovo and from what I hear its very loud and more expensive. So I tried this Omen X27 1440P 240hz Monitor, and loved it as soon as I got used to it which did not take long. I can play on Medium settings in Overwatch and always get 240 FPS. After about a week of owning it, 2-3 Pixels burned out which I tried not to let annoy me but it started to, then a week later 2 more pixels burned out. Ive NEVER had a monitor burn out pixels, and Ive used a few monitors every day for 8-10 years.

So I returned this monitor but as I am so used to 240hz gaming, going back to 144hz has been incredibly frustrating, as tracking targets while shooting is a much different. You wont notice the jump from 144hz to 240hz very much but you will notice it when you go back to 144hz from 240hz, the way you aim is different and I never thought it would be an issue.

The quality of this monitor is pretty good, the colors are decent. The menu buttons on the back of the screen are pretty annoying to use and the stand is very sharp so moving it around on your desk isn't the most pleasant experience but its full metal which is pretty cool. I will definitely be buying some 3rd party desk mounts for it though.

I ordered this monitor again and should arrive tomorrow, and I'm really hoping this time pixels don't burn out, or else I'm going to have to buy a 1080p 240hz monitor for my computer that is way too powerful for 1080p.

title: Great design, Great monitor (and recommended speakers)
text:
Has been a while since I purchased a monitor and I wanted to get an LED monitor, 1080P, that had a clean, stable (not wobbly) design and internal speakers. I wanted something close to 22 inches, which is a good, large size, for my desk.
Bad news first, the speakers are really poor if you are going to use them to watch movies or anything beyond basic computing. I'm still glad that the monitor has them but have added some external speakers since the monitor purchase. The only other issue that bugs me is that I don't want to see the ViewSonic logo each time the monitor is powering up.

Now the good stuff. First, I really love the design of the monintor and quality of the picture/display. Although it doesn't swivel on the base, the monitor is light and easy to move. It is stable on the stand and attaches to the stand very easily with one bolt. I like the clean lines, including the touch menu (no standard buttons) and construction appears to be excellent quality. It was pretty much plug and play for me out of the box.

When I first watched DVD (not Blu-Ray) movies using the monitor, I thought they were a tiny bit grainy (and they were) but then discovered that true 1080P movies, clips from the web, were excellent. I realized that my DVD player was the limiting factor, as it must not output 1080P, and am going to upgrade by picking up an internal Blu-Ray player soon.

Bottom line: this is an excellent monitor. If it had been more expensive, I would have been more hesitant at purchasing it because I am less familiar with ViewSonic versus Samsung or LG: I have a Samsung LCD television which is superb. That said, I looked at the comparable Samsung and LG monitors and liked this one's design (including the fact that it had speakers) better.

As an update, one of my kids managed to destroy the speaker-jack on the front of my computer, requiring me to purchase a set of speakers that had a jack on the front.
The Cyber Acoustics CA-2022 2.0 were a perfect match for this monitor in color, style and soft blue glow of the power button. After five months of owning the monitor I still highly recommend it. These speakers also produce very good quality sound in the opinion of my slightly damaged hearing: [[ASIN:B00006B9W3 Cyber Acoustics CA-2022 2.0 Computer Speakers- Black]]

title: MG7120 FOR CASUAL USE ONLY.  SUB-PAR ALL-IN-ONE FROM CANON
text:
Sadly, Canon, in its effort to make a wireless, compact all-in-one, has produced a piece of equipment which they should be embarrassed to put their name on. The worst mistake it to have eliminated to top loading tray for paper, replacing this with two flimsy trays inconveniently located under the output tray. These trays have limited capacity and are not visible, so that you don't know how much paper you have left. To make matters worse, you have to manually fold up the output tray in order to get to the paper trays. The output tray is poorly designed with no obvious reason as to why it was made with a narrow tab which is supposed to keep the output from falling on the floor. The 8 1/2 x 11 tray is so close to the lower edge of the machine that you almost have to hang it out over the edge of the desk in order to access the tray.

Unfortunately, the MG7120 does not have an on screen utility such as the wonderful MP navigator. This leaves you dependent on a small screen with clumsy menus with far too many choices. It takes a long time to set up anything other than the default. Even switching from printing to scanning to copying is major time consuming task. I do most of my work from the computer, and I have special settings for most of what I do.

I have owned several Canon Pixma all-in-ones and this one far noisier than anything else I have used. The print quality is fine, as with all Canons, but I find the color to be a little punchy for my taste. Strangely, in the middle of the set-up, the language was changed to Italian! This made it difficult to finish set-up so that I could change it back to English. Perhaps for casual users the MG7120 would be OK. I returned this after only a couple of days.

Clearplay has made a much wider range of movies viewable and/or more enjoyable to me and my family, and the ability to specify levels of filtering for various categories of objectionable material has made it much more flexible. They also release new filters for just about everything very promptly. I just wish there was a way for them to apply the technology to digital movie files, since I doubt DVD's are going to be around forever.

title: Pioneer Quality and Product Support Change a 5-star Review to a 2-star Review - Disappointing
text:
I bought this in July 2015. Just about the 2-year mark, no video would pass to the HDMI output ports (either one) from any of the HDMI input ports. I had sound, just no video.

For features and functions, I couldn't have been happier. I'm not running a movie theater in my house, but I do like nice surround sound and this AVR met my requirements. Number of HDMI inputs was more than sufficient. I loved the Zone 2 capability, which I used to run speaker to my deck/patio area. Really, really liked the iControlAV5 app. For me, it worked perfectly. I had access to all controls I need for the AVR on my Samsung Galaxy phone. My go-to music is always Pandora, which was easy to use. I can't think of one complaint.

Then came the 2-year mark. The quality is obviously a problem. For the cost of this item, I expect it to last until technology makes it obsolete. I contacted Pioneer support and only got a minimal response - the script-driven kind that are meant for dolts (and I mean that in the most endearing manner). Things like "how long is your HDMI cable?" Nonetheless, I responded to these questions and received no further support.

I had to buy another brand's AVR (Sony), which is probably as capable, if not more than capable, as this Pioneer. However, it does not have easy access to Pandora and a pretty dismal phone app, nowhere near as capable as Pioneer's.

I've lost confidence in Pioneer's equipment quality and their product support - both drove a 5-star rating to be a 2-star rating.

title: Horrible Lenovo Customer Service!
text:
I rarely write reviews and I try to be positive when I do, but I just had such a bad experience with Lenovo's Support Service that I am compelled to write a negative one. I had this laptop for 6 days (with only 3 days of actually playing and around 6 hours of use since I have been traveling). This is supposed to be a work machine for me, but I am glad I have not migrated anything on it yet!

First of, I'd like to say that it is a beautiful machine. I like the solid feel. It doesn't feel "plasticky" and cheap like some of the other marketed Ultrabooks out there. The laptop stays cool and quiet. The display is a bit muted in color in the beginning but a few tweaks on the display configuration made it better. The touchpad needs some getting used to. The only real issue that I have on the hardware is the lack of easy access for changing the battery.

Now for the software: WARNING! This laptop does not include any recovery disks!! Windows did its automatic updates on my third day of using this laptop. I tried a reboot after. The Lenovo Boot Optimizer started up...tells me there's an error but proceeded in trying to boot Windows. That failed. Windows started running its repair utility or whatever it needed to repair, but then says it can't repair (It said that it might have been caused by a software that I recently installed...I have not done anything on this except to install Microsoft Office Starter on the first day!!!) and I have to call customer tech support. Ok, so I called Lenovo Support. The first thing after briefly describing my problem, they told me that I the ONLY option that I have is for them to send me the recovery disks. I said great, send it to me please. But apparently I have to pay $59 for it!!! They said that it's a software issue and that it's not covered in their manufacturing warranty. I asked if there's a way for me to create my own recovery disks (by downloading the files from the website). Yes, he/she said...I can by burning it from the laptop! What irked me is the fact that after I described my problem, their "policy" is to "set my expectations" right away and tell me that they are a paid service. I wasn't asked any additional questions except "How can I help you today?".

I returned this laptop right away. Thank goodness for Amazon's excellent customer service policy! I gave two for stars for the hardware, but "product" for me extends to not just hardware but also software and customer service.

title: Better Performance With Some Problems
text:
Brand new, out of box, compared to MSI GTX 1060. First, $1,400.00 for a TI? LOL. So settled on this one. Performance is worth the upgrade. Getting up to 1950hz on core clock and only using auto settings. Ventilation on your case must be good to use this, it blows out some heat. Under load never above 70C. More noise but tolerable. Problems though makes it tough to rate more stars. I like quiet rigs, and the fans start and stop constantly at idle which creates a creaking noise. I am still playing with the X precision software to mitigate this. That leads into next problem. The software barely works. The fan control seems to work and the OC seems to although (it's like Afterburner) I don't use it, but it doesn't seem vary responsive to me. The UI is very clunky and the RGB control does not work at all. The default is a static dark blue which I don't mind. Would be nice to pair it with everything else though, which I use Asus Aura for. So far, after much research, this card is exactly what I thought it would be. The problems kill the performance upgrade enough to the point of in one word...meh.
Update: Using the new beta software X Precision 1 instead of XOC helps. The creaking noise on fan start up is still there, but less and the RGB lighting is now controllable. The RGB still will not sync with anything else, but at least I can change the color. I use 1080p, so the extra $$ for the TI version is just wasted money. Both versions have the same issues. From a 1060 gtx card this is a good upgrade, not worth it if you have a 1080ti though. Just know the issues these new 2080s have before you buy.

title: Is the MM60 a good PX-100 replacement?
text:
As many of those who reviewed this product, I am a proud owner of the legendary PX-100 that I've been enjoying for over 9 years. Failing to find a second pair, I came across the MM60 and was delighted to find it is still available on Amazon.com.

Design and build quality is essentially the same as the PX-100 with the addition of the mic/remote. When it comes to sound, I agree with others that it sounds a bit different from the PX-100 version I have. The MM60 lacks the detailed (yet non-exagerated) high ends that was very distinct in the PX-100. This also extends to the high-mid range. The PX-100 had very "tight" yet adequate bass. The low-ends in the MM60 are more "full/pleasing", yet at the expense for some "muddiness" at the low/low-mid interface. As noted in previous reviews, it seems that some batches of PX-100 had similar differences from what seems to be the earlier versions of PX-100. Hence, the impression that Sennheiser may have used different sets of drivers over the years of production.

Don't get me wrong, the MM60 are excellent headphones for their price. Just not up to the PX-100 in my opinion. If you are really looking at a PX-100 replacement, the MM60 is the closest you can get.

title: Great Phone For the Price!
text: I was looking for a Android phone, but I didn't want to spend $300 more for one.  I paid $116 for this phone and for all the features this phone has that was a great price.  The description of this phone says the screen size is 3.1" that is not true, but I knew that before I purchased it by reading the reviews.  The total screen size is 2 1/2 x 2" and the size of the phone is 4 1/4 x 2 1/4.  Of course the screen size on this phone is not as large as the HTC Evo or I phone, but it suits me very well.  I wasn't expecting everything that you can do with this phone, so I was pleasantly surprised.  You can set up you email accounts and the phone will alert you to when you have new messages.  There is a gps that works pretty well even though the screen is small.  You can download apps for the android market.  I haven't downloaded but a few and so far I have had no problems.  I saw one review that said Angry Birds did not work for this phone because of the screen size, but I have no desire to play it on a screen this small.  I have downloaded UNO and it works pretty well.  The graphic of the screen are descent and the colors are bright.  The camera is not the best but it is not bad.  Pictures look best when you take them in bright light and are still. You can view pdf documents and make them larger.  Of course you have to move them around on the screen to see the whole document.  Calls are clear and the ringers are very loud.  The speaker phone is descent also.  You can hear the person you are talking to really well and they could hear me... so that was a plus.  One of my favorite things about this phone is I can say "call Jackie" and it dials the number for me!  You can also say something like "directions to Nashville, TN" and it pulls up the directions!  The keys are really small, but surprisingly input is pretty accurate.  This phone has the 'Swype' input system so that makes it really easy to type a text message.  Swype is an entry method where you place your finger on the first letter of the word you are typing and just slide it from letter to letter.  It works pretty well.  All in all I highly recommend this phone to anyone who does not want to dish out over $200.  It is well worth the price at $116, and I received overnight shipping for $3.99 with my Amazon Prime.

title: Great replacement remote... for an average remote
text:
I purchased 2 of these to replace my parents' old TiVo remotes, which were several years old. A few of the "high traffic" buttons on their old remotes had begun to stick. Unfortunately, I think the squishy TiVo remote buttons are not really built for a lifetime of use, so I expect to get 3-4 years of use out of these remotes before they bite the dust as well.

These remotes are sold by WeaKnees through Amazon, and WeaKnees has a chart comparing the various TiVo remotes on their website. Honestly, there isn't too great a difference between the various remotes, beyond things like glow lighting (which several reviewers say drains the batteries) and the slide out keyboard (an EXTREMELY useful feature, but wasted on my parents who rarely type anything on their TiVo). I was tempted by the CO0210, though significantly more expensive, due to a review mentioning the more effective "clicking" buttons versus the typical TiVo "spongy" buttons, but I knew my parents would be put off by the change in button positioning. So I stuck with the same model they already had and have enjoyed using. Also of potential note, this is a dull grey finish, not the shiny black of some TiVo remotes. I prefer the dull finish, as it doesn't get that dirty, smudgy look the shiny one gets after a lot of handling, but to each their own.

The remotes each arrived wrapped in a clear sealed plastic bag (within a shipping box, obviously), so very easy to open, and had simple user manuals which explained how to access the Remote Control settings on your TiVo and set up the TiVo to work with your television. After putting in two AA batteries (not included), the remote controlled the TiVo (not the TV) instantly and perfectly. No setup required. Using the new remote, it is easy to go to the Remote Control settings on the TiVo and program the remote to control the TV.

The TiVo remote controls the television power and volume. Since those are not buttons you need for the TiVo itself, those buttons on the TiVo remote are "reserved" for your TV, once programmed. There is also a TV Input button. Which is where things go awry.

One of our TVs has an up-down menu, so as you keep pressing the TV Input button, it keeps going down the list until you land on the input you want. Fine. There is no further functionality past that, not even an exit button to remove the Input menu from the screen. No buttons on the TiVo remote can control any other aspect of your other equipment. Our other, newer TV, however, has a side scrolling input menu. It can NOT be controlled simply by pressing the input button repeatedly. You have to press the Left/Right buttons or use the laser pointer feature on the TV remote control. So if I press the TV Input button (even by mistake) on the TiVo remote, I bring up the Input menu... and have no way to navigate it, and no way to get that menu off the screen without hunting down the TV remote. Because again - NONE of the other buttons on the TiVo remote will control ANYTHING other than the TiVo.

This is a pain. A big pain. A pain that most cable company DVRs avoid by having a little switch on the remote, so you can use it as a universal remote to control all of your other equipment without hunting down other remotes. I prefer TiVo because my elderly parents find it MUCH simpler to use than the DVR from their cable company. I like the simple design of their remote. But I also think it is possible to keep the remote simple while adding some basic functionality. There are some pros and cons for using a cable DVR or using a TiVo, and everyone must pick what is right for them. But TiVo is gradually losing the battle, and their remotes are one of the myriad of little reasons why.

I docked 1 star because of the limited functionality and squishy buttons on the remote (though squishy buttons are not unique to TiVo remotes). The other 4 stars remain for being a an excellent replacement remote, that worked perfectly and did exactly what the original remotes did, right out of the box.

title: High quality, heavy duty connection
text:
This is a nice power strip. Here are the pros, cons, and workarounds that I have encountered.

Pros - Heavy duty, a switch for each port, ports are spaced apart

Cons - No USB, thick cord makes it hard to get it to sit upright, challenging to plug in some power bricks without turning its power switch off

Workarounds for the cons - Plug in a USB adapter to create USB ports, use short cords to move bricks off the power strip. As an aside, I find that the build in adapters can be unreliable and plugging in my own works out much better typically but of course this is an extra cost.

To avoid the cons, try using items that don’t require USB plug in or cords without a power brick.

Short extension cords example - https://www.amazon.com/Listed-Miady-Short-Extension-Outlet/dp/B07H9MCTGL

title: Great boards with excellent features made me a convert from being a hardcore ASUS fanboy.
text:
I purchased this motherboard as a replacement for the ASUS board that was previously in my HTPC. That motherboard had developed some issues with the raid controller, and would BSOD if we ever wrote faster than 3 or 4 MB/s. I am planning on replacing the old silverstone HTPC case that this machine is inside of with a Fractal Node 605, so I wanted to go with an mATX board so that I can include the slim optical drive in the new case.

My options for a new board were pretty slim, since I needed mATX or ITX with an AM3+ socket for the FX6300 in the machine, and I needed 6 sata3 channels for the 4 4TB drives in the machine for file storage plus the SSD primary drive and an optical drive.

When you start to filter down that far, there are not a ton of options, however I recently built a new monster rig and went with an ASRock motherboard, and had previously used an ASRock board for an altcoin mining rig, and have been thoroughly impressed with how well the boards perform, and how solid they have been, so deciding on ASRock this time around was pretty easy.

I've had this mobo up and running for about a month now, and it has remained rock solid the entire time, serving double (quadruple?) duty as not only the HTPC, but as a File, Plex and mumble server. All running 24/7. Considering I've had zero problems with my last two ASRock mobos, I do not anticipate any issues with this one.

title: Give Them A Chance
text:
These are my first Grado cans. After owning these for 2 days I can say I'm pleased! At first I was shocked by how bright and almost painful they were. After just 12 hours they already seem to be mellowing out a little. The bass response by themselves is thin, but gradually improving. When listening on my LG V20 I need to boost the bass quite a bit. Keep in mind that doesn't mean these are weak. In fact they are very capable of producing deep rich bass, but not the kind of overblown, unrealistic thumping bass that many popular headphones produce. These are very balanced...the way the artists heard their music in the studio. The real magic happens when I plug these into my vintage Sansui 661 receiver! Mind blowing good! Literally hearing things I never noticed before in songs I've heard hundreds of times. They are also very comfortable for me. I can wear them for several hours and not get sore ears. Overal probably the best headphones I've ever bought.

*UPDATE*
7/18/18
So it's been quite some time now. These are amazing phones. Well broken in. They are not nearly as bright as when new. Everything is balanced very nicely. The bass response is exceptional. title: Great Cable Modem
text:
I had a Motorola SB6121 4 channel cable modem but my internet service is 8 channel so I decided to upgrade.
I first purchased an Arris/Motorola SB6183 but returned it because the lights were too bright and also seem to have issues that I think were related to it being overly sensitive to line conditions.
Bought the Netgear CM600 to couple with a Nighthawk x8 router and I couldn't be more happy. I am getting about an 8 percent improvement in speed when compared to the SB6183 and there have been no issues at all. It just seems faster and smoother at loading web pages now.
It is more expensive than the Arris/Motorola SB6183 but I highly recommend it.

UPDATE: I have had this modem now for 3 months and it has now started in the last 2 weeks to slow down to under 10mbps until I reboot it. I have only had to do this twice but I never had to do this with my Motorola SB6121. I don't want to change to the Arris/Motorola SB6183 because of the lights but I may have to if this continues to be a problem

title: Had to get a replacement within 2wks, wouldn’t buy again
text:
:::UPDATE ON REPLACEMENT:::
I received the replacement promptly, before I could even take the original back to UPS to return. The issues with the previous projector work! In fact it seems that the keystone on the original was broken from the get, as the keystone on this one glides freely and responds immediately. There are no dark spots in the projection like the first one…yet, but the focus isn’t perfect. You can either have clear focus at the top or the bottom but not both. Whichever end you choose, the other is almost clear but still remains a bit fuzzy. I could deal with this, BUT. BIG BUT. The fan on this replacement unit is on CONSTANTLY, and it is NOT quiet. Quiet or silent moments in shows and movies are ruined, and even loud moments are sullied by the VERY LOUD whizzing whir of the unit’s fan. I honestly didn’t even know there was a fan on the last unit, that’s how quiet it was. Or maybe it was broken, too, who knows. But holy crap, the fan on this one is SO loud. I went to submit for ANOTHER replacement, but I guess 1 replacement is all Amazon will send you on one order, so I’m just going to return it. At this point, I’m too curious how another one will arrive and work, so I’m actually going to order it just one more time and keep my fingers crossed for a quiet one with keystone and focus switches that WORK and a fan that isn’t SUPER LOUD.

Prolly miss this one, y’all.

:::ORIGINAL REVIEW:::
It’s…fine. I was really hoping this could replace our TV in the living room AND be issuable outside once a year to play Hocus Pocus on the garage door for Halloween. Within 2wks, the keystone slider, which we have *never* used, is broken and the top of our screen is much wider than the bottom. We were still able to show the movie for Halloween coz kids don’t care, but it’s not suitable this way long term for replacing our TV, so I requested a replacement, which should arrive tomorrow. Since requesting that replacement 24hrs ago, the bottom left corner of the display has gone dark or shadowed. This projector has not been moved since the keystone randomly broke and I touched it to try and see if I could fix it. Nothing has jostled it since, no one has even touched it to turn it on; we’ve just used a remote. So…it just broke on its own like the keystone function. For 60 or so bucks, it seems fine to pull out for the holidays or the occasional family movie night, but, unless the replacement they send is just *stellar*, it won’t be replacing our TV any time soon.

Photos attached show random shadow that has appeared on the bottom left corner regardless of what’s in the scene. Keystone issue is slightly less noticeable in these pics, since they were taken from the side.

title: Super Fast Machine for the price. Doesn't *officially* work with Win7, but it is possible
text:
PROS: i7 is FAST. up to 32GB RAM. Runs Quite. lots of USB Ports (front and back). Simple Form Factor and lightweight, clean looking case. Can run dual Monitors. Expandable.
CONS: Win8 is awful. This machine doesn't officially support Win7, but it possible with some work. The power button is in an annoying spot, easy to accidentally push.

I bought this machine along with a Samsung 840EVO SSD Hard drive replacement. My plan was to immediately put the drive in, and install windows 7, as Windows 8 is such a pain to deal with.

I thought it would be easy, but it took a while to sort it out. I had to mess with the BIOS to get it recognize additional boot devices. Then, I had to disconnect the existing Win8 HD due to a conflict on the Win7 install.

The key to getting Windows 7 setup is to use drivers form the Asus M11AD (which comes with Windows 7).

So, I used the chipset drivers from M11AD and some additional Win7 Drivers for this M51AC (only a few were listed on the support page). Then, I used windows update to get the correct display drivers.

After all that, Win7 is fully operational and is blazing fast. All components are working. Next test, is to get some Crucial ram and get the machine up to 32GB.

Another small issue... the optical drive has no obvious eject button. So, to put in a disc when not in Windows, I used a paperclip and jam it in that little hole. So annoying. Thanks Apple, for setting the trend here. I realized there is a spot on the front that works as the eject button, but it's really hard to see. But, installing windows is about the only time I use optical media.

Great machine, but don't try to install Win7 unless you are up for a challenge!

title: Non-Technical Experience
text:
I had been looking for a Blu ray DVD player for some time. It seemed that when I decided to get Blu ray, everyone raised their prices putting Blu ray out of my budget. Over Memorial Day week end the price was reduced $ 30.00 to $ 218.00 ( No tax or shipping ). I purchased this machine through Amazon but it was executed through One Call. The delivery was incredible, Fed Ex showed up at my door far ahead of when promised.
One of the main purposes for getting this machine or one like it was the built in WiFi. I had no experience with WiFi but wanted it to link up with another computer in the house but mainly to stream Netflix. Set up was a dream. Yes, I did have to go to my computer twice, once to register with Sony Style and once to activate Netflix streaming. Both of these were very easy to do. Setup was a breeze ( remember this is from a non-technical person ). First I updated my Firmware on the Blu ray player. When hooked up to WiFi & internet; this means selecting upgrade, and it does the rest. Wow, that was tough. Then I put in my test Blu ray disc that I purchased ( Avatar ), the video and audio were incredible ( great ).
Next I wanted to try streaming video from Netflix, so I went to my computer again, selected a movie I wanted to watch on Netflix, added it to my instant play list, went back to Blu ray player, selected Netflix and the movie I wanted and it played. Netflix streaming video is not nearly as clear as a Blu ray disc but still excellent, maybe 720p. What was disappointing was Netflix sound, basic shallow stereo. I spoke with Netflix and they told me they were working on Dolby sound and it should be up and running by the end of the year. Meanwhile, this machine plays all my DVD's , including the ones that I have made. I should note that the player loads quite fast as that seems to be a complaint with a number of Blu ray players.
One negative for me that I noticed, the player does not have a repeat feature. Sometimes, when I am watching a DVD I want to see a scene over a number of times in a row, such as a song. You have to rewind for lack of a better word. What else can I say, it's a Sony and Sony puts out a quality product.

title: Good Introduction to Digital Recording
text:
I'm pleased with the Pioneer DVR-640H-S so far (after one month). I use it more as a VCR replacement/DVD player combination than a DVD recorder. Regarding recording to hard drive it's a great improvement over a VCR: no more making sure the tape has enough room, or that it doesn't have something you want to keep, or where the recording will begin on the tape, etc. The option to burn cable movies to DVD is there, but that's not for me.

The disappointments (again, after just a month and not having read the whole manual yet): you cannot rename recordings on the drive (listed by time/date); recording is just like a VCR in that if you screw it up (am versus pm etc) there's nothing you can do; you have to set the cable box up separately (no control of box via unit).

Consumer reports suggests renting a DVR (via cable company or TiVo) until the independently-sold selection improves. That wasn't an option for me as I needed a new DVD player anyway and figured I'd try the technology out.

Overall, I'm pretty happy with it, but not in love. The technology has plenty of maturing to do.

title: Not for all applications, terrible customer service
text:
I bought four for a condo complex I help manage. First of all, having hardwired power to them is a downside compared to other cameras with 2-5 year batteries. Second, all of the literature I read ahead of time, the instruction manual that came with it, the app, and the online tutorial all say it can be set up using wifi only and even have selections for that. I could not get the cameras to even power up that way. And, the methods to set them up was different depending on if you used the pamphlet, the app, the computer or a video. After searching all over website for customer service, the only thing I could find was leave feedback on the app. That goes to CS. Put in lengthy description, hit submit - and nothing. never sends. Finally found a customer support email. Send lengthy description, and they came back with a new method - I have to hardwire it by ethernet to the router to do the initial set up, then while connected, connect it to wifi, then disconnect. Our router(s) is on the roof(s) with access only by two sets of keys, separate for each building and wifi/ ssid is different depending on the final location. They said it COULD be done by wifi, but not very easy. I followed all of their instructions, tried every which way, spent hours playing with them. but could not get them to power up. Customer service is by email, and wait until middle of night for response, so essentially 24 hour lag. And the advice is not very good.

So, they look like rugged cameras, they might be - but they are too much of a hassle for this type of application. Never did see picture quality.

The issue in this complex is that the routers are on the roof, and we have various wifi signals/ SSID's around the complex.

title: Great product but it could be better
text:
I have been using Amazon Fire Cube for few years and ordered latest version of Fire Cube (2022) and Apple TV 4k 2022 one week apart. I wanted to compare both new models and stay with one that suits me best. This is my review of using Apple TV 4k 2022 after 2 days.

Pros:
- It is very sleek and I am particularly impressed with how the remote lets me navigate buttons without torturing my thumb. The tv unit itself is small and can fit in any area and in some cases without getting noticed
- The remote has the touch enabled click pad and it is a work of art. You can navigate different apps, movies, songs, lists with a swipe of your thumb. The home button is customizable and the settings allow you to control the TV functions within the same remote. The remote also allows you to speak what you need to type using the button on side which makes life easy
- Iphone connectivity is a blessing. Any time I need to search or type something up, a popup on my iphone lets me type and send it to apple tv. I can also control the on/off witch, changing Channels and navigation using my iphone
- Setup was so easy that I had to really scratch my head if it could get any easier than this
- Ethernet port built in to the Wifi+Ethernet version which is $10 extra then the WiFi only version.

Cons:
- I couldn't get my tv to turn off using the siri remote or the iphone. It is weird that I can turn on the tv using the remote, but unable to turn it off. I spent hours finding the solution on internet and it seems like it is an issue in some cases due to compatibility. Now, to be fair, my TV is from 2014, but still, Amazon Cube has never been an issue with on/off
- Youtube app - I am unable to exit youtube without having to get to home screen directly. For some reason when you exit youtube, the screen just goes blank
- I am unable to download Chrome Browser
- Batteries - you cannot replace batteries on the remote. You have to charge the remote when batteries go weak. And get this, apple does not supply the cable or charger for the batteries
- When using the iphone, I was unable to control the volume using iphone

Advice to Apple:
- Next release, think about wireless charging the remote using the top surface of the apple tv unit. Why not go further and allow wireless charging anything using the top surface of the Apple TV unit
- If wireless charging is not an option, add the charging cable a minimum with this product. Not everyone has a USB-C cable. Especially, if someone only has iPhone, (up to 13 pro), they still wont be able to use their cable for charging . Or change the charging port similar to what iPhone has. USB-C is only available in some versions of Macbook Pros and Macbook Air.
- Why not allow add chrome app to Apple TV? Why isn’t there a browser? If I screencast my phone to apple tv, and try to share something on web, the screen size does not do justice
- Improve the TV - Remote interaction. Mine couldn’t work when I try to turn off the TV. Amazon Fire Cube figured it out… why cant you
- Add color to the units similar to what you have done with iPhones
- Apple TV+… why should I spend $6 on this service? Add more channels to it. Let people enjoy something more for $6. I already pay for netflix and amazon prime, not to mention if I go with a cable provider where I have to pay $30 more. This is $6 extra that only would get me one more tv channel which is no match for showtime, HBO or ESPN.

I am sure there are many good things that I have not mentioned in my pros section, but I only wanted to mention the features that I normally use. Off course, the screen cast, facetime video sharing, smart-home integration and Airpods sharing could be something that makes this product stand apart from all the competition.

title: Packs a good punch in a very small footprint
text: This was the final piece in a new family room surround-sound system, with remainder of speakers being in-ceiling speakers.  The room is large (~20x23), and I was concerned that this would not be strong enough to provide the bass (especially since some reviews indicate this is used for a desktop computer surround set-up!), but some of my initial choice was based on aesthetics:  the room has a lot of white trim, and I wanted a very small footprint and a subwoofer that would blend into the background (there's a more "powerful" all-white speaker I also found on Amazon, but it cost $250 more than this one, so I thought I'd try this out first.  It has succeeded!  Listening to my kids watch some action-type movie the other day, I was struck by the significant bass-boost this little sub was able to put out.  Certainly enough for us.  We're not looking to blow the roof off, but it's definitely enough to provide the proper bass for our room.  Glad I found it! ***My only 2 minor quibbles is that it should have a white speaker grill instead of black, and that it should have a white cord (it comes with a black one).  I went out and bought a white cord to help it blend in, and it worked fine.

title: For those who wear glasses this is God sent!
text:
It took me a while to finally bite the bullet and order the viewfinder which arrived today.

I was hoping that this piece of kit would be useful for what it is, on the other hand the cost was almost half of what I paid for the camera itself, that is what was difficult for me to comprehend even though I read opinions of scores of people on the web.

Anyway, the parcel was waiting for me when I got home and after unpacking it installed it on the camera and switched it on. I checked it with my glasses on, not bad at all. I took my glasses off and adjusted the diopter dial underneath, all I could manage was WOW! I never expected the sort of image that I was looking at in the viewfinder, it was far superior to what I expected. It helped me see through the scene in front like never before, the LCD just did not do any justice.

I find it difficult to compose at arms length and keep the camera steady at the same time. I also wear progressive lenses (for those who may not know it is trifocals) and I always have issues with bright lights. being able to use the camera without my glasses on and at the same time never having to worry composing in bright conditions has made this gem of a camera complete in all respects.

This piece of kit will help me pick up the camera more often than not. I would not even hesitate to say this is an essential accessory for all those who buy the Panasonic Lumix DMC-LX7/GX1 and should be mandatory for all, over 50, with my kind of prescription glasses and have issues with bright light.

I know I got the best accessory for my camera and I would not hesitate to say it is money well spent.

LX7 now is my SLR from the film days, the way I was using it back then!

Thank you for reading!
