title: Great watch for the money
text:
Got this (my first “smart” watch) for a good price since it’s a couple models old now. For perspective, I’m a middle aged average guy starting to try to fight the dad bod and get into better shape. I also like classic watches (square forms just don’t do it for me) so I was happy to find an affordable round one like this.
I chose the green one for the nice soft silver watch body and replaced the band with a stitched leather one for a little more classy look for everyday wear. The green silicone band is comfortable and I’ll use that if I wear the watch in water, but for the rest of the time the leather really ups the look. Size isn’t too big, either (I have fairly thin wrists).
The software is reliable so far after a few weeks and the app is well-featured. I don’t use most of the features, of course, so it’s more than enough.
It’s definitely a fitness-focused watch with a few extras, not a full smart watch but adequate for average users like me who just want some basics to help me think about my activity level. It has lots of workout/activity choices, that’s for sure. I haven’t tried any sleep monitoring so can’t speak to that.
For the rating I stopped at 4 stars just because while they make a big deal out of the insane battery life, I think you’d have to tweak settings a lot to get that much. Leaving the watch factory settings as is, I’m getting about 8 days. That’s still fantastic compared to the expensive full featured smart watches, so no complaints. Also the weather app loses connection often. I wouldn’t care about that but I actually like it more than I thought I would, so hoping they improve it with a software update.
I like that the watch shows me texts when they come to my phone; it’s handier than I expected, helping me decide if I need to grab the phone to read more or reply.
People have been complimenting the watch, which is always nice. Looks kinda matter after all, since it’s still an accessory.
I definitely recommend the Amazfit brand now that I have this. It’s great as a watch with some nice added features at a great price, and if it’s your first smart watch, it can be helpful to get you more aware of your activity level and such, which can help add some motivation to put more effort into a healthier, more active lifestyle. Step counting alone has already made a difference for me.
Happy so far!

title: Excellent Product
text:
When I accepted a job requiring photography of houses, I was required to obtain a monopod. I am not a professional photographer, and have never used a tripod or a monopod before, so I spent some time researching the various products available on Amazon and other websites. I decided to purchase the Dolica 67-inch Lightweight Monopod based mainly on the great reviews, along with the price.

Since I have never used any of this type of equipment before, I had no idea how to attach my camera, or how to actually use this device. When it arrived, I was more than extremely pleased to see that it is very user-friendly with no fancy "bells and whistles" to figure out.

After I started using it in the field, I became more pleased with how easy it is to use, how light-weight it is, and the quality of the construction. While I am interviewing the homeowner, I can tuck this little monopod (collapsed) under my left arm, and still hold a clipboard and make notes during the conversation, as well as hand the homeowner the necessary paperwork, shake their hand, etc. While I am actually taking the photographs, I can adjust the height according to what I need to photograph, from the foundation to the roof, with the snap of a couple of the clips. I attach my camera to the pole as soon as I get in my car in the morning, and it stays on the pole the entire day, laying on the passenger seat while I am driving and the camera is plugged in to refresh the charge.

I would recommend this monopod to anyone who needs to photograph anything taller than they are and/or to people who need it just for stability of the camera. I use it for both, and could not be happier. It is small and lightweight enough to carry around all day, and adaptable to most conditions. Yes, it would be nice if the head would tilt, but that's not usually an issue. When I need a tilt, I lean it back and forth to get the correct angle.

title: The Frustration has Ended!
text:
This is my first foray into equatorial mounts, so I freely admit that I have no frame of reference with which to compare this mount.

I have had a longtime interest in amateur astronomy and tried to marry it to my love of photography many years ago in my youth. I spent a lot of time trying to follow stars with traditional tripods. (I grew up barely able to afford photography, and could not even consider the expense of an equatorial mount--not even for Halley's Comet.) All I can say is, even without any options purchased with it except the adapter to attach my camera equipment to the dovetail--is wow. Even without a motor, it helped me follow the recent (2017) solar eclipse in the US, and was by _FAR_ the most convenient way to follow a celestial body through the sky. Though heavy, the mount is rock-solid sturdy. The gears/mechanisms are very smooth, and their 360° operation (for Right Ascension and Declination), is nice. All I had to do was assemble and balance it by the provided instructions, and then on the day of the eclipse I merely (but carefully) aligned the helpfully marked leg with magnetic North and it followed the sun flawlessly by the mere turning of one knob. To a guy who grew up "jury-rigging" and the frustrations of "making do," the convenience and ease of use blew me away. Now I am eagerly looking forward to getting the motor and computer controls and studying the sky as I had hoped to do in my youth. My only real quibble with the thing is it took me possibly 3 times longer to get it back in its boxes and styrofoam inserts than it did to assemble the whole thing the first time.

title: Sunstri 2.0 iPhone flash drive problem and resolution.
text:
I had high hopes for the Sunstri 32Gb flash drive for iPhone.
There are several things you need to know.
My wife had 2000 photos on her iPhone 6s. Goal was to transfer to Sunstri drive. First problem I ran into has nothing to do with this drive but has to do with Apple ICloud.
My wife had iCloud enabled on her phone. Unbeknownst to me was that although it looked like there were 2000 photos of her iPhone only about 200 were full photos. The other 1800 were really just thumbnails of those pictures stored on the iCloud.
The Sunstri software downloaded okay but is confusing to use. Anyway, after much fiddling around the 200 real pictures on the iPhone downloaded. The others appeared to download but much faster than the real photos which took about a minute each which is very slow.
Next problem was getting the 1800 real photos off the iCloud onto my iMac. I tried on my own but it’s difficult to do. Finally I called AppleCare which I purchased when I bought my iMac. A technician spent an hour helping me export photos from iCloud to my Mac.
From now on we won’t be using iCloud.
Once downloaded my plan was to export to the Sunstri flash drive.
The process went very poorly. It took 44 hours to transfer all 2000 photos - about 5 GB worth. Ridiculous.
Once transferred almost all the thumbnails were missing making viewing any photos a complete chore.
Also it took about 2 mins for a photo on the drive to open up so you can view it.
At that point I had had it. I was going to erase and reformat drive as one last shot but that action “failed “.
Just to compare I exported the 2000 photos to my Sandisk extreme 3.0 32 GB flash drive in about 20 minutes.
Of course that drive can not be plugged directly into iPhone for viewing.
Since then I contacted the seller and they told me they would refund $15 for my trouble. I paid $22.99 but said I would take the $15.
So far I haven’t gotten any confirmation of the refund. I will update later when/if I get it.
So to summarize, I can not recommend this product. It did not do what I wanted it to do and in the end was inoperable.

Update 8/14/18
As promised I am updating this review.
As noted the above seller originally offered a $15 refund on this item which cost $22.99
After writing the above review, I was contacted by the seller who then said they would provide a full refund. I just received word from Amazon that I received the full refund of $22.99.
Although I had a bad experience with the product, it is certainly possible that the product I received happened to be defective. In view of all the other positive reviews, I would say this is likely. In any event, I was treated fairly by the vendor, MCSQUARE,who Contacted me promptly and resolved the issue to my satisfaction. Because of this I have changed my rating from one star to three stars.

title: Promising Case!  Looks like it will be awesome.
text:
Ok, so first off, I'll let you know that I'm returning this case- My mistake, I thought it was GREY and Rose Gold (as it seems in the pictures) but it is BLACK and Rose Gold. Well, if I'd read the color description better...anyway. It is quite nice, it just does not appeal to me.

On to the important parts!v Package arrived in excellent condition (RAGE FREE! It came in a durable ziplock bag) and quickly.

The case fits wonderfully snugly- not so tight that you're straining to get it on and off, but very secure fit. I purchased this case after I was incredible dissatisfied with the fit from the case I got at time of purchase- it was simply too loose. This is perfect!

The feel is very nice, easy to grip on the sides without being...too sticky or weird. The "metal" frame is actually made of some kind of really durable plastic- VERY FLEXIBLE so it's not going to break the first time you drop it, but I would definitely trust my phone in this case for drops (I drop my phone a lot...). The texture on the back of the case is interesting; it's a nice feel, though I'm not if it would trap all kinds of crap or not. The ridges are shorter and farther apart than they might seem, so I'm guessing it'd be find with the occasional disinfectant wipe that I use anyway.

Has a significant edge wrapping around the front of the phone to protect the screen, and accommodates glass screen protector. It should be noted, however, that this is NOT the CURVED glass screen protector that's in the works from Zagg; this one ([2 Pack] Galaxy S7 Screen Protector, SPARIN® [Tempered Glass] [Bubble-Free] [9H Hardness] [Scratch-resistant] Screen Protector for Samsung Galaxy S7) does NOT cover the entire surface of the screen, so I cannot say for sure that it will work with the upcoming curved protector from Zagg.

Works with my Samsung wireless charger, though I feel like i have to be a bit more careful in positioning it; maybe the thickness of the material makes it more finicky? But it does indeed work.

One more thing to keep in mind- I tried to plug in the little USB adapter that comes with the phone (for using a keyboard or jump drive) and it DOES NOT FIT securely while the case is on the phone.

This is nothing special, just a 17 year old well proven NXP 1334A DAC chip - and by being that, it saved our project!

An effort I'm involved in had a circuit board designed by someone else with a horribly mis-chosen DAC, a flaw I only became aware of at the last minute. So how on a Sunday can one purchase a generic I2S to analog DAC? Same day Prime of course!

Board arrived the day I ordered it, quickly soldered up a custom wiring harness to drive the I2S lines with our circuit instead of a raspberry pi, and... audio! Based on that experiment the well proven NXP 1334A DAC goes into the next revision of our custom board, and everyone is happy.

Do beware that in ordinary use this requires some soldering, and the ground pins will take a fair amount of heat. I imagine if you use it with a pi you also need to jump through some hoops to configure I2S output - there seems to be some guidance on the vendor's website.

title: Must buy NX lens
text:
Pros:
Fast focus
Nice bokeh
Crisp and clear picture quality
Small

Cons:
Sometimes hit and miss focusing
Not completely silent focusing motor
Because of the way the NX300 mount is; the pancake lens sticks out a little more than usual
Lack of iFn

This is a fun and great lens to use. The pictures are clear and the bokeh are smooth compared to the kit lens. There is almost no noise when focusing with the 18-55 mm lens and with lens there is a noticeable but not annoying noise when focusing. It is way quieter than the 20-50 mm kits lens. Focusing was quick very and accurate most of the time. There were a few times in low light and low contrast areas where the camera missed the focus entirely. Turning on the AF assist lamp will help help fix the problem. There is no image OIS, but since the lens is quick and has a large aperture, using a faster shutter speed will solve the issue. iFn is not available but since this is a simple prime lens it is not needed. It is a great overall lens and every NX camera owner should get one.

title: First experience with USB 3.0
text:
Like the title states this is my first experience with a 3.0 flash drive. At the time I paid $25.99 for this 32 GB drive and I am rather impressed at the speed at which I can write to it. Keep in mind to get the full benefit you need to have a USB 3.0 port on your computer. Testing the device I used a 800MB mp4 file and first copied from my computer to the flash drive and then from the flash drive back to the computer using both 2.0 and 3.0 USB ports. The times I recorded are as follows:

* 2.0 port from Computer to flash drive 9 min 24 sec
* 2.0 port from flash drive to computer 28 sec
* 3.0 port from computer to flash drive 1 min 10 sec
* 3.0 port from flash drive to computer 28 sec.

As you can see there is virtually no difference between USB 2.0 and USB 3.0 when writing from the flash drive to the computer (although with most USB 2.0 flash drives it would take 2 1/2 minutes ), but a world of difference when writing from the computer to the flash drive.

I was surprised to find that the flash drive comes completely empty. There is no pre-loaded security software or file management software.

All in all I'm satisfied with it.

title: "Oooo... I think it looks better!?"
text:
I'm an NOT an A/V Expert. Just a regular dude who likes to play games and watch blu-rays.

With that said, I recently purchased a Seiki 50" 4K TV. I bought this cable hoping to see it upscale my 1080P stuff to 4K.

First things i learned is, make sure you do this.
1) Sharpness should be set to Zero.
2) Motion Estimate and Motion Compensation should be set to zero

I bought this and first tested it on my Xbox one which was outputting 1080P 60hz before the u-vision cable. After U-Vision i was naively expecting 4K 30hz, but i still got 1080P 60hz. Well i didn't get this before i bought it, but it can only upscale 1080P 30hz (NOT 1080p 60hz) to 4K 30hz (now i get it!)

The box claims that the cable will still enhance the picture quality of the 1080P 60hz, but i honestly couldn't really tell.

Unfortunately, (or fortunately because why would you want to lower from 60hz to 30hz except in this case) I can't set the Xbox One to 1080P 30hz or 24hz. So instead I used the cable on my PS3.

Using the PS3, i played Dark Knight rises on blu-ray and TADA, the TV indicated that the resolution was not 1080P 24hz or 30hz, but it was at 4K! And i THINK it looked better.

Case in point, I give it 3 stars because it looks like it works, but my eyes can't really tell for sure.

I only post this review for anyone who's a newb like me and wants to see their xbox one output 4K. Welp, maybe you should just try turning your sharpness to 0 and see if it looks better.

OH and it upscales 720P to 1080P. That's pretty neat.

Short Recap

Pros
+ It's only 40 bucks for a upscaler
+ My Seiki definitely recognizes that the signal is now 4K
+ 720P 50/60 to 1080P 50/60
+1080P 24hz/25hz/30hz to 2160P 24hz/25hz/30hz

Cons
- To get 4K, it's gotta be 1080P 24hz/25hz/30hz. My Xbox One can only do 1080p 50hz/60hz.
- 1080P 50hz/60hz outputs 1080p 50hz/60hz (no change pretty much) except with supposed "Picture Quality Enhancement"
- My eyes couldn't see a significant difference when upscaling blu-ray on ps3 from 1080P 24hz to 4K 24hz. I was getting a "oooh. i think it looks better!?" vs the "OMG this is 4k!" i was hoping for.

title: Works great in Linux

I inserted the card into the PCI express slot on my laptop, connected the included USB power cable to an open USB 2.0 port and the other end to the card. I tried unplugging the card, re-inserting without seeing the drive populate /dev.

I decided to power the hard drive with the power adapter. This made me realize that connecting the power to the drive and the drive to the adapter then inserting the card works perfectly.

I'm very pleased and get nearly 10 times the speed on read/write using ext4 to ext4.

This worked for me in Fedora 15 & Knoppix 6.5, but failed to work or even respond to the Kernel in Debian squeeze/sid.

title: Good fit, great sound!
text:
I purchased the Rimor and was then offered a test for the B530. Enjoyed doing a comparison of the two! The fit of course was the same, both provided a choice of a tight, snug fit which pretty much buffered all outside noise, even the motor on my F250 truck. So yes to both for noise cancellation quality. Wind and background noise still carries over to phone conversations, my roosters rule if I'm outside on a phone call. The smaller tips I found more comfortable, but that is definitely personal preference. The smaller producing a looser fit and if heavily jarred can drop out. I'm not a runner so can't confirm the tightness there but I have had very few times that they have dropped and usually because I have not inserted well.
As far as music, for ear buds both the Rimor and the B530 are exceptional. If you like bass like I do then the B530 is the way.
I have not had the batteries run done as yet - At this point I have to take Tranya's promises on battery life. With both the storage in the ear bud and in the case and don't see them falling short on that promise.
Takes a bit of practice to take the earbuds out of the case as the cutout to slide your finger into is for a pretty small finger.
Packaging is quality for sure and the case will hold up and protect the earbuds from damage without a problem.
All in all the music quality for these earbuds is fantastic but is not superior to the use of full ear headphones. That is something I don't think one can ever expect.
Voice quality for phone usage (which is my primary use) has been great, I have no complaints. I prefer the Rimor's "not so deep" fit. Calls are easy to answer and to disconnect. The slight touch on the bud itself works well. Changing the volume while on a call or listening to music is a bit challenging but that seems to be a "user" problem and error and not a fault of the ear bud!
Yes, I would absolutely recommend these ear buds. Both Rimor and B530 are excellent.
Rimor: 1) Case is somewhat smaller and can easily go in your jeans pocket.
B530: 1) Deeper bass tones. A slightly deeper fit than the Rimor so does hold in the ear a bit tighter.

I'm still evaluating it. At first I was going to return it and get a 7inch model. Then I started using it and it works great for what I need it for. I'll add more to my review once I actually play with the Digital Multi Meter and other stuff. I do like the device.

title: With reserved expectation, this is a decent tablet for the price
text:
I bought two of these tablets as a gift from my parents and I for my nephew and niece for Christmas. Up til the date of my purchase, I was researching like crazy to find a tablet that was reasonably priced that could satisfy any need that my nephew and niece would have. Tablets like iPads, Kindle Fire or Nexus 7 which would have certainly gotten the job done with no doubt are too expensive for just one person or even 3 to give as a gift. I was starting to lose hope that I would find a tablet at all when I stumbled upon the IdolPad Plus. I was very impressed with the specs and the link below is to a video review by TheeBookReader which equally impressed me enough to believe that I had FINALLY found the tablet I was looking for.

[...]

While this tablet is not a terrible tablet by any mean, I found myself disappointing from it and a bit scared/upset to present it to my nephew and niece for Christmas. I will start with the biggest(Minor issue depending on who you ask or is using the tablet) issue I have with it. It will not run Angry Bird Space or Angry Bird: Star Wars. It will run the Original Angry Bird app PROVIDED I turn off WiFi. When it IS working, the Original Angry Bird game runs very well on this tablet but I shouldn't have to turn off WiFi to get it to work.(I doubt my niece and nephew will know how to do this as they are 2 and 6...). Now, I am sure that some of you are probably screaming at the screen/me that it is just Angry birds, who cares. This game is the BIGGEST reason why my parents and I got it for the kids since they often ask their parents for their expensive iPhones to play these games and other like it. It is a HUGE let down to me and I tried basic troubleshooting for the app(uninstalling and re-downloading it, etc). I sent a email to Rovio in hopes that they might be able to assist but I doubt they will be able to.(Who can blame them, the Android market is way too fractured with different products to fully support them all)

Moving on from the "petty" Angry Bird issue. The storage space is "terrible". I don't know if I missed something from the specs but the on board storage is only 2 GB, which leaves about 500 mb as the OS data takes up most of that space. The "missing" 2 GB is found in the included SD card. I had initially thought the SD card slot to be a great perk for the tablet as my nephew or niece could(With the help of their parents or I) increase the storage at a later time. I was under the impression that there was 4 GB on board(I knew the OS would take some but there should/would be more then 500 mb remaining). For those not familiar with Android, not EVERY app can be installed/run from the SD card and those that can run on the SD card typically run worse then those that run off of the on board storage space. All of the games that I successfully installed onto the SD card didn't have any issues BUT my niece and nephew(And their parents) will have to be taught how to move apps from the on board storage to the SD card.

As the other reviewers have mentioned, the battery life is not great which I knew of before getting the tablet in the first place. I don't consider this a huge problem(Maybe the 2 year old might get impatient though... D:).

Alright, now that I got the negative out of the way. Let's try to look at the positive!

The screen is actually ok.(Something I was concern about) It's not as sharp as current tablets from big names company like my Google Nexus 7 but it gets the job done and it doesn't hurt my eyes. The screen is pretty responsive with its capacitive screen. I only ran into issue tapping icon or menu opinion along the edges of the tablet. title: Effective, but took a bit to get to work
text:
I'm rocking an overclocked first generation i7 processor, but the motherboard I’m using is so old that it lacks USB 3.0 headers. I recently upgraded to a new case and the lack of them became a problem. I bought this PCIE card to add the appropriate headers to my motherboard. I needed two headers. A lot of the available options offer usb ports and a single header. I specifically needed two, because that is what the case supports.

This card was my solution. It has two USB 3.0 headers and that’s it, but that’s what I needed.

Unfortunately, what I got a was a mixed bag. It came in a generic box in an anti-static bag with a mini-cd containing a bunch of drivers for different products and an alternate low profile metal slot cover, presumably for use in smaller cases. Oddly, reading other reviews suggests that the inclusion of the CD and the alternate slot cover is somewhat hit or miss. Perhaps they don't always remember to put them in the box.

Installing the card on my motherboard was a bit of a problem. I’d read another review on Amazon that suggested that the card isn’t always detected correctly. It wasn’t detected by windows the first time I turned on my computer, or the second, or the third. I finally did something you should never do… install it with the computer turned on. Yeah. Call me an idiot. It worked though, and I have not had problems since. I wouldn’t suggest doing this, and frankly, the fact that this was only way I could get it to be detected is definitely a huge knock against this product.

Driver installation, likewise was a small headache. The box did not provide any specific information about the card, so upon trying to install the drivers for it, I found myself struggling with the included CD to figure out which of the several dozen included drivers was the correct one. Since I still use Windows 7 on my rig, it didn’t automatically update. Thankfully, a review of Amazon’s product listing gave me the answer I needed, but without it, it’d have taken a lot of trial and error.

If you need to install off the disc, run the Setup.bat file, choose PCI-E USB 3.0 drivers, then NEC 720201/720202.

Bottom Line:
I can’t say I’d recommend this card. I bought it because it needed two USB 3.0 headers and because the price was right. It works, but took a lot more work that it should have to get it there. Given the shortcomings, I can’t say I’d recommend it.

title: Great product, but there are some trade-offs.
text:
PROS:
1. Very rugged feel. MAGPUL type quality.
2. Solid adjustable kickstand design.
3. Quality seems on par with price.

Cons
1. Weight
2. As others have said, removal is painstaking if you don't want to crack your Surface Pro.

Verbose: I waited for some time to write any kind of review, because on its arrival I did not really know how I felt. I'll echo other reviewers and say that what surprised me most was the dramatic perceived increase in weight and loss of form-factor. I almost didn't think I would keep it and considered returning it because it turned this slim machine into something that felt bulkier and ungainly.

However, after some time I realized that it really wasn't that bad for my purposes. It (The Surface Pro + Case + Type cover) was still far lighter than my Lenovo, and in fact is still lighter than my Wife's 2015 Macbook Pro. It was annoying at times, taking a device that has slimmed to the point of actually having the form factor of an iPad and then tacking on a bunch of ounces...but I don't regret it and have left it on for one simple reason: I break stuff. I do. I have excuses: I'm in the military, I travel a lot, etc. I commute to work and I need something that I can throw in my bag and know that it can handle being jostled around. I'd like to take better care of my electronics, but I don't always have that ability. This thing has withstood a significant amount of travel and "jostling" over the past few months and the whole thing still looks like new. Yes, I wish it was lighter and sometimes I get annoyed that I can't get the UAG kickstand to sit quite as well as the original and I'll take the case off....but day to day? I keep the case on 95% of the time and don't regret buying it at all.

You do get what you pay for when it comes to telescopes and expecting to see "Hubble" images through this scope is bound to make you disappointed.
I was actually pleasantly surprised by the crisp image this scope gave when looking at the moon.

The supplied barlow (3x) and eyepieces are laughable to a "serious" amateur-astronomer but they do actually perform very well. Unfortunately a 4mm eyepiece is too powerful for a scope like this, it would have made more sense to ship it with a 8 or 12 mm instead. The barlow is plastic but the lens is actually of quite good quality and does not stretch or blur the image noticeably around the edges. If you already have a set of eyepieces you can throw the supplied once in the garbage without any regret, if not, the supplied ones will work pretty good but don't expect any 300x magnifications to work, that's utter bull and shouldn't even be mentioned...
Make sure to use the 45 degree diagonal as you will not get focus otherwise...

You will get stunning views of the moon using this scope, you will also be able to see the bands on Jupiter and the rings on Saturn as well as track their moons.

I would rate the image quality of the scope to 4 stars considering the price but the poor quality of the eyepieces and the finder-scope takes it down to a 3 star.

title: Good card tech - bad Amazon shipping dept
text:
I hear good things about the 5870 and was looking forward to mine despite the issues with immature drivers. This review is really targeted at the Amazon shipping policy.

First of all, let me say that I am a longtime customer of Amazon.com and love the selection and prices. However, the packaging for shipping can be a gamble. Strangely, they often ship delicate and expensive electronics with little or no real padding, just a bubble-pak thrown loosely on top inside a cardboard box. Why is this? Is it to shave the margin? How does that make sense when it surely increases the rates of damages and returns? Maybe the accountants at Amazon have it figured out, or maybe it's just one of those things they can improve if they pay attention to it.

Amazon ships hard drives this way all the time, which is madness. Mad I tell you!

Anyway the anticipated card arrived in the retail box as expected, but just sitting loosely in the bottom of a cardboard box with a bit of bubble pack thrown on top. This is totally inadequate to protect a heavy and sensitive piece of expensive electronics gear, especially one with moving parts.

I returned the card right away due to this potentially destructive shipping job. I don't want to have my $500 part suddenly die (and maybe take my computer with it) in 2 months because it got thrown like a brick by the friendly UPS guys.

Wake up Amazon! This poor shipping policy is really shaking my confidence in your business. Wrap that stuff up right, please!

title: Ouch, ouch, ouch!!
text:
A while ago i purchased a pair of relatively inexpensive "off-brand" wireless headphones, which i've never had a problem with but after a couple of months i tend to get bored of a product and start looking at a new replacement. I had seen these Plantronics Backbeat Fit headphones around the gym several times on different people, and my first impression was that they looked good, non-bulky and relatively comfortable.

To my surprise apparently you can't judge comfort without ever actually "trying on" the product, who knew right? Well, this is one of those times Amazon's return policy is worth every penny for the Prime membership. The extensive good reviews must all have ears completely different than mine. I tried these one and couldn't keep them on for more than 30 minutes. The rubberized ear piece that goes inside your ear is not as soft as i'd like it to be. Its built felt very intrusive, as if with every step i took they moved around and pushed against the hard cartilage right above the ear canal entrance.

The sound is very good, clear and great bass. Some people complained the volume wasn't very loud, to me it was, i wasn't able to reach the highest level without serious discomfort. Another comment i read was that the long piece that goes around the head was very long. This was the case for me and i don't have a small head. Since the ear piece itself didn't get a good fit the headphone itself wasn't very secure, making the whole thing move up and down as i ran, especially since the neck piece was bigger than i hoped for.

Overall i give these 2 stars, one for looks and another for sound, comfort was very much lacking, and i believe this rates almost as high up there as the sound quality of headphones, especially with how much time i spend wearing these a week.

title: Very happy with purchase
text:
Just received this yesterday, so I will update my review periodically. I have not installed Microsoft Office or eliminated any bloatware yet. This is the first ASUS product I've ever owned, and I'm also new to Windows 10, so there may be a bit of a learning curve for me, at least at first.

Packaging: very well packaged. The ASUS box was encased in a box, which was encased in another box. Very well protected.

Delivery: delivered on time, but I was surprised USPS left this item sitting on my front porch when I wasn't home. Normally if it's an item over like $100, they take it to the post office for me to pick up at my convenience. Luckily my husband was tracking the package like a stalker, so he was able to see exactly when it got dropped off, and I had my neighbor come over and snag it for me until I got home.

Size: I did not take out calipers and measure the laptop, but it is very thin profile, just like the description says.

Weight: Impressively lightweight, but appears to be very durable, as it is metal. Very minimal plastic from what I can see. Looks a lot like my husband's Mac, but much lighter and slimmer.

Overall look: Very sleek design, and the titanium gold looks pretty sweet. Yes, these are purely aesthetic things, but I figure if I'm dropping $700 on something, I like for it to look good. A lot of similarly priced products looked like a tank, which doesn't affect functionality.

Processing Speed: I played around on the internet some, just to get a feel for using it. Appears to be fast, especially for my purposes, which will include Microsoft Office processing, internet surfing, checking email, and some social media I'm sure. I am not a gamer.

Keyboard: Seems nice. No issues so far. It is a back-lit keyboard, which is nice. Remember that this is a 13.3-inch laptop. so you don't have the number keypad off to the right. While that, to me, is a nice-to-have, it also adds size and weight, which I was trying to minimize when shopping for a laptop. Just personal preference. I'm sure ASUS makes a 15.6" or larger version of this same laptop which would have a number keypad.

Multi-tasking: Haven't done much of this yet, as I don't have Microsoft Office installed yet. I can tell there are some bloatware on it that runs in the background and eats up memory, although I had no issues with memory for my purposes. I still need to see what programs I can delete to free up more memory in the future.

Noise: very minimal. I kept thinking it had turned itself off, but no--it's just very quiet.

Battery life: Up to 12 hours, and I believe it. I hovered over the battery icon at one point, and it was almost full but not quite, and it said 10 hours remaining. Oh, and it was already partially charged when I took it out of the box.

Other features:

I love that the lid opens smoothly without lifting the bottom of the computer with it. My Dell Inspiron from 2009 is bulkier and I have to hold the bottom down while opening the lid. Kind of a pain in the ass. The ASUS eliminates that nuance, as I'm sure most laptops nowadays do.

I like that the cursor pad is larger than the one on my old laptop.

If you're a Mac person, you'll find that some of the same keyboard/cursor pad short cuts can be used on this machine.

No issues yet. Although for some reason I had it in my head when I purchased this that it was a touch screen laptop. This is not the case. And that's totally fine, as the touch screen was not a critical thing when shopping for laptops. This way keeps my screen cleaner anyway.

Also, my husband (who is a die-hard Mac person) is really jealous of my laptop. For years, I have avoided conversations like, "I need a new laptop," or "my computer is so slow," because his response is always, "You should get a Mac." Well guess what--I don't want to shell out that kind of money, and Mac's OS and Desktop layout are completely different from what I'm used to. I use Linux at work, and I've always used Windows for personal purposes. I can't use his Mac because it is confusing and frustrating to me. The ASUS seems to be much better bang for the buck. He's always been like "Live by the Mac, die by the Mac," but he really likes this ASUS so far. They say once you go Mac, you don't go back.....well, I've read some of the reviews, and quite a few Mac people have converted to this computer. That's pretty impressive, because Mac folks swear by the quality and efficiency of their Macs.

title: After trying a few, I found what I think is the best protector.
text:
My review/comparison between Skinomi and TechArmor screen protectors:

Having never installed a screen protector on any of my devices, I decided to spend a little extra and buy different ones from a couple of the top rated manufacturers on Amazon. Skinomi and TechArmor. Since I had no idea what I would like, I tried two different TechArmor protectors for my tablet (one HD clear and one with the matte anti-fingerprint, anti-glare), and bought a Skinomi TechSkin for my phone.

Phone installation was first and was pretty straight forward. I was glad to have read some reviews, and knew in advance that immediately after installation the screen doesn't look that good. Since it's a wet application, it really does take a full 12 hours before it's all clear and smoothed out. But, the screen has a nice feel to it and the clarity and sharpness is excellent.

Next was the installation of TechArmor (matte finish) protector on my Nexus 7 tablet. This protector is by far the best choice for being fingerprint resistant, but the clarity of text and images was diminished enough that I opted not to use it at all. The installation of the HD clear version of the TechArmor protector followed. Image and text clarity are perfect but it really provides no resistance to fingerprints at all. The feel of it was also a little too grippy for my preference.

During the days of this experiment, I was using my phone with the Skinomi TechSkin, and liking it more everyday. The choice was really simple. Skinomi TechSkins somehow have found a way to provide perfect clarity for text and images while being VERY resistant to fingerprints. You will still wipe off your screen from time to time, but I'd say this protector reduces the problem with fingerprints by 70%. Naturally, I bought the same TechSkin for my Nexus 7 tablet.

The wet application is a little more difficult in general and especially on a larger screen. I totally screwed it up and ruined my Skinomi TechSkin for the tablet. Knowing it was my own fault, I had little doubts that I would have to buy another if I wanted it. Nevertheless, I emailed Skinomi support about what happened. To my surprise (and delight), they only asked for a copy of my order, a picture of the ruined protector and the code that comes with the documentation in the box. With that, they actually sent me a free replacement! If that's not excellent customer service, I don't know what is....

Before attempting the second installation of the same protector on my tablet, I watched the youtube video they tell you about in the instructions and noticed that I wasn't using nearly enough spray. This really solved all my problems. If you have enough spray on the protector, it's fairly easy to get it perfectly into place. Otherwise, it's nearly impossible. That's the only advice I'd give - watch the video and see how much they use and do the same. You'll have no issues.

I now have Skinomi TechSkins on my phone and tablet and couldn't be happier. With the money I spent in this little experiment, take my advice and just by yourself the Skinomi. You'll be glad you did.

title: Disappointed in Fire
text:
Ok - I really want to like my Fire. It has all the additional capabilities that I have desired since I bought my first Kindle - checking email, browsing the web, checking the weather, listening to music, watching movies, TV shows and Internet broadcasts. I aggregated my Amazon gift cards and pulled the trigger on 12/27/11. I opted for free shipping (which I believe takes it through China Fedex for delivery) and finally it arrived! I powered it up and have `utilized' it for almost a month. So here we go with a bottom-line review.

As a eReader - Wow - it is heavy! I definitely like my old Kindle better as it is lighter and easier to read with than the Fire
Web Browsing - I saw all the bad press about the browser and would agree totally - slow! And maybe it is me...when I did a Google search when I touched the links, nothing happened! I switched to Yahoo as the search engine and that worked better
eMail - easy to tie all my accounts together. One irritating item - when you navigate from the inbox list to the individual email, there is an artifact in the upper left quadrant of the screen from the previous screen. Not cool. Hard to believe it is there. Details!
Applications - limited to the Amazon Fire store. I thought that I could level the playing field with my iPhone with an "Android" tablet - not even close
Touchscreen -very sensitive - became very irritating when trying to navigate - yuk! Be careful! Also smudges easily and because it is black - it shows
Holding your Fire - I can't get comfortable with it in portrait mode (weight? shape?), a little easier in landscape - this is my first tablet, so this might apply to other 7" tablets
Volume control - all software driven, not consistent across apps, hardware control would be an improvement
Battery life - OK - I buried it the first day, but "normal" use will give you about 2 days
Carousel - touch screen issue again - if you want to launch an item from there - I had problems with figuring out the rotation

Stuff I like...
It is a tablet!
Netflix works great
Nice Revision3 app
Pulse is cool - (Flipboard is cooler though)
Accuweather app is good
Music and video streaming from the cloud works well
The 8 gig limitation - not a limitation to me

So........
I don't like my Fire! I have an iPhone, iPod Touch and PC as well. I found myself overlapping on emails, browsing and in general doing work. Where I am at - I am ready to sell the Fire as it moved to the bottom of the pole to get my work done. I plan to aggregate more dollars for an iPad2/3 to eliminate the PC. Maybe it is because I just finished the Steve Jobs book and learned about his drive to make great products - in my opinion, he would not have released a product with flaws.
However, I am going to stick with my Amazon and Kindle for reading - it really works for me.
Sorry Jeff! And good luck on the next Blue Origin test - I am rooting for you! The future of commercial space transportation lies with visionaries like you, Elon Musk and Richard Branson.

title: Don't buy this external hard drive
text:
I was concerned about buying another LaCie Hard Drive when I saw some of the reviews here on Amazon. Shocked, since I've had nothing but a great experience with them, but things do change and the company was sold so I thought maybe that was why and that I should try another brand.

I went online and went through reviews of various brands and ended up with the WD 5TB My Passport for Mac Portable External Hard Drive HDD.

So what was my experience with this device?

In short, it was a nightmare from the moment I finished activating the software to use it with my MacBook Pro. It rejected many files as "not being able to read" them (which stopped the copy process and took upwards of 10-30 minutes to allow me to begin again), it took 2-3 minutes to copy a simple folder with less than 2GB AND continually froze my computer.

Then, when I reached the end of my patience with the device and stopped the copying and attempted to erase my files on the drive, it took over an hour to do so (it might have been close to two hours). Yikes! How would I be able to use this as a drive for Time Machine??!!!

So my advice? Don't buy this WD 5TB My Passport for Mac Portable External Hard Drive HDD!

Instead, buy a LaCie.

P.S. FYI I went to Apple's website to see what they sell, because let's face it…they wouldn't recommend a product they didn't trust…and guess what? LaCie is pretty much all they sell. So I guess LaCie is still a great product and that's what I'm about to buy here on Amazon.

title: The OTA is very good, but not the package.
text:
As a starter telescope with the supplied tripod, diagonal & eyepieces this scope deserves a 2 to 3 star rating. You would be better off to spend $60 more for the blue colored infinity model (209004) that comes with a much better tripod & eyepieces.

The optical telescope assembly (OTA) is the same for both models. It is very good and that the reason I bought this package. I felt for $99 the telescope alone was worth it to me. I already have a tripod, diagonal and many excellent eyepieces.

I got very respectable views of Saturn and the Andromeda galaxy the first time I use the OTA and this was in very light polluted sky's. This telescope has a very short focal length of only 400mm, so it produces a wide field of view (FOV). That is why I bought it, so i could look at star formations like the Pleiades (seven sisters). There are better starter scopes for high magnification, but many astronomical curiosities require a wide field at low magnification to see the entire object. I just like scanning around the sky with the 4.0 degree FOV this OTA offers.

title: QGOO AX1800 - The Fastest Wifi Adapter I've Tried...!
text:
5 or 6 years ago, looking for the "fastest" 802.11AC USB 3.0 WiFi 5 adapter out of the ones that kept showing up on the "Best" lists, I tested most of them on my personal machine, and found the one that was the "fastest" out of all of them. Having gone through that whole exercise, I was satisfied that I had the best WiFi connection that could be had for my desktop computer upstairs after that. The internet speed I was paying for at the time was 150 Mbps.

But recently I upgraded my service to 900 Mbps because of an offer that made it less expensive than the slower speed I'd previously had, and was too good to pass up.

But after the upgrade, I found my previously "fast" WiFi adapter wasn't able to get beyond 250 Mbps downloads when I ran speed tests (from 3 different speedtest websites). So, that was a bit of a surprise and disappointment... and with the newer 802.11AX WiFi 6 standards, with it's faster transfer rates now being available, I thought it might be worth it to try some of the newer USB 3.0 WiFi 6 adapters (even though I'm still running Windows 7 64-bit, and my computer can't recognize the AX mode, with AC still being the fastest mode it can recognize).

After spending a bit of time doing a bit of research, reading a few "Best WiFi 6 AX Adapter" articles, reading details for the individual adapters, etc. I found most of the available AX adapters don't have any drivers for Windows 7; they only work on Windows 10. But I did find 4 that said they would work with Windows 7.

So, after narrowing the list down, I ordered the one that looked the most aggressive, and the most promising of the fastest speeds, being a desktop model sporting 4 antennas and has a 3' cable to allow it to be moved around the desktop to achieve best reception.

During testing, I found that adapter would consistently ratchet up to about 200 Mbps, then drop down to around 10 Mbps and repeat this over and over again. It was a new unit, and while I suspected I'd gotten one that was faulty somehow, I chalked it up to it just didn't work properly in my system, opened a return request, and ordered another from my list of possibilities.

The next one I tested reached speeds of around 350 Mbps, and when it did drop speeds would go down to the 250 Mbps area and climb back up. Not as bad as the previous one, as it didn't drop by as far when it did drop down in speed, but as I was paying for 900 Mbps speeds, I wasn't very satisfied with this either, although it was 100 Mbps better than what I had been getting with my original adapter. So, I considered it a "possibility" as an upgrade, and I ordered another on my list to compare it to, which would hopefully be faster.

Well, the next one reached speeds of 450 Mbps, and I was thinking that might be the fastest I'd actually be able to get in my system from the real world testing I'd done, despite it's advertised speeds of 1300 Mbps, and my computer only being about 9 feet away from my wireless router on the floor directly below me.

But after a couple of days, the thought just kept nagging at me to just give "one more" adapter, the QGOO AX1800, a try.

Honestly, I wasn't too thrilled with the cosmetics of it, the two antennas, or the fact that it didn't come with a cradle and wasn't sure it would even fit into the one available USB 3.0 slot on the back of my machine, as thick as the body of it was on one side of the connector, without losing use of the slot next to it... but I ordered it up anyway since, ultimately, speed is what I was after, and if it did end up giving me the fastest data transfer rates, I could figure out the other things later.

On the very first tests, I was pleasantly surprised to find the QGOO AX1800 easily hitting 520 Mbps, and with additional testing finding it crossing over to near-700Mbps speeds, making it clearly the fastest of all of the WiFi 6 USB adapters I'd tested. I was surprised... in the most pleasant of ways, of course...

I still had a couple of the other adapters I'd tested that I hadn't sent back yet sitting on my desktop, as well as the original, previously "fastest" AC adapter I'd been using for the past few years, so, just to be sure nothing had changed in my system, and to confirm the results, I swapped them out one by one, and tested and compared them all once again, and sure enough, they all tested the same as they had previously, while the QGOO AX1800 just ran away from every one of them with the kind of speed they had all lied about achieving...

...and while I was a bit disappointed to find that no AX adapter showed up as having "AX Mode" on my Windows 7 machine at all (does appear on my Win10 machine though), these speeds were still achieved by the QGOO AX1800 using the a/g/n/ac setting in the "Configure" section of the Properties screen (it's set to "auto" by default, which I just didn't trust, while testing anyway).

After all of the speed testing that I'd done over the past couple of weeks, I've kinda gotten into the habit of running speed tests before I do anything else, just to judge how the WiFi on my system is performing on that day, and although I'm paying for 900Mbps download speeds, my ISP is actually providing more than that, around 1020Mbps to ensure I'm getting what I'm paying for. So, while it's satisfying to see this card hitting over 520Mbps consistently, when it hits 680Mbps, it brings a smile to my face, and when it actually hits 800Mbps even for a peak during a speed test, as it does from time to time, it gives me peace of mind confirming that indeed I have found the fastest USB 3.0 WiFi 6 adapter out there.

It works great on Windows 7, and although they provided both a flashdrive and a mini-CD with the required drivers for it in the box it came in, the flash drive couldn't be detected on my machine (didn't even show up in Disk Manager), but the driver installed just fine from the mini-CD. The adapter wasn't recognized at all by Win7 initially, and required manual driver installation, so it's not "plug and play" on Windows 7 and requires the drivers to be manually installed to be recognized and to work.

It uses the RealTek 8322 driver, and the one I've got installed (after looking for a more updated one) is "Realtek 8832AU Wireless LAN WiFi 6 USB NIC 6/1/2021 5001.0.13.103" and it's giving me these speeds that I've noted, though I believe I was actually getting the same speeds with the one provided on the mini-CD to be honest, with this one simply having the Win10 drivers added to it, according to the documentation I found on it.

I also solved the problem of the disproportionate thickness on the one side of the body that would have caused me to lose the use of the USB port next to it (which is occupied and needed) by temporarily using one of the USB 3.0 cradles that came with one of the other USB 3.0 WiFi adapters I'd been testing, and as that one has to be sent back when I return that adapter, I ordered a separate cradle for it which is now on the way.

You can find these USB 3.0 cradles if you search for "USB 3.0 WiFi Adapter Extension Cable with Pedestal", and if the lightness of the cradle/pedestal/dock is of any kind of concern, just attach some large washers (easily obtainable at Home Depot, Lowes, or any other hardware store) or some quarters to their underside with tape, caulking, or glue (if you don't care if they're removable or not).

So, sorry for the length of the review here, but I think the background is important to justify why I give this QGOO AX1800 USB 3.0 WiFi 6 Adapter a 5-Star rating, and my highest recommendation... I don't believe you'll find a faster USB WiFi adapter out there for Windows 7, and I have no doubt that it will give those USB AX adapters that only work in Windows 10 & 11 a good battle for first place, as well...

If you're feeling "the need for speed", as I was, give the QGOO AX1800 a try, and I have no doubt you'll be just as impressed as I was...

All the Best...! ;-)

UPDATE:
I picked up a 2nd one of these for another computer I have upstairs with Win10 64-bit installed. With that machine the solution I used to get around having it sticking out of one of the ports was to use a "Monoprice USB & Lightning Cable - 3 Feet - Black | USB 3.0 A Male to A Female Premium Extension Cable" ($4.99), which allows me to lay it on top of the computer. I've been using it that way for a couple of months now, which has been fine, though I recently found a Netgear A7000 USB 3.0 cradle I really like as it has a bit of weight to it, and ordered it up.

Also, I've found on occasion, my transfer rates have actually peaked at over 1000 Mbps in off hours (like 2-4am) on both machines.

One last thing I'll mention in hopes it may help someone who finds their initial speeds lagging at some point - I did have a couple of days recently where my speeds dropped on the Win7 machine and wouldn't get over 220 Mbps for some reason. I've gotten used to the faster speeds by now, so it was a bit concerning, and none of the articles I read had any solutions, really. So, after a couple of days I tried just uninstalling the driver (using IOBit Uninstaller) and then reinstalling it manually again, and BAM...!! the speed was right back as if it had always been there.

I have found when running speed tests, on occasion when the speed is down a bit, like 450 Mbps or so, simply going into the adapter properties and disabling the adapter, and then re enabling it again purges and refreshes the cache and brings the speed back as well, with a subsequent test being back up in the 600 - 800 Mbps range.

At this point, I consider 520 Mbps to be "normal" and on the "low" side of the speeds this adapter usually provides. If it hits 520 Mbps when I run a speed test, I feel that's fine and everything's working okay. But if it comes back lower than around 480 Mbps or so, I'll refresh the cache by disabling/re-enabling the adapter, and then run a test again, and I find the speed always comes back again... well, until recently... but uninstalling and reinstalling the driver fixed that just fine.

title: An awesome watch - but Alexa built in not entirely true.
text:
I'm very happy with this watch. As a smart device it certainly meets most of my needs. The display is intuitive, crisp, and responsive. The battery life is insane. I've been using it constantly for a week and still have 35% of the original charge remaining. Synching with the Zeppe app is seamless and as an activity tracker, watch, and notification center on your wrist it's well worth the money.
But....the main selling point for this device over other similar products was the "Alexa Built in" feature. Our home is fully automated with an Alexa device in almost every room. Having "her" on my wrist when out of the house was exactly what I was looking for. When we think of Alexa we think of a device that is waiting patiently for the wake word "Alexa" and she's instantly there to respond. That is not the case with this watch. You either have to swipe through the apps to open the Alexa app, or long press the side button on the watch to activate Alexa. That to me is not Alexa built in. That to me is an app that is going to connect to the Alexa on my phone do what I ask and replay the response. I was expecting an experience more akin to Siri on the apple watch where you can raise your arm and say "Alexa..." not fumble on the screen, or press a button to wake the watch, then hold the same button to wake Alexa up.
If a good Alexa experience is your prime focus then there may be better options for you than this device. I'm hoping an update will address this. The watch does have an "offline" assistant built in that allows you to open the watches many apps with voice commands (so the watch is listening!!!), but it only recognizes the built in apps like "compass", "flashlight", "heart monitor" etc. strange it doesn't recognize the allegedly "built in" Alexa app as one you can open with voice as that would at least allow: "Open Alexa" and then you ask your question.
Summary - smart watch - it's amazing. Portable Alexa - disappointing.

It will be used for heavy software compiling and running Excel macros.

Update 8/4/2017
All is still working very good. The laptop is very quick. I did change out drive D: a 1TB HDD to a 500GB Crucial SSD (Amazon purchase)
It was not difficult. Used the Acronis True Image that came with the SSD. The Acronis software was a little confusing but worked. Suggest you watch You Tube videos showing and explaining use.
The Dell recognized the cloned SSD just fine. I had to rename drive back to D:
Also used Windows to relocate the Documents folder to drive D: Worked perfectly.
It appears the SSD has increased battery life to 14hrs plus at idle.
Very happy with this laptop used as a engineering work station.

title: Good replacement ear cups and batting
text:
This kit comes shipped in a small box, and includes the ear cups, a fabric covering for inside the ear cups you can optionally replace, and instructions.

Installing the kit took less than five minutes, including removing the old ear cups. The ear cups just snap off, and the black fabric you see behind each of them (and you receive replacements for) is held in place with two small adhesive strips, again easily removed and inserted. I had the old cups off in a jiffy, and the new ones on fairly quickly.

The ear cups snap into place, thanks to a cardboard rim around their back which you don't notice once they're in place. It took a few tries, but I finally got them to stay in place. If you're feeling brave, you might want to use something like a screwdriver to press the cardboard into place when you install the new ear cups, just to save a little time & effort.

Pro:
+ Looks just like the originals, and includes the black fabric components cover inside the ear cup as well as the ear cup
+ Easy to install, and instructions are very clear

Con:
- I had a little trouble snapping the new ear cups into place, but even then took less than 5 minutes total for installation.

This kit gave my QC2 a new lease on life at a tenth the price of a new pair, which made me incredibly happy!

So with the price I decided to take the plunge and replace my infinity bookcase surrounds.  First I will say that I love the look of these speakers with the mirror black finish.  They look great mounted on my wall ( which was a piece of cake using the included mounting brackets (used wall anchors from a box store to mount them).  Install took apps 10 minutes for me  Once installed I switched on my amp and put  in a blu ray of saving private ryan and I will say that immediately I noticed a greater surround field which I believe was a direct result of the horns being placed toward the listening zone.  Also I noticed a tremendous improvement in the bass response from my surrounds as well.  I mean even my wife who could care less about surround sound even said she thought they sounded much better than the old ones and that she could really hear the surround!!  I am going to spend some time next week experimenting with crossover settings on my onkyo amp.  I currently have the surrounds at 120hz crossover  With the solid bass response of these I might try a bit lower crossover and see how it sounds.  I am awaiting the larger center speaker with the horn and I can't wait to see how it matches up. I have always been a bit disappointed with my current center which is the largest infinity but it has always sounded muddy to me and I have spent countless hours tweaking it.  If you are in the market for and upgrade to your basic bookshelf surrounds then you should check these out.

title: Excellent overall and a Great price.  NOTES for First Time Installers: a list of my mistakes
text:
I gave it a 5star for "easy to install" because the item was perfect but the process of installing and mounting a big TV is never exactly Easy.

I love this wall mount and I am very happy that I bought it.

There are two things about TV wall mounting that have always been a mystery to me:
1) The depth of the screws that should be used when attaching the bracket to the TV
and
2) The *harsh* limitations of TV placement caused by having to straddle TWO wooden studs within the wall

This wall mount is great and you should buy it.
Everything I needed was in the box, hardware-wise.
The only suggestion I have for the manufacturer would be to inform or enlighten buyers a little more, in the instructions, about screw depths. This wasn't an issue for me (this time), but I could see it being a problem for a first time installer. Specifically, my Samsung did not come with mounting screws and nowhere in the documentation could we find any info about the *length* of mounting screw we should use. Remember, I'm taking issue with Samsung, here... and this mount by Echogear did everything it should and more (and for a great price and with fun packaging (seriously)).
I wouldn't want to tighten a 2 inch bolt into a TV that is just an inch thick! {Crack!}
Echogear provides spacers for just this reason. Echogear provides a variety of bolts so that you should have everything you need. Still, I sometimes can't tell if the screw is long enough to take hold. Only Samsung could tell me that... and they didn't. So: you should probably do some dry runs with the screws right into the holes on your TV... not tightening, just going in... and figure out which spacer(s) to use before you even mess with the brackets.

The micro adjustment screws were super helpful for when the TV was slightly out of level after it was installed. They worked great to easily level up and overcome my lack of craftmanship.

The hanging strings that lock-in the mount after it is installed are a nice bit of engineering as well.

OH.... don't be a dope, like I was, and don't hold the heavy metal bracket against the wall when marking your placement. The included paper template is much easier to tape to the wall (doh!).

Not that it matter, because you'll never see the thing again, but the finish on the metal bracket was beautiful. The whole thing is nicely machined and finished. The company is in MN. Dunno where it was manufactured... The head did come off one of the four mounting bolts when we used a standard hand ratchet to screw it into the wall. We must have hit a nail. Echogear has a helpline that you could call and I'll bet they'd send a replacement if you don't have substitute bolts in your garage. The head breaking off that bolt is my only criticism of the product... but I wouldn't expect anything better if I had paid five times as much.

Another note for newbie installers: The center of your TV and the placement of ANY mount is going to be severely limited by the placement of studs in your walls (assuming you have traditional wooden studs spaced 16 or 24 inches apart in your wall). You *could* (and I once *did*) bust open the wall and add all sorts of cross-member supports so that you could place your mounting screws wherever you want, but normal people rarely do that ;) Instead, this 24 inch (approx) wide mount is going to straddle your 16 inch apart (usually) studs and you will not have the opportunity to mount it just a few inches to either side.

After getting the side-to-side placement worked out, we mounted the brackets on our new TV and discovered that the holes on the TV were 6 inches higher than center. That could've been a disaster if we were any more rushed or intoxicated than we were, but fortunately we caught the issue in time and shifted the holes six inches up the wall to avoid mounting the TV way too low.
For the five percent of people who are dumber than I am, I hope I saved you from failure.
To the 95 percent who are smarter, I hope my near misfortune offers some amusement :)

The product is excellent.
You should buy it and either install it yourself or have someone else install it for you.
I wasn't able to find any videos online of anyone shining more light on the two great mysteries of wall mount installation. I probably missed them. Heck, the manufacturer has videos that I didn't look at and maybe my questions were addressed there.

I selected this mount because it was designed to handle my 82 inch TV and because it seemed to be the lowest price in that category. I did not expect it to be of such great quality, with amusing packaging and great instructions.

title: My Honest Review
text:
My experience from receiving it today and using it for a few hours.

Build Quality:
The overall build quality is great. I do not like how to screen is placed on the frame because there are gaps along the edges. The mouse pad is AMAZING compared to any computer, even a Mac. The Windows button on the screen takes a bit of pressure and you have to touch it spot on to get it to work. The keys feels very nice in their rubber finish. I have not put the computer hardware through any test (games), but the boot is VERY fast (it is an SSD so duh). The wifi for some reason is not as fast as my other laptop, but that may be due to my cousin using the internet or my router needs to be restarted.

Usage:
The keyboard that everyone says is garbage is okay. I have only used to computer for a few hours and all of the time was getting my programs and Windows settings in, so it was half and half with my mouse (VERY NICE) and keyboard. I have only used a touch keyboard for a few minutes when the first Surface tablet was introduced and my Surface 2 has the TypeCover, so this keyboard is completely new to me. To use it you have to forget all you know about using a traditional keyboard. Hitting the keys hard is a sure way to not get your desire results. You really have to gently touch the keys and once you get used to it, you should be good to go.

The Problems:
Two things: 1) my "Fn" and "F10" buttons do not work (I tested in the keyboard driver testing program and those two keys did not register); and 2) my 1 year warranty is already used up for 1 month (8/15 is when it started) and I just got this computer today (9/17), but that is an issue to take up with the seller and/or Dell.

Overall:
I am happy with this computer. My previous computer was the Lenovo Y400, so this going to this for an everyday school computer is perfect. The keyboard takes a bit to get used to with both the key positioning (because there is very little depth and that makes it hard to find the right keys) and of course the typing, but after a few days I know I will be fine. Everything else is perfect about this computer; especially the mouse.

title: *****Updated!  In our Home & in constant use for a full year. Why I'd buy it again!
text:
I waited almost 2 weeks before this evaluation. I wanted it to be more knowledgeable and we'll thought out. At first I was mainly considering other brands such as Samsung & LG. We already owned a Samsung 1080p 60" which we purchased in 2012. It is still running fine. But, I just began to notice that Sony products are still well reverred & there are many Sony enthusiasts out there. Sony used to be ranked #1 but Samsung has had that spot for past decade. After weeks of research I decided to give Sony a place in my home. So far I can say that I absolutely love the remote and the way the app interface is designed. There is a user friendly & intuitive quality to both. But, it's the picture quality that is primarily important. I am quite pleased with the picture. It has a richness & contrast that are very true to life. I purchased a Sony 4k Bluray player & Sony sound bar to optimize the overall ease of operation and viewing & listening experience. Since what's the point in owning a 4k television & not be able to see 4k movies? Obviously the slim shape of today's televisions leaves the audio lacking so a sound bar addition is important to enhance the sound quality. I want to say that I have not changed any of the factory picture settings, they seem perfect. And, I'm usually very picky! The picture & sound offers many unique mode settings which I am looking forward to checking out in the weeks ahead. I want to add that I am a movie enthusiast and also enjoy watching TV shows but don't have any gaming set up at present. So I'll keep you posted!

*****UPDATE (after 1 year of constant use)

I am still very pleased with this purchase. It was the best value for the money and I wouldn't replace it with any different unit that was even $500. more. I've called the Sony Support people just to help set a few things up and they were easy to reach & very helpful.

I bought Sony Blu-ray player & a moderately priced sound bar that came with a good separate Bluetooth bass. It is good & bassy enough that my poor husband occasionally gets woke up at the opposite end of the house when I am watching movies late at night! It also works with some of the Sony Bluetooth speakers that make it a 5.1 set up in the future. I also bought an additional Sony Blu-ray player that is a World all regions player so I can buy any Blu-ray or DVD sets from Amazon UK for example & they play! Occasionally, titles have better features on other regions versions & prices!

When I say this TV has been used constantly I mean often up to 18 hours a day! We live out in the middle of nowhere & are retired/disabled so this is our main entertainment. And I've been a Home Theatre enthusiast since Video Tape players got invented in the 1980s. I have tried to buy the best quality in moderate-lower high end components. I have always done much research before making my purchases. Hope this all helped!

title: decent but with deficiencies
text:
I received my Zenbook UX534FTC-XH77 on 09/18/2020. Today is 09/25/2020, a week later.

Overall, it is a pretty decent laptop. Royal blue color is very nice. So far, everything works. Although I am not impressed by the screen pad 2.0 and use it only in the traditional touch pad mode, I am quite happy with this laptop.

However, by comparing to the Microsoft Surface Pro 4 that I own for almost 5 years, I found the following deficiencies of the Zenbook UX534FTC-XH77:
1) The main screen is not a touch screen. I used to be able to scroll up and down with my finger directly on the screen with my old Surface Pro 4, and now I cannot.
2) There is no num lock indicator. You can't tell whether the num lock is on or off. I went to Settings -> Ease of Access -> Keyboard and turned on the Use Toggle Keys to work around this deficiency. However, it is no replacement for a real fix. Also, scroll lock key and indicator are both missing.
3) There is only a back facing camera, but no front facing camera. I used to use my Surface Pro 4 to take pictures of objects or record events happening in front of me that is interesting. This is now not possible.
4) Touch pad is not centered to the main keyboard section. My Zenbook is 15.6" and therefore it has number pad at the right hand side of the main keyboard section. Touch pad is centered to the PC, not centered to the main keyboard section. It is so much to the right from the center of the main keyboard section that I accidentally touched the touch pad by my right palm several times and changed the cursor location while I was typing. In my opinion, totally centered to the main keyboard section may not be good either. Because it will make it hard to balance the laptop on your lap while you are typing. However, it should not be this much to the right from the center of the main keyboard section as it is now.
5) Screen resolution is only 1920x1080. My 5-year old Surface Pro 4 has 2736x1824. Consequently, all objects are big and the display can only show so many of the objects. Not only that, I can actualy tell that the objects are much less refined both in color and shape by the Zenbook than my 5-year old Surface Pro 4. I don't game. Without gaming, my old Surface Pro 4 with 2736x 1824 resolution did not give me any speed issue. This new Zenbook, with less resolution, did not show me any performance gain either. For my use, I would prefer to have a higher resolution. I can get 4K quality through the HDMI external display. But this is only practical when you are right in front of the home or office display, not when you are away working with the PC on your lap.

[09/28/2020]
Attached a picture showing how far right the touch pad is from the center of the main keyboard section.

title: Looks new to me
text:
For a "refurb" laptop that came very well packaged in a plain brown box, this laptop looks very much like new. I don't see any kind of mark on the outer shell, screen, or keyboard. I've had it for 6 days now and can say that I'm happy to have tried this refurb laptop, so 5 stars for like-new condition and savings (though didn't include an active stylus).

So regarding the laptop itself, it has everything that I wanted in a laptop... 8th gen i5-8250u cpu, 14" 1080p IPS display with touch screen, 2-in-1 feature, backlit keyboard, ssd (more on this later), and decent battery (52 Wh). The Nvidia GPU is nice with 2Gb of dedicated GDDR5 ram (but will eat some battery life). Though the 940MX is last gen, I really won't use it to play games but the GPU can help with photo/video editing.

One thing that I wanted was an SSD instead of a regular hard drive, and this Lenovo Flex 5 has a unique attraction...I haven't seen any other 2-in-1s that actually offered a PCIe NVMe drive. Most laptops can't even accommodate an NVMe drive, and yet this already comes with one installed in the M.2 slot. That's really cool.

Other notes: 8GB DDR4 ram runs at 2400Mhz; the 940MX has GDDR5 ram (not the older DDR3); there's an open 2.5 inch SSD/HDD slot and includes mounting bracket and screws; battery rated at 52.5 Wh (I've cycled the battery 4 times and system shows the battery at full health).

Only two small gripes about the design...short 6-foot charger cable, and the backlit keyboard doesn't auto timeout.

Overall a really good buy.

title: Good build quailty and functionality - a great lens support for the money.
text:
Love the flexibility of this lens holder. Yes, it seems a little bulky, and I doubt I will used the full vertical adjustment, but the bottom of the Y shaped piece also serves as a foot to keep the end of your rails off the ground.

Good build quality and I really also like the two slots cut into the top of the arms of the Y piece whic allow you to use two strips of velcro to clamp the lens body to the holder. Make sure you use two pieces of velcro, as opposed to one, with the joins positioned at top dead center, over the top of the lens, so that you can undo BOTH layers to get the lens free quickly.

Components used to built my DSLR video cage rig:

Smallrig 1750 - Professional Camera cage
Smallrig 922 - 90 degree Rod Clamp Railblock for Side Handles
Smallrig 1784 - Universal Lens Support with 15mm LWS Rod Clamp
Smallrig 1674 - Low Profile Base Plate with Rod Rail Clamp
Smallrig 870 - 2 of SmallRig 15mm Carbon Fiber Rod - 20cm 8inch Long Complanate Surface (non-thread, Pack of 2)
Smallrig 1061 - 2 of DSLR Camera Rod Handle, Leather Grip with 15mm Rod Clamp ( Black)
Smallrig 1053 - Aluminum Alloy 15mm Rods 30cm 12inch Long (M12-30cm) (Pack of 2)
Haoge 50mm QR Quick Release Clamp Adapter with 60mm Plate (Compatible with Arca-Swiss Standard)
Fotyrig Camera Top Handle Cheese Handle Grip with Cold Shoe Mount

I also made sure to get some 1/4" to 1/4 and 1/4" to 3/8" threaded screw adapters to fix things to the cage

Total came to a little over $320, but I now have a completely bespoke rig that feels completely right to me (despite being a novice), and I've had good feedback from others who have seen it regarding functionality and stability. I need to add a little more to give me a shoulder rest. but overall I'm stoked with the end result!

I specifically put a QR clamps inside the cage, under the camera, to make releasing the camera easier without having to disassemble the whole cage. I use the cold shoe to lock the top of the camera to the top plate of the cage and increase rigidity, but this does make removal a little more involved. I then attached the ARCA plate from the QR clamp underneath the cage such that I can instantly clamp the rig into a tripod if I need to do a panning shot etc.

The 8" carbon rods are used for the handles - one 16" rod, split in the middle, that sits in the handle clamp but come out without having to take one handle off the rig. Handles stow for a reduced footprint when packing away.

Please like this review if you found the information here helpful. Thanks!
